title: What happened at Aaron Donald’s second Rams workout?
summary: Aaron Donald had another workout with the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday, as he and the team continue to figure out if he can give the 2026 season an honest go. Many assume that Donald will be back with the Rams at some point, but he could decide that he wants to stay retired […]
full_text: Aaron Donald at the Harold and Carole Pump Foundation 25th Anniversary Celebrity Dinner held at The Beverly Hilton Hotel on August 15, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Tommaso Boddi/Variety via Getty Images) | Variety via Getty Images Aaron Donald had another workout with the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday, as he and the team continue to figure out if he can give the 2026 season an honest go. Many assume that Donald will be back with the Rams at some point, but he could decide that he wants to stay retired despite all these public efforts. No clear answer has been given, so any workout, any sign that AD is closer or not to making a decision, it’s being heavily looked at. So, Donald had another workout with the Rams. Is he closer to making his decision? We don’t know yet, but it still seems quite possible that he will be back with the Rams. Eventually. So, nothing new learned, yet. But it’s confirmed (again) that AD is still working on potentially getting back with the Rams, and the Rams are likely eagerly awaiting to see if this is going to really happen or not, so they can prepare as well. Then again, maybe both sides already know what the future holds, while it’s the fans and those on the outside who await the confirmation. Aaron Donald had another workout with the Rams on Sunday (ramswire) “Sean McVay shared an update on Aaron Donald after the Los Angeles Rams ‘ win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, saying the two sides weren’t at the point where they have clarity on Donald’s plans. He’s still considering coming back to the Rams but McVay didn’t want to set an “invisible deadline” for the future Hall of Famer. Well, one day later, Donald was back at the Rams’ facility working out. According to the transaction wire, Donald had his second official workout with the Rams on Sunday as he continues to weigh his options. He had his first workout with the team earlier in August, making this his second such “tryout” for the Rams.“ Aaron Donald officially works out for Rams — again, Sean McVay shares ‘behind the scenes’ (nypost) “Here’s what I would say; we have a great dialogue. It’s going to be on his timeline. When he feels good about having clarity, whether that is yes or whether that ends up being a no, we have had some tentative decisions behind the scenes,” McVay told the California Post’s Vinnie Bonsignore on Saturday night. Donald’s involvement with the Rams this summer has only increased and football fans are simply on edge as the eight-time All-Pro weighs coming out of retirement. “We have some loose things where we’ve identified, you know, dates that we’d like to be able to hit. But what I don’t want to have is any sort of unnecessary pressure on him if there’s some unforeseen circumstances,” said the Rams head coach.“ Max Klare is already emerging as a leading star in Rams preseason cast (ramblinfan) “Fans knew that veterans Tyler Higbee or Colby Parkinson wouldn’t play on Saturday. And after the team’s first unofficial depth chart named both Terrance Ferguson and Davis Allen as alternative starters, they dropped out of the preseason competition as well. Until further notice, then, Klare will be the featured tight end in the preseason. He was joined Saturday by veteran Mark Redman, who returns from a solid 2025 preseason and has a full year’s experience on the practice squad.“ LA Rams Sign Australian Punter Cut by 49ers Ahead of Melbourne Opener (heavy.com) “The Los Angeles Rams have added an Australian specialist less than a month before opening the regular season in Melbourne against the team that recently let him go. KPRC 2 NFL insider Aaron Wilson reported on Aug. 16 that the Rams signed punter Jack Bouwmeester, a 27-year-old rookie who spent training camp with the San Francisco 49ers before being waived four days earlier.“ 5 Takeaways from Rams’ 20-12 preseason Week 1 win over Chiefs: Ty Simpson looks comfortable, Max Klare a trustworthy target, Xavier Smith’s big punt return and more (therams.com) “ Smith delivers special teams highlight: A 40-yard punt return by Smith to the Kansas City 23 at the start of the fourth quarter had special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone fired up. The offense was just as excited, and capitalized with a drive that ended with Simpson’s first touchdown pass of the game.“ Xavier Smith shut down Rams roster drama in one preseason game (ramblinfan) “Los Angeles Rams receiver and return specialist Xavier Smith emerged as a surprising cut candidate during training camp as the team explored other options on special teams and he failed to secure his roster spot in the receiver room. Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels turned in noteworthy performances; Jordan Whittington is a willing blocker and is entering his third year in the rotation. Smith took a back seat. Even without a veteran addition or preseason standout, his place wasn’t guaranteed. The Rams could decide to roster only five wideouts and use an extra spot on a fifth tight end. After Saturday’s preseason game against the Chiefs, count those questions answered. Smith impressed in both roles enough so that he should be all but a lock to make the team.“ LA Rams’ Matthew Stafford Sends 5-Word Message to Red-Hot Ty Simpson (sports.yahoo) “The rookie has a legendarily accomplished passer in Matthew Stafford ahead of him in the depth chart, but the 38-year-old veteran helps the rookie prepare for that eventual starting opportunity. Before Simpson made his preseason debut against the Kansas City Chiefs on Aug. 15, reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford extended his younger teammate a simple five-word message. “Just go let it rip.” Simpson revealed Stafford’s advice before taking the field at Arrowhead Stadium.“ “Great competitive stamina!” Sean McVay’s victory speech after preseason win vs. Chiefs (therams.com) “Watch Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay’s victory speech after Saturday’s preseason win against the Kansas City Chiefs.” Stetson Bennett faces major setback after Rams first preseason game (dawnofthedog) “Leading into the Rams’ game on Saturday Bennett was the leader to be their backup. When current starter Matthew Stafford was being rested during practice Bennett was the one getting snaps with the other starters . Getting the start during Saturday’s game further showed that he was leading Simpson. Simpson however just made a big push to win the backup job over Bennett. It remains to be seen if he will actually win the backup job over Bennett, but this performance made life a lot more difficult for him. Bennett also is running out of time to show every other NFL team what he is made of. His contract with the Rams expires after this season, and the consensus among NFL experts is that the Rams won’t resign him and will use Simpson as their backup until Stafford retires. Bennett needs every chance he can get to prove he’s a good player so he can get signed to a new contract next offseason, but if he doesn’t get to play then his chances of getting signed next offseason will likely decrease.“ "I feel great about our football team as it currently stands, and I know he'll add value if he decides to come." Sean McVay remains optimistic, but realistic to an Aaron Donald return to the football field. @CBSLosAngeles | #RamsHouse | #RamsCentral pic.twitter.com/LIqc32aNKx — Sports Central LA (@SportsCentralLA) August 15, 2026 Comment of the day: The consensus seems to be that Ty Simpson had a better Saturday than Stetson Bennett, but that may not mean anything come Week 1. We’ll see. “I agree Simpson seems to have a higher ceiling than Bennett from a small sample of one game. But don’t forget, Stetson went.. “ 44 of 64 passing attempts for 512 yards, five touchdowns, and two interceptions, earning a 105.7 passer rating .” Last year in 2 games. Just sayin.“ -Anthmart27 Feedpost of the day: Checking in on former Rams’ player Tutu Atwell.

title: The candidates who’ll lead the Raiders in takeaways this season
summary: Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has plenty of work ahead of him in his initial season as play caller. And the Las Vegas Raiders’ 27-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals last Thursday in the Silver & Black’s preseason opener showcased the challenges that await Leonard. At the tail end of last month, I dove into one […]
full_text: Bills cornerback Taron Johnson during training camp. Jg 072619 Bills 18 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has plenty of work ahead of him in his initial season as play caller. And the Las Vegas Raiders’ 27-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals last Thursday in the Silver & Black’s preseason opener showcased the challenges that await Leonard. At the tail end of last month, I dove into one of the prime areas of opportunity for the Raiders defense: Improved tackling. The defeat this past Thursday showcased signs of both sound tackling and the bad habits which resulted in Las Vegas whiffing on attempts — vanilla scheme notwithstanding. Another item on Leonard’s and his assistant coaches’ plate that’s mission-critical: Takeaways. With Patrick Graham orchestrating the defense last season, Las Vegas took the ball away 16 times (eight interceptions and fumble recoveries) giving it the 23rd ranking amongst the 32 teams. Go back to when Graham was hired as defensive coordinator (2022) and the year prior, it provides a five-season scope of how the Raiders are historically doing in forcing turnovers. From 2021 to 2025, the Silver & Black rank 31st in the league with 79 takeaways in that span. That’s two more than the New York Jets who are rock bottom with 77 takeaways the last five seasons. In the three years Graham helmed the Raiders defense, the team’s highest output taking the ball away was 22 (19th overall) in 2023. Before that it was a paltry 13 total in 2022 putting Las Vegas dead last amongst the 32 teams. Then in 2024, it was another 13-takeaway year (ranked 31st) before last season’s output. Hence the tall task Leonard and Co. have improving a historically inefficient portion of the Raiders’ defense. “We’ve got to make plays when they’re available for you,” Raiders defensive backs and defensive pass game coordinator Joe Woods said. “But the biggest thing for us is always playing your technique because if you play your technique, then the turnovers will come. So, we do a lot of ball drills, so that’s definitely an area we need to improve from last year.” Dean doing the dirty work 😤 Get to know Nakobe Dean ➡️ https://t.co/39hUynNqSm pic.twitter.com/b84ZiMJLEV — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) March 18, 2026 Let’s take a look at the defenders who led the Raiders in takeaways last season before jumping into the candidates to lead the team this coming season: By The Numbers Raiders 2025 Takeaway Leaders No. 1: Kyu Blu Kelly, cornerback, 3 interceptions, 1 fumble recovery No. 2: Isaiah Pola-Mao, safety, 2 interceptions No. 3: Devin White, linebacker, 1 interception No. 4: Maxx Crosby, edge, 1 interception No. 5: Charles Snowden, edge, 1 interception I have to admit: This piece left me stumped quite a few times considering defenders on the Raiders roster are light on takeaways in their respective careers. That said, based on the projected playstyle Leonard wants out of his defense — fast, aggressive, with eyes on the ball — here’s the group that have the mental and physical makeup to generate much-needed turnovers: No. 1: Isaiah Pola-Mao, safety No. 2 : Maxx Crosby, edge No. 5: Quay Walker, linebacker No. 4: Nakobe Dean, linebacker No. 5: Taron Johnson, cornerback Surprised to see Pola-Mao atop the list? Despite facing competition from second-round pick Treydan Stukes, the 27-year-old veteran took the majority of snaps at free safety in 2025 and appears primed to man the spot again this coming season. Second on the team in interceptions last season, the 6-foot-3 and 203-pound safety heads into his fifth year in the league and is an opportunistic-type defender. Pola-Mao totaled 1,081 snaps and was a 17-game starter last season and it’ll be interesting to see how Leonard, Woods, and safeties coach Matt Robinson deploy a secondary that’s a mix of veteran starters and young and hungry talent behind them. Then there’s Crosby, the epitome of disruptive frenetic energy. With his trade to the Baltimore Ravens scuttled, the 28-year-old is back in the Silver & Black fold and has an even bigger chip on his shoulder. Showcasing do-it-all performance last season with his first-career interception, expect the edge rusher to play even more determined in 2026 as both run annihilator, quarterback hunter, and even thief in coverage. There’s one part of Corsby’s game — that if elevated — makes him even more of a terror: Forced fumbles. As in either strip sacks or when he’s making stops as a run defender. Taron Johnson: “I feel like I’m an all-around. … I feel like I can pretty much do anything on the field and Rob [Leonard] is letting me do that.” #Raiders pic.twitter.com/WSlQR9jZQ2 — Levi Edwards (@theleviedwards) August 6, 2026 Shifting to the Linebackers Grimm, the expectation is high-priced free-agent additions Walker and Dean to be driving forces in Leonard’s defense. Especially when the Raiders deploy the 3-4 looks as the duo are looked upon to stop the run, cover tight ends and running backs on pass plays, and even blitz to rush the quarterback. Both Walker and Dean have the athleticism and mentality to all that but between them, have just two interceptions (one apiece) to go along with six forced fumbles (three apiece) and three fumble recoveries (Dean has two). Walker does have nine career sacks to his name while Dean has 7.5, so those are opportunities for strip sacks. Lastly, Johnson. At 30 years old and the elder statesmen of the Raiders secondary, the 5-foot-11 and 192-pound cornerback is set to man the all-important nickel spot Leonard’s defense. A do-it-all type who can run, cover, tackle, blitz, Johnson has six career interceptions under his belt alongside eight forced fumbles, a trio of recoveries, and eight sacks. He didn’t have a pick last year and two of his six interceptions arrived in 2024. But picking a Raiders cornerback to pace the team in INTs is anyone’s bet as CB1 Eric Stokes has only one career pick (in his rookie year in back in 2021), while Darien Porter (second year), Decamerion Richardson (third year), Greedy Vance (second year), and Hezekiah Masses (rookie) have none. “I think we’re making a lot of plays on the football in terms of the PBUs. We want to pull them down,” Woods said. “Like I said, the number one stat in terms of winning games is taking away the football. We’re going to be aggressive in coverage. We may get a few penalties here and there, but you have to challenge people in order to get the ball. And I think we’re heading in that direction. We’ve just got to come down and finish plays.” Stokes and whomever earns the starting role opposite him (likely Porter), will get plenty of targets and interception opportunities, but both are light in that department, so far in their careers. “I think first and foremost, with anything you do, any walk of life, it’s your mindset. And I think for us, it’s confidence,” Woods added. “We have to have the mindset when we go out there that we can cover anybody. We’re going to be covering the best athletes on the opponent’s team, so we’ve got to have that confidence that we can get the job done.”
author: Ray Aspuria

title: Ashton Jeanty working to improve in passing game during Las Vegas Raiders’ training camp
summary: What can get lost in Ashton Jeanty’s rookie season is that he was a productive pass-catcher out of the backfield, hauling in 55 catches for 346 yards and five touchdowns last year. All three of those figures were in the top 10 among running backs during the 2025 regular season, highlighted by his receiving touchdowns, […]
full_text: Sep 28, 2025; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty (2) catches the ball during the first quarter against the Chicago Bears at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What can get lost in Ashton Jeanty’s rookie season is that he was a productive pass-catcher out of the backfield, hauling in 55 catches for 346 yards and five touchdowns last year. All three of those figures were in the top 10 among running backs during the 2025 regular season , highlighted by his receiving touchdowns, which were tied for the third-most at the position. Still, during the early stages of the Las Vegas Raiders’ training camp , Jeanty is looking to become a more dynamic weapon in the offense by improving in the passing game. “The more that [running backs] can do, the better it’s going to be,” running backs coach Omar Young said. “He goes out there every single day in special teams period and he’s working all the routes and trying to get better. I know he talked about that as being one of his goals in the offseason, to go attack that process of being a better route runner, and you’ve seen that show up here. “Like he already has some stuff and that dude has really good hands and good stickums. And so, when you talk about the patience and understanding defenses now and how to set things up, I think that’s really cool to see it come to the field and how it plays all out.” For clarity, players who don’t participate on special teams typically get extra individual drills when the rest of the team is working on the kicking game during practice. Jeanty only took two snaps on special teams last year and likely isn’t going to be used in that phase of the game since he’s expected to have a big workload in the Raiders’ offense moving forward. The Boise State product being a productive receiver in year one wasn’t too much of a surprise. While he only had 23 catches for 138 receiving yards and one touchdown during his historic 2024 College Football season, the former Bronco caught 43 passes for 569 yards and five scores the year before. However, a lot of those touches came as an extension of the running game (i.e., screens and swing passes), and it was a similar story in Las Vegas last year. According to Pro Football Focus, over 70 percent of Jeanty’s catches came behind the line of scrimmage, and he had a negative 1.6 average depth of target as a rookie. Becoming a more dynamic route-runner should be a point of emphasis and help open up the playbook for him. Another area of improvement for the 2025 No. 6 overall pick is becoming a better pass protector. PFF had him on the hook for 12 pressures (three sacks) on 85 opportunities last season, which was tied for the third-most pressures among running backs and resulted in an ugly 34.1 grade. The Raiders coaching staff, specifically Young, is chalking that up to a technique issue. “When you go back and watch this tape, it wasn’t like it was bad,” the coach explained. “He’s going to go in there, and he’s going to throw everything he’s got at it. The thing that we’ve been working on with him is his technique. And his technique has gotten way better and improved since last year, and it’s awesome to see that. I mean, he’s attacking that every single day and trying to bring that into his game so he can be an every-down back and be on the field at all times.” Off the field in Las Vegas, the team also could use a vocal leader in the running back room. Barring a free-agent signing during camp, Dylan Laube has the most years in the NFL under his belt with just three. So, despite only entering his second season, Young has tasked Jeanty with taking on the veteran role in the backfield. “That was one of my first challenges to him when I first got here,” Young replied when asked how Jeanty has grown as a leader. “…And he’s been doing a great job of that every single day of just trying to be a leader but trying to be himself with him being a leader and not trying to do things that are not him so it’s not inauthentic. He wants to be his authentic self and he’s doing a really good job of that. He’s leading us the right way and he’s got our group going in the right direction. I really like and love how he’s attacking that part of it.” Of course, Jeanty is still working on improving his vision and toting the rock as well. That is the primary responsibility of his position after all. But expanding his game, in both the offense and the locker room, has clearly been a point of emphasis so far in training camp.
author: Matt Holder

title: Jackson Powers-Johnson exits Las Vegas Raiders’ training camp practice with injury
summary: According to ESPN’s Ryan McFadden, Las Vegas Raiders’ offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson exited Monday’s training camp practice with an apparent injury. McFadden noted that Powers-Johnson went down during the team’s red zone period and “quickly popped back up” before heading to the sideline and walking into the facility with a trainer once the period concluded. […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 12: Jackson Powers-Johnson #58 of the Las Vegas Raiders stands on the field during the first half of an NFL football game against the Tennessee Titans at Allegiant Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s Ryan McFadden , Las Vegas Raiders’ offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson exited Monday’s training camp practice with an apparent injury. McFadden noted that Powers-Johnson went down during the team’s red zone period and “quickly popped back up” before heading to the sideline and walking into the facility with a trainer once the period concluded. At the time of writing, the extent of the injury is unknown. But Silver and Black Pride will provide updates as more information comes along. This major setback for Powers-Johnson for a couple of reasons. He’s competing with second-year pro Caleb Rogers for the starting right guard spot and appeared to have the upper hand in the position battle. Those two have been rotating recently, but the former has taken the majority of the first-team reps in camp so far. Also, he was listed as the starter on the Raiders’ initial depth chart . If the Oregon product does have to miss time, that gives Rogers an opportunity to win the job with about two weeks left of camp. Also, Powers-Johnson already has a rather long injury history heading into his third NFL season. He missed two games with an illness as a rookie, and he ended last season on injured reserve with an ankle injury, sitting out the final eight games of the 2025 campaign. He also missed a game with a concussion last year, and the former Duck dealt with hip, groin and concussion issues in college . Again, S&BP will provide updates when the severity of the injury is known, but this could be a significant setback for Las Vegas. Last year’s offensive line struggles were well-documented, and the team is counting on Powers-Johnson to at least compete for a starting spot in the trenches. With Spencer Burford likely starting at left guard, after Rogers, the Raiders’ options on the other side are Jordan Meredith, Atonio Mafi, rookie Trey Zuhn III or Will Putnam if Powers-Johnson has to miss time.
author: Matt Holder

title: Las Vegas Raiders training camp stars Hezekiah Masses, Malik Benson face significant tests in Houston Texans joint practices
summary: If we’re picking early winners from Las Vegas Raiders training camp, rookies Hezekiah Masses and Malik Benson have to be at the top of the list. Both were day three picks but have been the talk of camp with how much they’ve exceeded expectations, setting themselves up to compete for starting spots or at least […]
full_text: Jun 3, 2026; Henderson, NV, USA; Las Vegas Raiders cornerback Hezekiah Masses (35) runs a drill during organized team activities at Intermountain Health Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If we’re picking early winners from Las Vegas Raiders training camp, rookies Hezekiah Masses and Malik Benson have to be at the top of the list. Both were day three picks but have been the talk of camp with how much they’ve exceeded expectations, setting themselves up to compete for starting spots or at least have a role on their respective sides of the ball. However, this time of year, there’s always the question of whether the hype is real or a byproduct of who they’re going against. For example, Dont’e Thornton Jr. was drawing plenty of praise during camp a year ago but had a disappointing regular season and is widely considered on the roster bubble this summer. This comes with the territory of training camp because the Raiders are primarily facing off against the Raiders, a team that went 3-14 in 2025 and ended up with the No. 1 pick of the draft. Also, it’s no secret that Las Vegas’ receiving corps leaves something to be desired, and the team is very young at cornerback, adding fuel to the argument that Masses and Benson are benefiting from the competition they’re facing. Preseason games can help add context to the situation and provide a litmus test to sort out the real contributors from the pretenders since the Raiders get to face another team. However, those contests are still dominated by backups and players who won’t be on 53-man rosters in September. Instead, joint practices are a much better barometer, and the Silver and Black have a big one coming up against the Houston Texans. The Texans have made the playoffs every year since Demeco Ryans took over as head coach in 2023, winning the AFC South twice and finishing last season as a 12-5 Wild Card team. Heading into the 2026 campaign, Houston is expected to be a Super Bowl contender again, tied for the fifth-best odds (+1700) to win it all according to FanDuel Sportsbook . A big reason for that is that Ryans has created an elite defense that is full of All-Pros and Pro Bowlers, including cornerbacks Derek Stingley (2024 and 2025 first-team All-Pro) and Kamari Lassiter (2025 Pro Bowler). Also, nickelback Jalen Pitre is no slouch either, earning a three-year, $39 million contract extension during the 2025 offseason. To put it in perspective, Stingley (75.8, 11th) and Lassiter (72.9, 23rd) posted top 25 coverage grades from Pro Football Focus last year, with the former ranking tied for 13th in coverage snaps per reception allowed (16.1) and the latter finishing 12th with 12 forced incompletions. Pitre was equally as impressive, posting the fourth-best passer rating when targeted ( 62.4 ) in slot coverage. So, whether it’s in one-on-ones, seven-on-seven or the full team periods, Benson will get a chance to prove himself against an elite secondary. And if he’s breaking free from the likes of Stingley, Lassiter and Pitre, that’s a strong sign that the Raiders found a diamond in the rough with the sixth-round pick. Also, Benson is known for his speed, and free safety Calen Bullock is not to be forgotten in Houston’s defensive backfield. Bullock, another 2025 Pro Bowler, is an emerging deep defender in the league and surrendered just 233 yards as a primary defender in coverage last season, per PFF . Depending upon whether he gets enough reps against the Texans’ first-team defense, that makes any explosive plays the former Oregon wideout more notable. The Texans don’t have as much talent on the other side of the ball, but they do have a wide receiver who has made back-to-back Pro Bowls in Nico Collins. Collins has a streak of three consecutive 1,000-yard and six-plus-touchdown seasons, including 71 catches for 1,117 yards and six scores last season. He was one of the most efficient wide receivers in the NFL a year ago, finishing tied for ninth at the position with 2.35 yards per route run, according to PFF . A big reason for that is the 6-foot-4, 215-pound receiver with a 4.45-second 40-time has the rare combination of size and speed to win downfield, tying for the 11th-most receptions ( 10 ) on targets 20 or more yards past the line of scrimmage in 2025. The closest receiver the Raiders have to that skill set is Thornton, who has been injured and missed several practices early in training camp. So Masses, who is 6-foot-1, 179 pounds and ran a 4.46 this past February, hasn’t faced a wideout like Collins yet. That will likely change during Tuesday’s joint practice, allowing the rookie to show what he’s got against a premier talent. On the other end of the size spectrum, Texans wideout Tank Dell has been marred by injuries, having his rookie year cut short (11 games) due to a fractured fibula and missing all of last season after suffering a nasty knee injury at the end of the 2024 campaign. But he managed to record 98 catches, 1,376 and 10 touchdowns in 25 games with 18 starts during his first two years in the league. At 5-foot-8 and 165 pounds, Dell brings a different skill set than his counterpart out wide. He’s a shiftier receiver who thrives on short to intermediate routes with his route-running and ability to create separation. In other words, Masses’ coverage skills will be tested by a variety of wide receiver styles against the Texans. Ultimately, this is part of the reason coaches like to schedule joint practices at this time of the year. It gives them a true feel for the team and for which players are ready to contribute when they aren’t facing someone they know well and the level of competition increases. If Masses and Benson can rise to the occasion, that will help make the future look even brighter in Las Vegas.

title: Top 5 first-time Pro Bowl candidates on Las Vegas Raiders’ roster
summary: While the Pro Bowl has lost its luster in recent years, the recognition still matters when it comes to contract negotiations and/or incentives. With training camp underway and the 2026 season right around the corner, let’s take a look at five players on the Las Vegas Raiders’ roster who could make their first appearance in […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 15: Kolton Miller #74 of the Las Vegas Raiders lines up on the defensive line during the NFL 2025 game against the Los Angeles Chargers at Allegiant Stadium on September 15, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Pro Bowl has lost its luster in recent years, the recognition still matters when it comes to contract negotiations and/or incentives. With training camp underway and the 2026 season right around the corner, let’s take a look at five players on the Las Vegas Raiders’ roster who could make their first appearance in the All-Star game this season. Kolton Miller Surprisingly, Miller hasn’t made a Pro Bowl yet. There have been plenty of seasons where the eight-year veteran was at least a top-four offensive tackle in the AFC, especially in pass protection, as he’s been considered one of the biggest snubs on a handful of occasions. Miller might have been on his way to finally earning the bid last season, giving up just four pressures and ranking third among all NFL offensive tackles with an 86.5 grade from Pro Football Focus before getting sidelined for the rest of the campaign after just four games. If he picks up where he left off and the Raiders’ offensive line improves as a whole in 2026, that should help the soon-to-be 31-year-old finally get the recognition he deserves. Ashton Jeanty Speaking of how bad Las Vegas’ offensive line was last year, Jeanty’s rookie season is considered a disappointment because of how much the team struggled up front last year. With a healthy Miller, adding three-time Pro Bowler Tyler Linderbaum, and Klint Kubiak bringing long-time offensive line coach Rick Dennison into the building, the Silver and Black should be much better in the trenches this season. Obviously, that’s good news for the 2025 first-round pick, who nearly rushed for 1,000-yards despite constantly facing defenders in the backfield. He started to break through when the offense got him the ball in space, where the elusiveness that made the Boise State product a Heisman Trophy finalist shined through. According to PFF , Jeanty finished last year with 61 missed tackles forced, tied for fifth among running backs during the regular season. With more breathing room, he’s poised for a breakout performance. Tre Tucker While the last two seasons have been painful for the Silver and Black, Tucker has been one of the few bright spots. His production and role in the offense have consistently improved year-after-year, going from 19 catches and 331 yards as a depth piece off the bench in year one to making 17 starts and being the team’s leading receiver with 57 grabs for 696 yards last year. That trend should continue since the 2023 third-round pick enters training camp as the top wide receiver on the Raiders’ roster for the first time. Granted, he’ll have to compete with tight end Brock Bowers for targets, but Tucker has earned an expanded role in the offense with how he’s grown over the last three years. Plus, he’s entering a contract year for some extra motivation, and earlier this offseason, Kubiak mentioned how he likes what the Cincinnati product can bring to the table. Eric Stokes Stokes was one of the few pleasant surprises from last year’s 3-14 club. The former first-round pick went from being cast aside by the Green Bay Packers to becoming the top cornerback in Las Vegas, earning a three-year, $30 million contract extension this offseason. While the lack of a formidable support cast certainly helped, the former Packer led all cornerbacks with at least 146 opportunities in coverage snaps per reception allowed (19.8) last season, according to PFF . He’ll likely have to add some interceptions this year to earn a Pro Bowl bid, as the five-year veteran hasn’t had a pick since his rookie season . But if he can continue to be a shutdown corner and throw in a few turnovers to beef up the stat line, Stokes will make a compelling case for his first All-Star game. Connor Heyward Fullbacks are an endangered species in the NFL, and only one from each conference makes the Pro Bowl per season. Over the last several years, the position has been dominated by two players: the San Francisco 49ers’ Kyle Juszczyk and Patrick Ricard, formerly of the Baltimore Ravens. Juszczyk has earned the bid in each of the last 10 seasons while Ricard has gotten the nod six times over the last seven seasons. However, those two will have to compete with each other after the former Raven followed John Harbaugh to the New York Giants. That opens up the door for the handful of AFC fullbacks to make the Pro Bowl roster, including Heyward. On top of that, the free-agent signing has a similar skill set to Juszczyk with his background as a tight end and ability to impact the passing game in addition to being a lead blocker. Considering 49ers’ head coach Kyle Shanahan is one of Kubiak’s mentors, a big season could be incoming for Heyward. It also has to help that Connor has some name recognition since his father, Craig “Ironhead” Heyward, had an 11-year NFL career as a fullback/running back and was a Pro Bowler in 1995.

title: Does Quinn Ewers’ performance this year matter?
summary: The Miami Dolphins lost to the Washington Commanders on Friday in the opening round of the preseason for 2026. The results of the game itself really do no matter in the long run, but rather the play of the individual players and the position groups is the biggest take away from the night. There was […]
full_text: Aug 14, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Miami Dolphins quarterback Quinn Ewers (14) passes the ball against the Washington Commanders during the first half at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Miami Dolphins lost to the Washington Commanders on Friday in the opening round of the preseason for 2026. The results of the game itself really do no matter in the long run, but rather the play of the individual players and the position groups is the biggest take away from the night. There was some good for the Dolphins, particularly their opening drive when the offense moved down the field and scored a touchdown behind efficient passing, a ground attack that established itself early, and an offensive line that was highly effective, Things fell apart for Miami when the second-string rotated into the contest. Backup quarterback Quinn Ewers finished the game one-for-eight passing for 27 yards. He threw one interception and finished the game with a 1.6 passer rating. He did sustain a groin injury that he played through , but the dismal performance from a player who started three games down the stretch last year for Miami has a lot of analysts and fans talking. Does Miami need to move on from Ewers? Should they be looking for a veteran to backup starting quarterback Malik Willis? The more important question, however, may be: Does Quinn Ewers’ performance this year matter? The Dolphins are in the first year of what they are hoping will be a quick rebuild under new head coach Jeff Hafley with Willis at quarterback. Miami has loaded their roster with rookies, bringing them to the youngest team in the league, with a few veterans sprinkled into the roster on one-year contracts. Miami’s 2026 season, while they will be looking to win every game they play, is about the long-term growth of the team, looking to create a franchise that can sustainably compete every year over a team that sells out for winning this season. Which brings us back to the question. If the Dolphins have to rely on Ewers for any stretch of the season, does his play really matter? The Dolphins are looking toward Willis as their potential franchise quarterback. If he cannot live up to those expectations, leading to Ewers having to replace him during the season, then Miami has their answer and will be looking to select a quarterback early in the 2027 NFL Draft. If Willis is injured and misses a significant amount of playing time, then the Dolphins are likely looking to select a quarterback early in the 2027 NFL Draft. If Willis plays well and the Dolphins feel they have their quarterback of the future, then Ewers likely saw little to no playing time this year. It all comes down to a fairly simple idea: Ewers’ play this year does not matter. If he is in the game, Miami is probably looking to select a franchise quarterback in the Draft – and losses actually help that cause. Ewers struggling could play into Miami’s longterm vision of the franchise. Is the addition of someone like Jimmy Garoppolo going to make a massive difference for the Dolphins? This team is built to evaluate Willis. That is what matters in 2026. Finding a veteran quarterback who can stabilize the team for one year may feel better during the season, but it does not help the long-term growth and development of the Dolphins into a consistent winner. Miami is not looking for mediocrity this year. If they can spark a run deep into the playoffs, they have their answer in Willis. If everything falls apart, they have their answer in Willis. They need to know what they have in the younger players, not try to hold on to a middle-of-the-pack standing. Whether the team is good or bad – the Dolphins have to get the answers they need for 2027. If Ewers is needed and dominates, Miami has their answer. If Ewers is needed and everything falls apart, Miami has their answer. If Ewers never sees the field and Willis dominates or falls apart, Miami has their answer. Ultimately, Ewers’ performance this year does not matter for Miami.

title: Patriots to sign veteran free agent in light of offensive line injuries
summary: Injuries along their interior offensive line have prompted the New England Patriots to bring in some veteran help. Greg Van Roten has agreed to terms with the Patriots, as first reported by Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston. The 36-year-old, who is a veteran of 12 NFL seasons and 105 career starts, was in town […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 28: Greg Van Roten #74 of the New York Giants lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 28, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Injuries along their interior offensive line have prompted the New England Patriots to bring in some veteran help. Greg Van Roten has agreed to terms with the Patriots, as first reported by Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston. The 36-year-old, who is a veteran of 12 NFL seasons and 105 career starts, was in town for a free agency workout earlier this month. Van Roten arrives in New England off a two-year stint with the New York Giants. Lining up at both right guard and center, the 6-foot-4, 295-pound blocker started a combined 34 games for the team over that span and amassed a total of 2,275 offensive snaps. Overall, Foxborough will be the ninth stop in a pro career that originally began in 2012. An undrafted free agent out of Penn, he started out with the Green Bay Packers and later also spent time with the Seattle Seahawks, Jacksonville Jaguars, Carolina Panthers, New York Jets, Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders. A two-year stint in the CFL is also part of his résumé. Van Roten is now signing with the Patriots in the aftermath of two significant injuries along their backup interior offensive line. Ben Brown, the nominal No. 4 behind the starting trio of Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson and Mike Onwenu, suffered an injury in the preseason opener against Indianapolis that is expected to sideline him for multiple weeks. In addition, Andrew Rupcich, who appeared to be the next man up on the depth chart, was placed on injured reserve (even though his reported MCL sprain is not considered season-ending ). The Patriots use Jacob Rizy and Mehki Butler to replace the pair against the Colts. In addition, they currently also have James Hudson, JonDarius Morgan and recently-signed Darrian Dalcourt and Joe Michalski under contract at the center and guard positions. New England will host the Philadelphia Eagles for two joint practices later this week before a preseason meeting on Saturday, Aug. 22, at 7 p.m. ET.

title: 5 performances of note from the Patriots’ 17th training camp practice
summary: Coming off a walkthrough on Monday, the New England Patriots increased the intensity and competition again on Tuesday. The full-padded session lasted about 90 minutes and featured plenty of full-team work. To recap the 17th practice of the summer, please head over to our Patriots training camp notebook. In the meantime, here is who caught […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - August 15: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye at practice on August 15, 2026. (Photo by Barry Chin/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images Coming off a walkthrough on Monday, the New England Patriots increased the intensity and competition again on Tuesday. The full-padded session lasted about 90 minutes and featured plenty of full-team work. To recap the 17th practice of the summer, please head over to our Patriots training camp notebook . In the meantime, here is who caught our eyes. Standout of the day QB Drake Maye: It’s hard to look past the Patriots’ starting quarterback for player of the day honors today. Simply speaking, the third-year passer was splendid. Maye completed 15 of his 17 pass attempts during 11-on-11 team drills, with his connection with wide receivers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs in particular looking promising. . @DrakeMaye2 goes DEEP to A.J. 💣 pic.twitter.com/Ja12nfgMKR — New England Patriots (@Patriots) August 17, 2026 The MVP runner-up was at his best to close out the session, though, taking his unit down the field for a scoring drive that started at his own 20-yard line with 1:15 on the clock. He spread the ball around well, connecting Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Kayshon Boutte and Rhamondre Stevenson to move into field goal range. Maye was accurate, made good decisions with the ball, looked calm under pressure, and very much was the player the team is hoping to get on a weekly basis this season. Other performances of note RB3: The competition for the Patriots’ third running back spot keeps evolving, with recently-signed Hassan Haskins and JaMycal Hasty the next men up behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson on Monday. It could have just been a case of “let’s see what we have there” but it was still a noteworthy development within the context of the position battle. The same is true for rookie Jam Miller repped exclusively working with the third team. WR A.J. Brown and WR Romeo Doubs: As noted above, the connection between Drake Maye and his newest weapons continues to grow by the day. On Monday, it looked like they had been playing together for years. Maye and Brown hooked up on a 70-ish-yard touchdown that was perfectly executed by both, whereas Doubs hauled in a team-leading four receptions during 11s. LB Namdi Obiazor: A week ago, Chad Muma and Khalil Jacobs looked like the frontrunners to earn the depth spots at linebacker. However, the picture was a different one Monday. With Muma absent and Jacobs used as a second-stringer, fifth-round rookie Namdi Obiazor joined the starter-level group. He didn’t stand out in any meaningful way, but he looks the part from a size and athleticism perspective. The Patriots will be back on Tuesday for what is expected to be another walkthrough. The session will be closed to the general public, but Pats Pulpit will be there to have you covered.

title: Patriots announce date for Rob Gronkowski Hall of Fame induction
summary: One of the best players in NFL history will take his rightful spot in the New England Patriots’ Hall of Fame later this year. Rob Gronkowski, the most productive tight end to ever wear the franchise’s uniform, will be inducted in a public ceremony on November 7. The event will take place at the Patriot […]
full_text: FOXBORO, MA. - SEPTEMBER 9: New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski] celebrates his touchdown during the first quarter of the game against the Houston Texans at Gillette Stadium on September 9, 2018 in Foxboro, Massachusetts. (Staff Photo By Nancy Lane/Digital First Media Group/Boston Herald via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images One of the best players in NFL history will take his rightful spot in the New England Patriots’ Hall of Fame later this year. Rob Gronkowski, the most productive tight end to ever wear the franchise’s uniform, will be inducted in a public ceremony on November 7. The event will take place at the Patriot Place Plaza. No time has been announced yet. @RobGronkowski 's Patriots Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony will take place Saturday, November 7! pic.twitter.com/Kks5jcTKEz — The Hall presented by RTX (@TheHall) August 17, 2026 Gronkowski will receive the famous red jacket in his first year of eligibility, after he beat guard Logan Mankins and kicker Adam Vinatieri in a fan vote in April . The 37-year-old will become the 38th inductee since The Hall was established in 1991, and the second tight end after Ben Coates in 2008 to receive the honor. A second-round draft pick by the Patriots in 2010, Gronkowski spent the first nine seasons of his career with the organization. The Arizona product saw action in 115 regular season games and recorded 521 receptions for 7,861 yards and 79 touchdowns. He added 81 catches for 1,163 yards and 12 scores in 16 playoff contests. One of the most productive and decorated players in franchise history, Gronkowski won three of his four total Super Bowls during his time in New England — he later won another ring as a Buccaneer in 2020 — and was voted to five Pro Bowls and named All-Pro on four occasions. He also is a member of the Patriots’ All-Dynasty Team and 2010s All-Decade Team, and the NFL’s 100th Anniversary Team. “It’s just such a prestigious honor to be inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame, especially as a first ballot,” Gronkowski said in a media call back in April. “And to do it after so many others have led the way — Tom two years ago, Julian last year, you got the Tedy Bruschis the Willie McGinests — just so many guys that are just so great. And to be in the same category as them, it is just an absolute honor. There’s no doubt about that.” The Patriots will host the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium on the weekend of Gronkowski’s induction.

title: Cory Durden’s voice, game continue to grow in New England
summary: Cory Durden isn’t afraid to be heard on the football field. So much so that there are times his own head coach needs to tell him to quiet down. “I’ve got to try to shut Cory Durden up,” Mike Vrabel said. “I’m like, ‘OK, Cory, you made your point.’ ” Those interactions were not taking […]
full_text: Aug 11, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots defensive tackle Cory Durden (94) walks to practice during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cory Durden isn’t afraid to be heard on the football field. So much so that there are times his own head coach needs to tell him to quiet down. “I’ve got to try to shut Cory Durden up,” Mike Vrabel said. “I’m like, ‘OK, Cory, you made your point.’ ” Those interactions were not taking place at this time last year. That’s because Durden was a member of the New York Giants before being waived during final roster cuts. The Patriots signed him to the practice squad and quickly promoted him to the active roster, where he went on to play in every game for the team last season. “He played hard, has great energy, it means a lot to him, it’s important to him,” Vrabel said. “He’s easy to coach. You can coach him hard, and he usually tries to make the corrections and comes back, and I think he has continued to improve. He’s played well in the run game, flashed a little bit of first and second down pass rush, being able to get into the pocket.” Under Vrabel in New England, Durden’s game became more that just talking trash. The defensive lineman carved out a role, playing a career-high 383 defensive snaps while posting bests in pressures (30) and run stops (18). Something Durden was not able to do, however, was record his first career sack. That’s a goal he easily plans on changing this season. “I feel like I’m a good pass rusher. I want to go get 5.0 sacks this year,” Durden said. In order to do that, Durden worked with defensive tackles like Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark this offseason out in Las Vegas, picking the veterans’ brains on how they manipulate offensive lineman and more. Durden and the rest of the Patriots’ defensive front also plan on returning to last year’s early-season dominance against the run. The 27-year-old will be a big part of that success as he takes over the starting role held by Khyiris Tonga. Through 17 training camp practices, Durden is encouraged by his progress. “I feel like I’ve progressed the way that I need to,” Durden said. “I’m right on track where I want to be. Just trying to be prepared for Week 1 against Seattle, so I feel like I’m right on track. “In the scheme, I’m playing fast. I know this defense like the back of my hand. It’s my second year in it, so I know what everybody’s doing around me. So just being able to play fast, it’s very helpful.”

title: Patriots training camp recap: New wide receivers continue to impress
summary: Following a walkthrough on Sunday, the New England Patriots were back on the practice fields for the third straight day on Monday and ramped the intensity back up. Here’s what went down on the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Setting Attire: Full pads Duration: ca. 90 minutes (10:15 a.m.-12:15 p.m. ET) Conditions: Cloudy, temperatures in the low 70s […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 06: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots holds the football during New England Patriots training camp on August 6, 2026 at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Following a walkthrough on Sunday, the New England Patriots were back on the practice fields for the third straight day on Monday and ramped the intensity back up. Here’s what went down on the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Setting Attire: Full pads Duration: ca. 90 minutes (10:15 a.m.-12:15 p.m. ET) Conditions: Cloudy, temperatures in the low 70s The sun was not seen in Foxboro on Monday as the rain did ultimately hold off. New England did return to wearing full pads with the focus on full-field work until the final end-of-game drive. Attendance Absent: CB Christian Gonzalez, WR Kobe Prentice, OLB Xavier Holmes, LB Chad Muma, OL Ben Brown, WR Kyle Dixon Injured: OLB Jesse Luketa Returnee: DL Christian Barmore (limited) PUP/NFI: ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler New England’s usual group remain sidelined on Monday as cornerback Christian Gonzalez continues to work through the return to play phase. The Patriots did see Christian Barmore return to action and sparingly work in with the first-team defense. Along the edge, veteran Jesse Luketa left practice early with a trainer as he appeared hobbled. Takeaways A.J. and Doubs: New England’s offseason wide receiver additions continued to impress on Monday. That began with A.J. Brown posting the offensive highlight of the day, as the receiver got wide open downfield before being hit in stride by Drake Maye for a 70-plus yard touchdown. Brown then kickstarted a successful end-of-game drive by Maye as he worked across the field as Maye was forced out of the pocket to connect for an explosive along the sideline. As for Doubs, the 26-year old caught four passes from Maye in full-team work. Unlike Doubs recent success that has come in more downfield, jump ball situations, the connection today featured strong timing between the quarterback and wide receiver. Maye hit Doubs on a curl, corner, out right, and quick out as their chemistry grows. 1-on-1s: In a unique wrinkle to practice, Mike Vrabel lined the whole team up across the field and slowly picked players out to matchup 1-on-1 against each — which included some special teams situations as well. Defensive tackle Cory Durden shared he had never seen that done throughout his NFL career. As for the highlights: Kyle Williams beat Karon Prunty on the first play Efton Chism III bested Channing Canada on an out route Eli Raridon easily worked by Namdi Obiazor on a corner Jared Wilson stopped Joshua Farmer in the trenches Gabe Jacas failed to get by Caleb Lomu working around the edge After Hassan Haskins appeared to stop Khalil Jacobs, the linebacker easily won the rematch One-minute: To end practice, Drake Maye took the field with 1:15 on the clock and the ball at the 20-yard line. Maye quickly got to work, connecting with Brown on the aforementioned completion outside of the pocket and found Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, and Kayshon Boutte on short passes to move into opponent territory. A swing pass to Rhamondre Stevenson against a blitz then got the unit comfortably into field goal range, where they were able to center the ball and kill the clock with three seconds remaining. Andy Borregales then knocked through a 40-yard field goal through the skinny field goal posts. Skinny posts: Back working on the skinny field goal posts, Andy Borregales connected on 3-of-his-5 attempts — with a long of 50 yards — before the final make. Borregales’ first miss from roughly 45 yards out would have likely been successful on regular field goal posts, while his second miss from 52 yards out would have been close to the left upright. After missing three field goals in the preseason opener, Borregales is now 10-of-12 in two practices working on the skinnier field goal posts. Other notes: Efton Chism III continues to see time with the first offense. That included snaps in the final one-minute drive and connecting with Maye earlier in 7-on-7s. Chism also had two catches during the day from DeVito. Hassan Haskins was the first running back behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson to receive carries today. Haskins ultimately out touched Lan Larison while JaMycal Hasty also got some run with the second unit as Jam Miller largely worked with the third offense. Rookie Caleb Lomu worked at both left and right tackle today. He won his 1-on-1 reps against Jacas on the right side before losing to Bradyn Swinson on the left. New England’s backup offensive lines struggled on Monday, as Jeremiah Pharms, Leonard Taylor, and Eric Gregory were in the backfield at times for potential sacks. Gabe Jacas continues to work in with the first-team defense, as did linebacker Namdi Obiazor. Charles Woods continued to rep opposite of Carlton Davis. While Woods was beaten by Brown deep downfield for the receiver’s long touchdown, Woods was on scene for a pass breakup to the receiver later on. Karon Prunty recorded a PBU downfield on Kayshon Boutte. Marcellas Dial and Channing Canada also recorded breakups on the day. Top kick return pairings: Kyle Williams/Lan Larison and Efton Chism/Hassan Haskins. Also returning: Nick DeGennaro, Jam Miller, Cameron Dorner Preview The Patriots will be back on the practice field for their fourth straight day on Tuesday for a walkthrough. That comes before a pair of highly anticipated joint practices with the Philadelphia Eagles on Wednesday and Thursday.

title: Efton Chism making sure wide receiver decisions will be difficult for Patriots
summary: If Efton Chism ends up falling short of the New England Patriots’ 53-man roster, it won’t be because of a lack of trying. An understudy to teammate Mack Hollins, whose own work ethic has been well-documented through the years, Chism has impressed the Patriots preparing for his second season in the NFL. Naturally, the club […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - August 11: New England Patriots wide receiver Efton Chism III makes a catch during a joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts on August 11, 2026. (Photo by John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images If Efton Chism ends up falling short of the New England Patriots’ 53-man roster, it won’t be because of a lack of trying. An understudy to teammate Mack Hollins, whose own work ethic has been well-documented through the years, Chism has impressed the Patriots preparing for his second season in the NFL. Naturally, the club might be forced to make some difficult decisions when it comes to building the team come late August’s cutdown deadline. Wide receivers coach Todd Downing can attest to that. “It’s no secret that we have a pretty deep room,” he told reporters on Sunday. A super sub in a competitive wide receiver room, Chism is not challenging for a starting spot on offense, but nonetheless pushing hard to make the team. At the moment, he is one of seven wide receivers with realistic hopes of doing so. But while A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas can be considered roster locks, something that very well might also be true for fellow sophomore Kyle Williams , the rest of the picture is unclear. Including Williams, the current second tier at the position features the likes of Kayshon Boutte, who himself has drawn rave reviews from Downing , as well as best buds Chism and Hollins. Depending on how the club views its depth elsewhere on the roster, all seven making the cut simply might not happen. Consequently, the coaching staff will have to think long and hard about what to do with the group, Chism included. “I love where Efton’s at,” said Downing. “He put a really hard offseason in at work and it’s paid off.” That hard work is even drawing comparisons to a former Patriots captain, who during his own time with the club developed a reputation as one of its hardest workers: Jabrill Peppers. For DeMario Douglas, the comparison stems from Chism’s ability to treat practice with the same intensity as game day. “I love that guy, his work ethic,” said Douglas about the second-year wide receiver. “For me, when I came in, I saw Pep really work hard. My first year, I watched him. That was the first person I’ve seen really work hard from practice to game and really look the same. It was hard to find somebody like that, who practices just like that. To watch Chizz, he practices just like it’s a game. That’s great competition. I’ve always learned that practice has to be like the game, so the game could be easy. And I feel like my guy is pushing me to be better also.” An undrafted free agent out of Eastern Washington, the same FBS school that produced Cooper Kupp and Kendrick Bourne, Chism had a strong rookie training camp and preseason. It allowed him to be one of just two UDFAs to make the Patriots’ initial roster last year. And while his eventual impact on the team was limited — he served as a reserve and ended with four catches for 95 yards and a touchdown — he nonetheless laid a solid foundation. This offseason, the 24-year-old is building on it. “Much like Pop, he’s more and more comfortable with some of the decision he’s being asked to make,” added Downing. “It helps him play faster. And maybe he’s a little bit more comfortable with some defensive recognition, which leads him to some better decisions. I think he’s gotten stronger, and you can see his sturdiness and his route craft and play strength. That’s been really cool to watch as well.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Kayshon Boutte has left a lasting impression on Patriots’ receivers coach
summary: Kayshon Boutte’s name has been mentioned in trade rumors going back to last season, meaning he has spent a significant portion of his professional career so far in a state of relative uncertainty. And yet, the New England Patriots wide receiver has been a model citizen. In fact, Boutte’s professionalism has left a lasting impression […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - July 30: New England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte at training camp on July 30, 2026. (Photo by Barry Chin/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images Kayshon Boutte’s name has been mentioned in trade rumors going back to last season, meaning he has spent a significant portion of his professional career so far in a state of relative uncertainty. And yet, the New England Patriots wide receiver has been a model citizen. In fact, Boutte’s professionalism has left a lasting impression on his position coach. “It’s an example I will use for the rest of my coaching career, the way that he has just been a pro and shown up every day,” Todd Downing told reporters ahead of Sunday’s walkthrough at Gillette Stadium . A five-star recruit at LSU who later joined the Patriots as a sixth-round draft pick in 2023, Boutte’s career has been one of many twists and turns. Whether it was only sparingly seeing the field as a rookie, to developing into one of Drake Maye’s favorite wide receivers, to working with six offensive coordinators in six years between college and pros, to his trade rumors, the 24-year-old has had anything but a straight-forward journey so far. And yet, amid it all, he continued to find a way to develop into a starter-caliber wide receiver in the NFL. Coming off a season that saw him catch 42 passes for 719 yards and seven touchdowns, however, that starter role seems to have been going to offseason additions A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. While those moves set the stage for his role changing and him requesting a trade this offseason, Boutte has remained an active part of New England’s passing offense this summer. While nominally the fourth option on the depth chart behind Brown, Doubs and fellow fourth-year man DeMario Douglas, he has stepped up on multiple occasions to show why Maye keeps trusting him with the ball. More than that, however, he has done whatever the team asked him to do in light of his unclear outlook. “I have a great relationship with Kayshon and I value that a lot,” added Downing. “I’ll keep our conversations private, but I would say that he is an absolute joy to coach and I’m really glad he’s here.”

full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 13: Hassan Haskins #26 of the New England Patriots takes the ball from Behren Morton #15 of the New England Patriots during a preseason game between the New England Patriots and the Indianapolis Colts on August 13, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Hassan Haskins’ path to his first preseason contest with the New England Patriots wasn’t a typical one. New England signed the free-agent running back on Wednesday , just one day before its preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts . It’s an opportunity that Haskins is excited for with the chance to reunite with head coach Mike Vrabel. Before Haskins concluded his 2025 season with the Los Angeles Chargers, a Tennessee Titans team led by Vrabel drafted the Michigan product in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft. “It’s nice, man. That’s my guy, for sure,” Haskins said after Sunday’s walkthrough practice about the reunion. “We definitely have history. I’m excited to be back. I know the mindset he has, and I’m going to bring it here.” The Patriots’ move to sign the ball carrier, along with familiar face JaMychal Hasty, was a corresponding move after last year’s third running back, Terrell Jennings, was placed on season-ending injured reserve. Following the initial free-agency period in March, Haskins remained unsigned up until he arrived in New England. “I’ll take it one day at a time,” Haskins said. “The first preseason game, I was lucky to be back playing football with an organization as good as this one,” Haskins said. “And I’m just excited to be out there. I just want to have fun, and I’m glad to be back.” Haskins immediately filled in on the kickoff coverage unit and logged five offensive snaps in the second half, breaking three tackles while carrying the ball five times for 15 yards. The 26-year-old also broke loose for a 13-yard rush early in the fourth quarter, but a holding penalty negated the first down. Learning the playbook is one of the things Haskins had to quickly adjust to in the short period leading up to Thursday’s game. He credits running backs coach Tony Dews, who also coached him in Tennessee, with doing a good job explaining things to him. For Haskins’ career, the St. Louis, MO, native has totaled 229 yards and two touchdowns on 76 attempts through three seasons. He has also proven capable as a receiver out of the backfield with 119 yards on 18 receptions. Through the remainder of the preseason, Haskins will compete for a spot on New England’s final 53-man roster in 2026. Special teams contributions play a crucial role in some players securing roles, and Haskins has extensive experience doing so in the NFL and in college. “Your attributes to special teams — I just always did it in college,” Haskins said. “So, it just always was built in me, and I feel like anywhere I can get on the field, I’m going to do it and do it to the best of my ability.”

full_text: Greg Van Roten | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Another former New York Giants player has found a new home. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN is reporting that the New England Patriots have signed former Giants’ guard Greg Van Roten to a one-year deal. Van Rotne, 36, is a well-traveled journeyman guard who has played for Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks (practice squad), Toronto Argonauts (CFL), Jacksonville Jaguars (PS), Carolina Panthers, New York Jets, Buffalo Bills, and Las Vegas Raiders before signing with the Giants in 2024. The Giants initially signed Van Roten after an injury to (then right tackle) Evan Neal forced them to reshuffle their offensive line. The Giants moved Jermaine Eluemunor from the left guard position which he was originally intended to play to right tackle, moved Jon Runyan Jr. from right guard to left guard, and then inserted Van Roten at right guard. That lineup — LT Andrew Thomas, LG Jon Runyan Jr., OC John Michael Schmitz, RG Greg Van Roten, RT Jermaine Eluemunor — would ultimately be the Giants starting offensive line for the next two seasons. Van Roten proved durable despite his age and started each of the next 34 games for the Giants. And while he wasn’t an excellent guard for the Giants, he was dependable. The Giants opted to move on from Van Roten with the arrival of John Harbaugh, looking to get younger and more powerful at the position. Now Van Roten moves on to the next chapter of his career and will at least provide valuable depth at guard and center for the Patriots.

title: Roster move: RB Dante Miller waived/injured
summary: The New York Giants have shifted out of Turbo mode. The team announced on Monday afternoon that they have waived running back Dante Miller (known to fans as ‘Turbo’) with an injury designation. Miller suffered a groin injury in the Giants’ 13-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. The Giants announced that Miller was waived as […]
full_text: Dante Miller carries the ball Saturday night against the Jets. | Getty Images The New York Giants have shifted out of Turbo mode. The team announced on Monday afternoon that they have waived running back Dante Miller (known to fans as ‘Turbo’) with an injury designation. Miller suffered a groin injury in the Giants’ 13-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. The Giants announced that Miller was waived as a part of a series of roster moves that also includes officially signing quarterback Jake Haener and linebacker Chandler Martin. The Giants needed to free up one roster spot after CB Sam Webb retired Sunday, and Miller’s was the one they elected to use. The Giants originally signed Miller after a curious series of events that led to him being ruled ineligible for the 2022 college season, as well as the 2024 NFL Draft. It was ruled that he should have been a part of the 2023 NFL Draft, but hadn’t declared because he was still trying to gain eligibility to play college ball that year. Therefore, he immediately became a free agent and signed with the Giants prior to the 2024 draft. Miller quickly became a fan favorite thanks to his blazing (4.27) speed and home run potential. However, he didn’t survive final cutdowns and spent most of his rookie season on the practice squad. It was widely expected that he had forced his way onto the roster thanks to a series of explosive plays over the course of the 2025 training camp and preseason, but the Giants once again waived him during final cutdowns and he spent a second season on the practice squad. The Giants also hosted former first-round running back Najee Harris on Monday, and he could be on their radar once he’s in football shape.

summary: The New York Giants have signed quarterback Jake Haener, per a report from Mike Garafolo. full_text: Running back Najee Harris with the Pittsburgh Steelers. | Getty Images The New York Giants have signed quarterback Jake Haener , per a report from Mike Garafolo. At the same time, Adam Schefter is reporting that the Giants are hosting free agent running back Najee Harris for a visit. Haener came into the NFL as a fourth-round pick by the New Orleans Saints out of Fresno State in the 2023 NFL Draft. He did not play in the 2023 season and was only active for eight games in 2024 with one start. Giants fans may remember Haener coming onto the field in 2024 after Derek Carr was injured in the Giants’ 14-11 loss to the Saints. He largely spent the 2025 season on the Saints practice squad, and signed a reserve/future contract with the Kansas City Chiefs in 20226. He was waived by the Chiefs back in May to make room for undrafted free agent signings. Haener will take the roster spot vacated by the sudden retirement of Sam Webb on Sunday, and gives the Giants another option at quarterback after Brandon Allen’s poor performance against the Minnesota Vikings. The Giants’ interest in Harris comes in the wake of a groin/abdomen injury suffered by running back Dante Miller. Harris is a familiar face for John Harbaugh, as he was drafted by the Pittsburgh Steelers out of Alabama in the first round (24th overall) of the 2021 NFL Draft. He spent the next four years with the Steelers and ran for at least 1,000 yards in each of his first four seasons. Harris is also a familiar face for senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, who coached him last year when Harris signed with the Los Angeles Chargers in free agency. Unfortunately, that pairing was cut short when Harris tore his Achilles tendon in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos. Harris is a big, physical runner at 6-foot-1, and roughly 235 pounds, bringing some of the size and power that Harbaugh enjoyed at Baltimore with Derrick Henry. He isn’t a big-play threat, but does have solid hands as a receiver and is a reliable runner between the tackles. Harris was also very durable player prior to tearing his Achilles, starting every game as for his four years as a Steeler and carrying the ball 1,097 times in his 68 starts. As of this writing, it remains to be seen whether the Giants will sign Harris. Stay with Big Blue View while we keep an eye on the situation.

full_text: As popular and unique as our ‘ Kudos & Wet Willies ’ game review is, I recognize that the immediacy of it can sometimes lead to players being missed — postively or negatively — and that sometimes initial impressions without the benefit of a game replay can by misleading. In the past, when time has allowed, I have tried to post some thoughts once there has been an opportunity to look at the All-22. That is what I am going to do today, giving some thoughts on what I saw while reviewing the New York Giants-Minnesota Vikings preseason game. I will do this whenever I can. As I always remind readers, I am not a scout. I cannot break down Xs and Os the way Chris Pflum and Nick Falato can, and I will not try. These might be more considered more generic impressions. I’m not going to cut clips, though I may use one or two from other places. Since this was a preseason game and playing time was divided, I will break this into first and second half categories. First half Something I have said many times over the years is that as much as I like linebacker Micah McFadden, when I watch games I feel like I see plays McFadden is in position to make and can’t, or plays that need to be made that McFadden can’t quite get to. I thought I saw three of those in the first half against Minnesota, including the 18-yard run on the first play of the game. At first blush after Saturday’s game, I wanted to be critical of nose tackle Josh Tupou. After reviewing the game, I understand how he received a nearly elite 89.5 Pro Football Focus grade. Tupou was stout at the point of attack, with the exception of one play I saw where he got turned sideways. Defensive back Nic Jones didn’t help his case for a roster spot by getting driven back about 10 yards trying to block on a kickoff return by Deonte Banks. There was a weird-looking incomplete bubble screen by Jaxson Dart Saturday. I couldn’t understand why he spun all the way around to throw the ball until I saw how awful the shotgun snap from Bryan Hudson was. On the play where Dart pulled the ball down and was sacked (not the big hit) I still believe he had an opportunity to deliver the ball to Isaiah Likely. Throw that ball on time and Likely might take a hit, but it’s probably a first down instead of a sack. The best thing about Sisi Mauigoa’s game? He was barely noticeable, which is exactly what you want. John Harbaugh said after the game that Cam Skattebo was getting closer to the player he saw on film last year. Skattebo ran hard, and was his typical, aggressive self. Want to know how Kayvon Thibodeaux and Chauncey Golston are going to get on the field? There were a lot of four-man fronts on Saturday with Golston functioning as a defensive end. I hadn’t noticed it live, but the sack Darius Alexander had came on a play where the defensive tackle dropped into coverage and then came up to the line when Minnesota quarterback J.J. McCarthy started to move around. Second half Brandon Allen was as awful on tape as I thought he was live. He never saw the linebacker on his first interception, and never should have thrown the ball on the second. There is a reason why the Giants signed veteran quarterback Jake Haener . After Allen’s interception, journeyman defensive tackle Leki Fotu made back-to-back nice plays. He was largely responsible for stuffing a run up the middle. Then, Fotu sniffed out a screen pass, dropped to the receiver, and batted the ball away with his left hand. On a sack of Allen in the third quarter, left guard Daniel Faalele and left tackle J.C. Davis were both beaten. Faalele did not look good. Evan Neal looked OK. That’s what I’ve got. I didn’t get to watch much of the fourth quarter, but this gives you an idea what I did see.
