title: NY Giants coach John Harbaugh puzzled by big hit Jaxson Dart took vs. Vikings
summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart was “puzzled” about why he ended up undergoing a concussion check after taking a big hit to the midsection in Saturday’s preseason game againt the Minnesota Vikings. Head coach John Harbaugh was puzzled about how Dart got hit in the first place. “There’s no way he should have been […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart was “puzzled” about why he ended up undergoing a concussion check after taking a big hit to the midsection in Saturday’s preseason game againt the Minnesota Vikings. Head coach John Harbaugh was puzzled about how Dart got hit in the first place. “There’s no way he should have been hit there,” Harbaugh said. “I mean, it just shouldn’t have happened. That was a basic protection. Should have been protected and we expect in that situation to be protected in the future. “It’s not like he’s going to be never hit, never tackled, never sacked. But it shouldn’t have been in that one, and it shouldn’t have been that easy to get to him.” Dart was blasted by blitzing Minnesota Vikings safety Jay Ward when running back Tyrone Tracy missed his blitz pickup. How it feels getting blown out in your Week 1 fantasy matchup pic.twitter.com/CEbT6gocpk — PFF Fantasy (@PFF_Fantasy) August 15, 2026 Here are some other takeaways from Harbaugh’s Sunday day-after-game media availability. Blame the wind Why didn’t Harbaugh give Dominic Zvada a chance to try a potential game-tying 62-yard field goal with 2:29 left in Saturday’s game? Zvada made a 62-yard field goal during practice on Wednesday with the wind at his back. “We thought it was too far into the wind there a little bit,” Harbaugh said. “I’m talking to [special teams coordinator] Chris Horton about the field goal and all that. We both felt like that was just a little long to be realistic on. But we wanted to kick it. I mean, I promise you, we wanted to get him out there to try one. So, it just seemed a little too far. But maybe we would have knocked it through.” Harbaugh also felt that the Giants might get a better opportunity if the defense could force a three-and-out. “We’ve got a really good chance to get the ball back there,” Harbaugh said. “There’s over two minutes left. We’ve got three timeouts, I think we had. If we basically make a tackle, we’re getting the ball back there to go kick the same field goal. I don’t think it was the wrong thing to do at all. But you miss it, now they’re in range. They get 10 yards, and they kick the field goal to put it out of reach, you know? So, it wasn’t the wrong thing to do.” ‘He didn’t play like a rookie’ Third-round pick Malachi Fields caught a 15-yard touchdown pass from Dart on Saturday. Harbaugh was impressed by more than that. “I thought he played all around really well,” Harbaugh said. “He did some things on special teams, which was cool to see. He practices that every day really well. He blocked exceptionally well in the run game as a wide receiver in some of those insert blocks and going to get to safeties and things like that, tremendously. Thought he ran his routes really well. Even when he didn’t get the ball, the routes were run correctly. Right depths, right amount of steps, right splits. “All those things that make so much (of a) difference that, really honestly, we need to clean up across the board to present better pictures for our quarterback. He did all those things really well. He didn’t play like a rookie out there. It was really fun to see.” ‘Much to do about not much’ Some fans, and even some media members, have been up in arms about Odell Beckham Jr. getting open Saturday on a deep route where the ball wasn’t thrown to him. Harbaugh had no issue with quarterback Jameis Winston on the play. “I think that’s much to do about not much,” Harbaugh said. “It was a seam route. They were in zero. They basically flat-footed and just let it go. He ran a nice seam route. The ball went to a hot read quick and was completed, so that was fine.” Harbaugh explained further about the situation Winston was in. “If he’d been looking over there, he would have thrown it, I’m sure, hot to Odell but he wasn’t,” Harbaugh said. “He’s got two rushers coming right in his face. He didn’t have a chance to scan the field and see all the receivers. He was looking to his left. If we’re talking about the same play, the right seam. “Jameis would have to have five eyes all the way around his head to be able to see all those routes.” Sometimes, as Harbaugh indicated, when a receiver isn’t the primary target on a play the quarterback never gets the opportunity to look that way. “If you’re a receiver, you really can’t get upset about that because you understand that he wasn’t looking at me. If he’d have been looking at me with a blitz, he’d have thrown it to me,” Harbaugh said. “It’s great that he ran a good seam route and he was open. I wish he would have thrown it. Another time we had (wide receiver) Braxton (Berrios) came open in a similar way against a quarters-type coverage that the eyes were another place. There will be times definitely where the quarterback will be [looking] there and we’ll hit those when they pop open.” On to Miami The Giants travel to face the Miami Dolphins on Saturday in their second preseason game. They will hold a join practice with the Dolphins in Miami on Thursday. How will Harbaugh handle practices this week? “We’ll be on our alternate schedule, and the practice down there against the Dolphins will be a padded practice,” Harbaugh said. “That’s on Thursday. So, we’ll go shells [Monday], pads [Tuesday], shells [Wednesday], pads [Thursday], and then we’ll play the game on Saturday.”

title: NY Giants’ Malik Nabers could progress to live team drills this week
summary: Malik Nabers’ workload promises to be the major story of the upcoming week for the New York Giants. The star wide receiver, coming back from a pair of surgeries to repair a torn ACL, could participate in team drills for the first time as early as Monday afternoon. Nabers wore a red jersey on Thursday […]
full_text: Malik Nabers during training camp. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Malik Nabers ’ workload promises to be the major story of the upcoming week for the New York Giants. The star wide receiver, coming back from a pair of surgeries to repair a torn ACL, could participate in team drills for the first time as early as Monday afternoon. Nabers wore a red jersey on Thursday for the first time while participating in team periods during what head coach John Harbaugh called a “no-physicality” jog through practice. Nabers has yet to participate in 1-on-1, 7-on-7, or live 11-on-11 drills. Last week, Harbaugh hinted that Nabers could do work in team periods this week. “We’re looking towards soon ramping him up into some group periods and perhaps some team periods,” Harbaugh said. “Maybe next week, we’ll see. He’s doing great. He’s working hard. Spirits are high. And yeah, we’ll see where we’re at next week.” That, of course, is now this week. The Giants are on the road this Saturday to face the Miami Dolphins in their second preseason game. They will be in Miami on Thursday for a padded joint practice with the Dolphins. Nabers is unlikely to participate in either of those uncontrolled situations. Normal practices, where the Giants can put Nabers in the red, non-contact, jersey, and control how aggressively he is covered by defenders, are different. The Giants have not put a timeline on Nabers’ return to game action. The season-opener is Sunday, Sept. 13 against the Dallas Cowboys, and since training camp began last month in West Virginia, the speculation has always surrounded the idea of whether or not Nabers could be ready to play in that game. Nabers has looked increasingly comfortable throughout camp running, cutting, and acrobatically adjusting to imperfectly thrown passes. While in West Virginia, Harbaugh credited coordinator of rehabilitation and return to play Allie Boudreau with the work she had been doing with Nabers. “She’s working with him. And she’s been working on situations where you’re off balance, up, landing off balance, and unpredictable type situations that you’re going to get, rather than just doing normal rehab, and then going out there and all of a sudden being surprised by the awkwardness of football,” Harbaugh said. “Try to create as much as you can in a controlled setting. And I think she’s doing a great job with that, and Malik’s working really hard on it.” The next step for Nabers is to participate in some form of competitive drills. We will see if that happens on Monday, when the Giants will be in shells rather than full pads.

title: Early Winners and Losers from Training Camp
summary: The season is almost here. With just two preseason games to go training camp is in full swing. We’ve now got spring practices and a few weeks of training camp as data for the upcoming season. Obviously, winners and losers in training camp isn’t everything. We’ve all seen major training camp winners turn into duds […]
full_text: Aug 14, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (83) gains yards after catch during the first half against Tampa Bay Buccaneers at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The season is almost here. With just two preseason games to go training camp is in full swing. We’ve now got spring practices and a few weeks of training camp as data for the upcoming season. Obviously, winners and losers in training camp isn’t everything. We’ve all seen major training camp winners turn into duds and unheralded guys make a splash after camp. That said, these are still noteworthy. It gives insight not only into the players, but into the coaching staff’s thinking as we march toward the season. Remember, Aaron Glenn knows he’s on the hot seat so all he cares about is winning this season, especially early. Any decision Glenn is making should be viewed through that lens. He likely isn’t developing for the future, he’s trying to save his job first and foremost. Winners David Bailey : You have to start with the star of camp. Nobody has been hyped up more for their camp performance than the #2 overall pick. Bailey has dominated most days and his battles with last year’s first round pick Armand Membou have become must watch. That’s exciting news for the Jets considering Bailey is the key to unlocking this defense. If he can be an immediate impact pass rusher it should create a fearsome duo with Will McDonald, and the Jets could be a rare team with two double digit sack artists. Last season only the Saints, Lions, and Texans had multiple players with at least 10 sacks. The Jets had just 26 as a team. Isaiah Williams : Williams came to the Jets last season as a castoff return man. He ended up one of the best returners in the NFL, leading the league in punt return touchdowns, while slowly working his way into the offense. It was expected that Williams would return as the team’s return man and perhaps carve out a role for himself as a gadget player. However, the 25 year old has had an exceptional spring and summer. As a result, he’s jumped first round pick Omar Cooper on the depth chart and is currently enshrined as the team’s starting slot receiver. Even more impressive, it doesn’t even seem like a competition anymore. Williams played just 7 snaps in the first game, the fewest of anyone of the first team offense. A player competing for a role certainly doesn’t take the fewest snaps of anyone. Dane Belton : The former Giants safety was a more under the radar signing in free agency. Expected to be a depth safety and special teams ace, Belton has instead come in and pushed for a chance to start alongside Minkah Fitzpatrick. He’s been noted for consistently making plays all camp, and while he didn’t get run with the first team defense in the first preseason game, it’s clear he’s in a battle with Andre Cisco for the starter role, as Cisco stayed on with the second unit. Belton is known for having a knack for turnovers and excellent tackling ability, two things the Jets defense sorely missed last season. Losers Kenyon Sadiq : The tight end position is notoriously one of the most difficult to learn and transition into in the NFL. In recent years some rookie TEs have made it look easy like Brock Bowers and Tyler Warren, but for most that’s not the case. Sadiq came in as a raw prospect in need of development, and he’s missed all of spring and nearly all of training camp with an injury. As a result, Sadiq will likely start the season buried on the depth chart as he plays catch up, which is going to mute his impact early in the season. That’s not a death sentence, but it’s certainly not how the Jets hoped to start the development cycle of a first round pick. Omar Cooper Jr. : Another first round rookie, Cooper has been nearly invisible in camp according to reports. After the Jets traded up to select Cooper in the back half of the first round the expectation was that the WR from Indiana would be the team’s starting slot receiver. Instead, Cooper has lost the job to Williams, who has never had 200 receiving yards in a season. Cooper played six drives in the first preseason game, the most any first round non-QB skill position player has played since 2022. His 21 snaps led all Jets skill position players. That’s not a place you want to be. Players who get that many snaps in preseason are usually on the roster bubble fighting for a roster spot, so coaches want to get as many reps as possible to see them. That’s not to say Cooper is on the roster bubble, obviously he’s not. However, that many snaps would indicate the coaches were not happy with Cooper’s performance in camp and wanted to see something in real game action. That’s a rough place for the rookie to be. The Jets Kicking Situation : Neither Cade York nor Jason Sanders has had the best camp. They’ve both been up and down and it feels safe to say neither is safe. York got the first shot as the team’s kicker in preseason game 1 and hit both field goals, though the second one appeared to be a miss called good on the field. The Jets are clearly shaky here, and for a team that’s likely going to have trouble moving the ball the kicker is everything. It’s very possible the Jets kicker is not currently on the roster, which could spell trouble for a team that’s already worried about scoring points.

title: Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Positive signs from DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon
summary: Today marked the twelfth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES UP NEXT: The Eagles have a walkthrough closed to media access on Tuesday before they ship up to Foxborough, Massachusetts for two joint training camp practice […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JUNE 2: DeVonta Smith #6 and Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on June 2, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today marked the twelfth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed down at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES EAGLES INJURY REPORT: DID NOT PARTICIPATE: WR Makai Lemon (hamstring) While Lemon did not practice, he did get some rehab work in on a side field away from the rest of the team. Lemon’s workout included running some routes. He also took part in the “catch circuit” where almost everyone on the team practiced catching the ball after team drills ended. So, there are finally some signs that the Eagles’ 2026 first-round pick is getting closer to returning. RB Tank Bigsby (toe) Bigsby apparently got banged up in Saturday’s preseason game. WR Johnny Wilson (knee) Wilson returned to practice last week only to miss Saturday’s game and now be out again. Seems like a setback. TE Grant Calcaterra (back) Calcaterra apparently got banged up in Saturday’s preseason game. CB Jonathan Jones (shoulder) Vic Fangio previously noted that Jones is going to miss “some time” with his injury. CB Mac McWilliams (groin) McWilliams apparently got banged up in Saturday’s preseason game. CB Jakorian Bennett (knee) Bennett got banged up early during Saturday’s preseason game. OT John Ojukwu (pectoral) Ojukwu apparently got banged up in Saturday’s preseason game. RB Dameon Pierce (hamstring) Pierce had some nice moments early in camp before getting banged up and being out since then. EDGE Jose Ramirez (hamstring) Ramirez apparently got banged up in Saturday’s preseason game. CB Shaun Wade (eye/shoulder) Wade apparently got banged up in Saturday’s preseason game. LIMITED PARTICIPATION: WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) Good to see Smitty back with a helmet on at today’s practice. He did not take part in team drills but he’s ramping up with some position work. Perhaps he’ll be ready to practice against the New England Patriots this week. S Cole Wisniewski (hamstring) The rookie sixth-round pick was upgraded to limited after previously missing most of camp and spring practices. He saw some reps in team drills. EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby (ankle) The rookie seventh-round pick was upgraded to limited after previously missing most of camp. CB Tariq Castro-Fields (heel) TCF missed some practice time and the Eagles’ first preseason game but he might be able to play this weekend. WR Danny Gray (concussion) Gray took part in team drills but has still yet to officially clear the concussion protocol. FULL PARTICIPATION: Quinyon Mitchell (glute) and Cooper DeJean (groin) were notably removed from the injury report after missing some time last week. Good to see. Saquon Barkley was full go despite a brief injury scare last week . ACTIVE/PHYSICALLY UNABLE TO PERFORM EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) RESERVE/NON-FOOTBALL INJURY S Tucker Large Makai Lemon doing some stretching off to the side away from the rest of the team prior to today’s practice. pic.twitter.com/8ucBt4fvRS — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 17, 2026 JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Thought Hurts was just OK today. THE GOOD: Hurts hit Darius Cooper over the middle with good timing on the first rep of 7-on-7. Hurts also had another completion to Elijah Moore along the right sideline. Hurts threw a nice ball to Hollywood Brown, who sat down in a soft spot in the defense. Most positive play Brown was involved in in some time. THE BAD: Hurts threw over the middle to Dontayvion Wicks and had the ball knocked down by Quinyon Mitchell, who was unsurprisingly playing tight coverage. Still, a better throw might’ve been complete. Hurts missed an open Elijah Moore along the right sideline. Either the timing was off or it was an overthrow. Hurts threw a ball over the middle and down the field to Quez Watkins that was intercepted by Michael Carter II. The ball looked like it lacked proper zip. Could be bad but not necessarily the case: Hurts seems to be throwing across his body more often than he has in the past. I don’t think doing so has burned him yet; he’s actually completed a number of passes like this. But it’s generally not the best practice. BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE UPDATE: Andy Dalton flat out missed a throw in the flat. See what I did there? Tanner McKee threw a ball into the dirt well short of an open Stone Smartt. Neither backup is looking good at the moment. Jalyx Hunt notched a “sack” while going up against Jordan Mailata. Oftentimes, the quarterback will still throw the ball after a “sack” occurs since the defenders aren’t actually allowed to get close to the QBs, who are wearing red jerseys as a reminder to not contact them. But Hunt clearly won to the point where Hurts didn’t even bother to throw. Dallas Goedert had a really bad drop where he bobbled the ball up into the air with no one around him … and still didn’t make the catch. Offense was pretty lucky that wasn’t a pick. Landon Dickerson looked a little slow to get up at one point but he stayed in. There are times where it looks like he’s lumbering around. Byron Young and Moro Ojomo combined for a really nice interior rush at one point. Willie Lampkin ended up on the ground. Shorter practice today, so, shorter notes. UP NEXT: The Eagles have a walkthrough closed to media access on Tuesday before they ship up to Foxborough, Massachusetts for two joint training camp practice against A.J. Brown’s Patriots on Wednesday and Thursday! Stay tuned to Bleeding Green Nation for our observations from those sessions.

title: Eagles rookie report card: Ravens preseason game
summary: The Eagles lost their first preseason game. Not the biggest deal in the world, as it mostly matters that they go into the season healthy and confident in their roster. What Saturday’s game gave us some insight into, however, was where some young players stand. Here is how the rookies did in game one.  Makai […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 15: Cole Payton #10 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks to hand the ball off during the second half of the preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles lost their first preseason game. Not the biggest deal in the world, as it mostly matters that they go into the season healthy and confident in their roster. What Saturday’s game gave us some insight into, however, was where some young players stand. Here is how the rookies did in game one. Makai Lemon: N/A Makai Lemon missed the preseason opener as he continues to nurse a hamstring injury. The Eagles wide receiver lineup really needs to help, so, here’s hoping he can get well soon! Eli Stowers: C Eli Stowers started at tight end and played a handful of snaps in the first quarter. He lined up inline and in the slot, catching three short passes. It was a pretty unremarkable day for the talented rookie tight end. His role this year will require him to make the most out of his targets and provide some solid run blocking. Stowers failed to look dynamic catching the football and only looked fine as a blocker. It is not a huge red flag given it is his first live game NFL snaps and he is playing with a bunch of guys who will not be starting in a few weeks. Hopefully he can continue to grow and make the most of his snaps through the next two preseason games. Markel Bell: A- Word out of training camp has been good for Markel Bell, but he exceeded even those expectations with a great first showing. Bell’s major concerns coming into the league had to do with how he’d deal with NFL leverage given his height. Well the good news is he looked really comfortable against some talented pass rushers. He moved well on the edge and looked great coming downhill as a run blocker. Bell has the luxury of getting to wait in the wings this year, but the Eagles should be thrilled with where he is at this point in his development. Micah Morris: B- Micah Morris looked really solid through the night playing at guard. He was a solid run blocker and I was surprised how solid he looked as a pass protector. The Eagles need some solid depth at interior offensive line and Morris looks ready to fill in if needed. Cole Payton: B+ Cole Payton was a breath of fresh air last night. After some really uninspiring play from the other Eagles backup quarterbacks, Payton stepped in and was, at the very least, exciting. His mobility was immediately evident as he picked up some big gains on scrambles and designed runs, including a few runs where he brushed off contact to pick up a few more yards. Then the big highlight came on a play he was able to extend with his feet, but kept his eyes up and found a receiver in the back of the endzone for the Eagles’ lone touchdown of the night. The Eagles backup quarterback situation is one to monitor this preseason. There are trade rumors swirling about Tanner McKee, even if he had a rough game against Baltimore. It’s possible Payton continues to get long looks in these preseason games so he can play himself into that QB3 spot. Uar Bernard: D Uar Bernard played his first live football snaps ever last night. So given that, his grade could be curved a lot higher. But purely looking at results, Bernard mostly had negative plays against the run but had two snaps against the run and pass where he held his own and you could get a glimpse of the talent. Again, the Eagles are probably encouraged he could stay standing up on a given play, let alone actually make the offense respect him. I bet he keeps getting a bit better each week. The Rest Zion Wilson: Wilson is one of a few UDFA defenders on the Eagles. He looked overmatched in all phases last night. Kapena Gushiken: Gushiken was a pleasant surprise in his first NFL action. The former Ole Miss rebel played both safety spots and slot defender with a lot of comfort, looking especially good coming up to stop the run. Maximus Pulley: Another impressive rookie safety, Maximus Pulley looked excellent playing both safety spots. Joshua Weru: Uar Bernard isn’t the only international project the Eagles have on the roster. Joshua Weru is a former rugby player who is hoping to earn a roster spot as an edge defender for the Eagles. At 6’4”, 244 pounds and athletic, there is much to like about Weru from a talent perspective. However, he will need a lot more work as he struggled in his first NFL action. The physicality of Baltimore’s offensive linemen overwhelmed him as a run defender and pass rusher. David Blay Junior: David Blay Junior has a lot to like. He has a stout build at 6’2” and 295 pounds and plays with a nice burst. He had some nice reps as a pass rusher last night but struggled to make an impact as a run defender. The tools are there, but he needs to continue to learn to anchor against an NFL run blocker.

title: Eagles News: NFL insider says members of the team are raving about Jalen Hurts’ effort to improve
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Jay Glazer – Twitter“Spent a couple days with the Eagles on my annual Glaze Across America NFL Training Camp Tour and the biggest takeaway I walked away with… the number of people at different areas of the team are raving about how much effort Jalen […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 15: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles attempts a pass before the preseason game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Jay Glazer – Twitter “Spent a couple days with the Eagles on my annual Glaze Across America NFL Training Camp Tour and the biggest takeaway I walked away with… the number of people at different areas of the team are raving about how much effort Jalen Hurts has put in to improving in many areas on and off the field. Can’t tell you how many “I’m really proud of him” I got. Last year he was at the center of issues but they are speaking a MUCH different tune on him so far in camp. Even guys who were previously frustrated with him were absolutely praising him for the work he’s put in and the concerted effort he has made. Good for him! It’s never too late and in this league you always need to find ways to improve, evolve and improve some more. It never ends if you want to be THAT GUY! Plus, they think this offense will be much better suited to him, the offensive line, Saquon, all around.“ Eagles-Ravens snap counts: Jihaad Campbell, a starter who was not rested – BGN Jihaad Campbell was the only projected 2026 full-time starter (non-specialists, obviously) to play in this game. A little interesting. Jihaad Campbell: ‘Everybody is striving for more and more’ – PhiladelphiaEagles.com “It’s going to be amazing, man. Everybody is striving for more each and every day. I think it’s going to be amazing to go up against another team, especially joint practice in another environment,” Campbell said. “It’s my first time going against another team in their environment.” Some Perspective – Iggles Blitz There isn’t as much good to say about the offense. Andy Dalton got the start and played poorly. His erratic play made it tough to judge some of the other players. I thought Tanner McKee was better, but he was still far from good. Both guys made some curious decisions on who to throw to. The offense couldn’t get into any kind of rhythm and struggled until the end of the game. Cole Payton showed the value in having a mobile QB. His legs brought some life to the offense and put points on the scoreboard. One of the big problems last year was OL depth. Saturday gave us some encouraging signs. Willie Lampkin played well at both G and C. He feels like a lock to make the team. Now the Eagles have to decide how they want to use him. The Eagles’ backup quarterback battle that nobody is winning – NBCSP This quarterback competition didn’t have a winner Saturday night. Just two losers. Neither Andy Dalton nor Tanner McKee did anything Saturday night in Baltimore to separate themselves in their battle for the Eagles’ backup quarterback job. They were on the field for a combined eight drives that generated no points, 77 net yards, two first downs, seven punts, 31 rushing yards, 46 passing yards and no plays longer than 13 yards. Only when rookie 5th-round pick Cole Payton entered the game did the Eagles look remotely like an NFL offense. Payton – who’s not part of the competition for the No. 2 spot – ran for 45 yards and threw for 37 with a TD to generate the Eagles’ one scoring drive in the final minutes. As for Dalton and McKee, it was just a lifeless evening in what wound up as a 24-7 preseason loss to the Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore. “Yeah, execution wasn’t there in a lot of different phases,” McKee said. “Playing behind the sticks was tough just with penalties and stuff. So I would say multiple reasons (for the poor performance), but I would say the penalties and execution.” Eagles 53-man roster projection 2.0: Will Uar Bernard and Joshua Weru make the team? – The Athletic Berman (6): Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, Moro Ojomo, Byron Young, Ty Robinson, Uar Bernard. If you thought Robinson might be on the bubble, he came on this past week and punctuated the practices with a strong performance in the game. Robinson is on the team. The question comes back to Bernard. I’m still in the camp that the Eagles are not exposing him to waivers and are committed to this as a multiyear project. That doesn’t rule out a late-August injury that would allow him to spend a year learning the game and adjusting to NFL life while on injured reserve. But it would surprise me if the Eagles allow him the opportunity to develop elsewhere. That’s why he’ll remain on my 53, barring an injury. Former Cowboys OG John Niland dies at 82 – PFT Niland made 111 starts in 124 games over nine seasons with Dallas. He played one season for the Eagles before retiring after the 1975 season. Cowboys free agency rumors: Cornerback Adoree Jackson could be next after Von Miller – Blogging The Boys The Dallas Cowboys appear ready for action. About 30 minutes after news broke that veteran pass rusher Von Miller is expected to join the team, the Cowboys formally announced the news as well, it was reported by ESPN that Dallas is looking into cornerback help as well. Jeremy Fowler mentioned Adoree Jackson as the name to watch here. Commanders Free Agency: Former Washington RB added with Jeremy McNichols out – Hogs Haven The Washington Commanders had eight players in for workouts on Sunday and four of them were running backs. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that veteran RB Jeremy McNichols would be sidelined for a few weeks with a quad injury. Washington has now signed Craig Reynolds for training camp and the final two preseason games per ESPN’s John Keim. Cornerback retires after 4 days with NY Giants – Big Blue View Cornerback Sam Webb has retired from football four days after signing with the New York Giants. Webb signed with the Giants on Thursday, played 14 snaps on Saturday in the Giants’ preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings, and was placed on the NFL reserve/retired list on Sunday. The 28-year-old Webb has played in 36 NFL games over four seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders, Carolina Panthers, and Cleveland Browns. The Giants have had a rash of injuries at cornerback, with Dru Phillips, Paulson Adebo, and Greg Newsome all missing time. 6 NFL Preseason standouts from Week 1 – SB Nation Yes, we know — there are myriad reasons nobody should get over-excited about preseason performances in the NFL. The vast majority of the league run vanilla defensive schemes, trying to ensure they don’t give anything away before the real football begins, and teams have so many rotating pieces on both sides of the ball that the teams we’re seeing right now end up being nothing like their counterparts a month from now. Need more convincing? The Giants and Browns were the most dominant teams in preseason a year ago, while the Seahawks and Packers both looked like they were struggling. From a top-down view it’s critical not to get carried away with full-team performances, but we can start to see trends emerge in the preseason when it comes to individual players, particularly young guys who already appear as if they’re adjusting to the NFL and ready to surprise. title: Eagles-Ravens snap counts: Jihaad Campbell, a starter who was not rested
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason loss to the Baltimore Ravens are in. Let’s take a look. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 07: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jihaad Campbell #11 looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 7th, 2026 at the Jefferson Health Training Complex on August 7th, 2026 in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ preseason loss to the Baltimore Ravens are in. Let’s take a look. OFFENSE The Eagles took a long look at rookie Micah Morris, who played at left guard. Jake Majors took all 34 snaps at center. I was hoping the Eagles wouldn’t play Darius Cooper much because they’ve already seen enough to believe he deserves playing time and thus would like to preserve him. But they didn’t do that. He played a lot. Cooper led the Eagles in receiving with a mere 21 yards. He would’ve had more had he not dropped a would-be first down conversion. Willie Lampkin began the game with four snaps at center before shifting over to right guard. A recent development: the Eagles utilizing John Ojukwu at left guard, where he lacks experience. They were previously having him work at both tackle positions. Ojukwu took 10 snaps at left guard and 13 at left tackle in this game. I think he’s on the roster bubble. Markel Bell got the start at right tackle. Eli Stowers started the game and played the most of any tight end. His three receptions resulted in 12 yards. The rookie also saw a lot of action on special teams. Pro Football Focus graded him 29th out of 29 Eagles players on offense. Tanner McKee followed Andy Dalton, who started the game. Then Cole Payton took over in the fourth quarter. Myles Hinton played exclusively at left tackle despite often repping at guard this offseason. Drew Kendall and Fred Johnson started the game but didn’t stay in for too long. They could be the sixth and seventh offensive linemen behind the five starters. Elijah Moore and Hollywood Brown each had one touch in limited playing time. DEFENSE Mac McWilliams saw a lot of playing time. PFF charted him with an allowed four targets for four catches, 37 yards, a 105.2 passer rating, and two penalties. Not a good night for the second-year corner. Smael Mondon Jr. was active as a blitzer, generating three pressures, which was tied for a team high. Ty Robinson played a lot, which isn’t necessarily good, but he generated three pressures … including a sack. I think he’s doing enough to convince the Eagles to keep him. The Eagles took a good look at undrafted rookie linebacker Deontae Lawson on both defense and special teams. The Birds are so loaded at his position that I don’t know that he’ll make the roster. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. looked pretty good when he played. Don’t really see the need to play him much more in the preseason. The Eagles used Kapena Gushiken (or “Gush” as Vic Fangio called him, not to be confused with Gish ) in multiple roles. PFF charted him with 14 snaps in the box, nine at slot corner, and 10 at safety. Joshua Weru and Uar Bernard both saw a decent amount of playing time in the first football game of their lives! Michael Carter II got the start at safety. He seems to be still be adjusting to that new role for him. Brandon George played 14 defensive snaps for a team he only joined the day prior. He graded out highly by PFF in their special teams grading. ST is supposed to be his calling card, so, that’s good. Jihaad Campbell was the only projected 2026 full-time starter (non-specialists, obviously) to play in this game. A little interesting. Jakorian Bennett got injured early in the game and did not return. SPECIAL TEAMS Stone Smartt didn’t manage to get any offensive snaps, only played on special teams. Ditto for Hollin Pierce, who barely played at all in this game. Poor guy. DID NOT PLAY To no surprise, the Eagles rested almost all of their starters. DeVonta Smith, Makai Lemon, Cole Wisniewski, Quinyon Mitchell, Jonathan Jones, Cooper DeJean, Dameon Pierce, Tarqi Castro-Fields, Keyshawn James-Newby, Jonathan Greenard (active/PUP), Chance Campbell, and Johnny Wilson were all on the injury report prior to Saturday’s game. The starters from that group obviously won’t have played anyway. Curious to see that Wilson was out since he recently returned to practice. Maybe being extra cautious to prevent a setback there. Marcus Epps being rested seems like a really good sign for his chances of winning the so-called safety battle. Johnny Mundt being rested clearly shows he’s going to have a meaningful role as TE2.

title: Mike Tomlin set to appear on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon
summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin is making the rounds on television, following his debut as part of the Sunday Night Football broadcast on NBC. His debut received rave reviews as his passion and knowledge for the game came through the television and provided analysis that is digestible for viewers of all levels. Tomlin […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 30: Head coach Mike Tomlin of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on prior to a game against the Buffalo Bills at Acrisure Stadium on November 30, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin is making the rounds on television, following his debut as part of the Sunday Night Football broadcast on NBC. His debut received rave reviews as his passion and knowledge for the game came through the television and provided analysis that is digestible for viewers of all levels. Tomlin discussed his decision to finally get into broadcasting, as it felt like a natural progression from the rigors of coaching. “It’s probably not an overnight decision,” Tomlin told Maria Taylor of NBC. “But it’s probably not something that I could articulate or share with people. There’s a loneliness with leadership. I just thought it was a good time for me, personally. And by that, I mean just where I am in life. And I thought it was a good time for the organization, to be quite honest with you. We didn’t have a lot of success in the playoffs in recent years.” Now, Tomlin will join Jimmy Fallon on tonight’s edition of the Tonight Show. This is his first appearance on any late-night talk show. The latest portion of Tomlin’s career has a ton of promise as even people across the media landscape praised Tomlin and his ability to break down the game. Following Tomlin’s resignation, Michael Wilbon said the former Steelers’ coach could impact broadcasting to the same level of John Madden. “Mike Tomlin can reset television as a form of entertainment, football as a form of entertainment on television in a way that no one has since John Madden,” Wilbon said . “And that may be new ways we don’t know about, it may be one of the existing ways with an existing network or platform. I don’t know, I’m not a television executive. But Mike Tomlin, who you have loved to hear talk and talk to for 20 years, you know Mike Tomlin would be great at that.” As part of Sunday Night Football , Tomlin will return to Pittsburgh in Week 13 when the Steelers host the Houston Texans. title: Mike McCarthy ends speculation on Steelers’ future at St. Vincent College
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have officially wrapped up training camp, with their final practice on Monday being cancelled due to inclement weather. Much was made of several current and former Steelers discussing going to St. Vincent College for training camp over the last handful of week.s Former head coach Mike Tomlin made it clear he doesn’t […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Head coach Mike McCarthy of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have officially wrapped up training camp, with their final practice on Monday being cancelled due to inclement weather. Much was made of several current and former Steelers discussing going to St. Vincent College for training camp over the last handful of week.s Former head coach Mike Tomlin made it clear he doesn’t miss the dorms. “I don’t miss that dorm room in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, where I spent a calendar year of my life,” Tomlin said during NBC’s coverage of the Hall of Fame Game. Former Steelers edge rusher Bud Dupree ad current defensive captain Cam Heyward shared the same sentiment when discussing training camp on Heyward’s podcast, Not Just Football. “The best training camp we had was the COVID year,” Dupree said . “We stayed at our own house. I hated the dorms. I hated it.” Heyward echoed Dupree’s displeasure with the dorms. “The COVID year, we were trying so hard to win a Super Bowl so then we could tell Mr. Rooney and be like, Mr. Rooney, we won a Super Bowl, we don’t need to go back to Latrobe,” Heyward said. “It did not work out in that way. We were back in Latrobe the next year.” This raised questions to whether the Steelers would continue their tradition of holding training camp at St. Vincent College, but head coach Mike McCarthy put those questions to rest. “Not at all,” McCarthy said when asked if he’s considered not having camp in Latrobe in 2027 . “Hell, we’ll see if we can stay longer next year.” So for any fans worried that 2026 may have been the last time they could take a trip to St. Vincent to see the Steelers during the summer, fear not. summary: There’s a bit of good news and not-so-good news coming out of the Seattle Seahawks’ Monday practice. On the positive side, running backs Jadarian Price and Jacardia Wright are back in pads and practicing in team drills. The potentially bad news? Second-year wide receiver Tory Horton, who missed the back-half of last season with a […]
full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JULY 25: Tory Horton #15 of the Seattle Seahawks runs during practice at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on July 25, 2026 in Renton, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s a bit of good news and not-so-good news coming out of the Seattle Seahawks’ Monday practice. On the positive side, running backs Jadarian Price and Jacardia Wright are back in pads and practicing in team drills. The potentially bad news? Second-year wide receiver Tory Horton, who missed the back-half of last season with a crackted tibia, was not part of Monday’s session at VMAC. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald didn’t have much to offer in terms of injury specifics for Horton or anyone else. “Tory’s working through some things,” Macdonald said at Monday’s press conference. “Yeah, not a lot of updates on the injury front right now, but they had a couple guys down today.” Horton did not play in Saturday’s preseason loss versus the Dallas Cowboys, although it’s unknown whether that’s injury related or if he’s enough of a key offensive component to not be risked for a game. Dating back to his final season at Colorado State, he’s had consecutive seasons end prematurely due to leg injuries. And yet, Horton’s training camp has been encouraging up until this point. Having had offseason surgery, Horton did not participate in OTAs or mandatory minicamp, but was ready for Day 1 of training camp. This is only the second practice he’s missed since late July, so hopefully this is just being cautious instead of anything more serious than that.

full_text: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald never seemed overly concerned about rookie running back Jadarian Price’s injury , and his return to the field seems to indicate he had no reason to be. Price was a full participant in Monday’s non-contact practice for the first time since August 7, after missing five consecutive sessions and the preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys while recovering from nagging leg soreness. The 2026 first-round pick slotted into the team’s starting offense, where he’s trending toward playing in the regular season. Jadarian Price in pads today as Julian Neal. pic.twitter.com/qC3gofh4CF — Bob Condotta (@bcondotta) August 17, 2026 During his absence, Price was listed as a limited participant on the team’s August 11 walkthrough, which seemingly indicated his return was on the horizon. Backup running back Jacardia Wright (lower leg) also returned to practice following an extended absence, likely a move that prompted the releases of T.J. Harden and Justin Jones this morning, after both were signed early last week. Price and Wright’s returns bode well for their chances to play in the team’s second preseason game against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, although Macdonald hasn’t provided an indication of whether either will take the field.

title: Seahawks make 6 roster moves, place Shemar Jean-Charles on IR
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are back at practice following their 2026 preseason debut against the Dallas Cowboys, and as is standard during August, a slew of roster changes were made. Arguably the most attention-grabbing news comes at the cornerback position, and no it’s not related to Terrion Arnold (at least not yet). Shemar Jean-Charles placed on […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Shemar Jean-Charles #34 of the Seattle Seahawks runs during the first quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks are back at practice following their 2026 preseason debut against the Dallas Cowboys, and as is standard during August, a slew of roster changes were made. Arguably the most attention-grabbing news comes at the cornerback position, and no it’s not related to Terrion Arnold (at least not yet). Shemar Jean-Charles placed on injured reserve After a rough outing in which he gave up a long touchdown, a pass interference penalty, and a couple of other big catches, Jean-Charles’ season looks to be over due to an undisclosed injury. Jean-Charles dealt with injuries last year and stayed on the practice squad. Seattle could still waive Jean-Charles off IR with a settlement agreement, thus making him a free agent, otherwise the next time he’ll play is 2027. Pair of running backs waived T.J. Harden and Justin Jones have both been let go after playing in the Cowboys game. Harden’s highlight was recovering a muffed punt in the fourth quarter, but otherwise neither he nor Jones did much on offense. With Seattle’s running back room banged up, Harden and Jones were always short-term camp bodies. 3 players signed to Seahawks roster Not too long after Anthony Hankerson worked out for Seattle , the former Oregon State star running back has been added to the team. It remains to be seen whether any of Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson, or Jacardia Wright will be ready to return to practice and even play against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Meanwhile, the Seahawks also brought back linebacker Power Echols, who was signed and just as quickly waived last week . It must be emphasized that Power is his actual first name, which is awesome. Lastly, wide receiver Julian Hicks was signed. The UDFA out of Albany was most recently with the Green Bay Packers last season, but has never been on an NFL regular season roster.

title: Trouble in the trenches halts Seahawks in preseason opener
summary: Well, that sure was a preseason game, huh?  Your 2025 Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks took the field for the first time in 2026…well, the backups and backups to the backups did, at least. It started off pretty well with a clock-eating TD drive, albeit one helped along by penalties, to take a 7-0 lead […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Jalan Gaines #47 of the Seattle Seahawks gets set during the fourth quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that sure was a preseason game, huh? Your 2025 Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks took the field for the first time in 2026…well, the backups and backups to the backups did, at least. It started off pretty well with a clock-eating TD drive, albeit one helped along by penalties, to take a 7-0 lead over the Dallas Cowboys in Lumen Field. More to come on the abundance of flags later. After that first drive, it was a snoozefest to be honest. The offense couldn’t get out of their own way no matter who was playing QB, and the defense couldn’t get off the field. Add in a missed FG by Jason Myers to make it a relatively poor showing by all three phases of the game in a 17-7 defeat . There were a few positives, but largely this game can be used as teaching tape for improvement. Seattle will need a lot of that if they plan on “running it forward” this year regardless of whether the backups were playing or not. Seahawks Droppings First off, let’s talk QBs. Sam Darnold didn’t play, so the game was split between Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe, with each of them rotating after two series for the majority of the game. Lock started, and led Seattle on their only TD drive of the game, connecting with Montorie Foster Jr. He also probably should’ve thrown a pick-six on his first pass of the game if the defender had turned his head to look for the ball. There was another deep ball later to Foster that he overshot. Lock played fine, I don’t think he did anything to hurt or help himself in the opener. Depending on who you ask about Jalen Milroe, you will likely get a different answer on his performance. Overall, he was also “fine.” However, I was encouraged with his on-time passes and thought he looked much more comfortable as opposed to a year ago, particularly when under center. Milroe still has that tantalizing athleticism that caused Seattle to take a flier on him. The fact that he didn’t get much going has as much to do with the rest of the offense letting him down with drops and penalties as it does with his own performance. Yet, QBs are ultimately responsible for the function of the offense. Putting together some of the comments from the Mikes (Bennett, Robinson, and Macdonald) both before and after the game leads me to believe that there’s a little push and pull with Milroe not showcasing his running ability. Macdonald is firmly in the camp of wanting him to use that as much as possible, while it seems like Milroe is doing everything he can to prove he can be a pocket passer if needed. There needs to be a happy medium if the Milroe experiment will progress to the next phase. To put it bluntly, I thought the offensive and defensive lines were both bad. Part of Milroe’s inability to lead a scoring drive was a direct result from near-constant pressure when he dropped back to pass or being behind the sticks from a penalty. There was no push in the run game, either. Flipping over to the defensive line, there was push in the run game…just not in the right direction. Seattle’s DL were consistently getting blown off the ball a few yards, leading to easy conversions. There was also a noticeable lack of pass rush, giving the Cowboys QBs all day to find open receivers. Yes, there were backups playing all over, but that was the case with Dallas as well. For all the hype he’s been getting, I was disappointed with Rylie Mills. He should’ve been eating those Cowboy OL for lunch and wrecking shop. Except for maybe one play, that didn’t happen. One of the very few bright spots on defense was LB Tyrice Knight. Macdonald said after the game that they were undermanned in the LB room, so Knight had to play more than they wanted him to. All he did was look like the best player on the field. Knight was instinctive, playing fast and laying down the wood. By all accounts, he’s had a great camp and deserves to get regular season snaps in the LB rotation. Flags, flags, and more flags. The amount of penalties last night was unfortunately another huge facet of the preseason opener as it felt like there was a flag thrown on every other play. There were 21 combined accepted penalties for over 180 yards. It wasn’t like there were terrible calls either, they were all legit. It felt sloppy and unfocused. No wonder why Macdonald was displeased in his postgame press conference. I could harp on some other things, but I think that’s enough. One preseason game doesn’t embody the entire preseason, let alone the regular season to come. Maybe the biggest positive was that there were no serious injuries. Macdonald and crew have plenty of corrections to make, and I trust them to get the job done. Hopefully the next preseason game against the Tennessee Titans will look more like the Mike Macdonald Seahawks we’ve been used to. It’s a nationally televised game, after all!
author: Ted Zahn

title: 6 key takeaways from the Seahawks’ snap counts vs. Cowboys
summary: The Seattle Seahawks came stumbling out of the preseason gates with a 17-7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Penalties, blown assignments, miscommunication, and generally disjointed play defined Seattle’s performance, which is by no means the end of the world when you’re talking about backups and roster hopefuls as opposed to starters, but it’s still not […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Cody White #82 of the Seattle Seahawks runs back the kickoff during the second quarter of the NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks came stumbling out of the preseason gates with a 17-7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Penalties, blown assignments, miscommunication, and generally disjointed play defined Seattle’s performance, which is by no means the end of the world when you’re talking about backups and roster hopefuls as opposed to starters, but it’s still not something Mike Macdonald and his staff want to see. As ever, preseason is a component and not the deciding factor for who makes a roster and who does not. We still can glean some information off of not just who’s playing, but how much they’re playing, and which point of the game they’re playing and with whom they’re with. Now that the snap counts tallied in the official NFL game book over the weekend, here are my main takeaways from both sides of the ball. Seattle Seahawks offensive snap counts Montorie Foster played a lot, but that might not be a good thing In my 53-man roster projection , I had Montorie Foster making the team. I’m going to retract that unless something changes with his special teams snaps. I saw him take training camp reps as a kick and punt returner, so I figured he’d be in the special teams mix. Foster played the whole game and led all receivers with 41 snaps, scoring Seattle’s only touchdown. He led the team in receptions and yards, which is nice for his audition to make the 53-man roster. That’s good! No special teams reps? That’s bad, if not ominous. Cody White, Ricky White III, and Emmanuel Henderson Jr all had some ST reps, with Cody running back a couple of kicks. There is zero chance any WR6 on the squad can get in without playing some special teams. Bryce Cabeldue is firmly on the bubble The second-year guard out of Kansas had zero offensive snaps in the first half, which is not encouraging. In camp, I’ve seen him get in some left guard work with the twos but also mixed in with third-team right guard. At the moment, it looks like Mason Richman has firmly staked his claim as a backup to Grey Zabel. And unlike Richman, Cabeldue really is kinda limited to guard, whereas Richman can play across the line. He’s even listed as a G/T but I’ve seen him get some work at center. Tory Horton is evidently an “established starter” Mike Macdonald made it clear on Friday that no established starters would play on Saturday (except, of course, Michael Dickson, Chris Stoll, and Jason Myers on special teams). I thought there would be a chance that Tory Horton, especially having not played a game since November, would get a few reps in with the second-team offense. That did not happen. Whether that’s exercising caution because of his injury recovery or deciding he’s valuable enough as a WR4 to not risk anything in preseason reps, sitting Horton did surprise me a bit. Meanwhile, Elijah Arroyo got 41 snaps on offense and played into the first snap of the fourth quarter. I expected him to be done by halftime and it’d be a Nick Kallerup and Nick Vannett sort of evening. Seattle Seahawks defensive snap counts A.J. Finley takes the bulk of the safety snaps alongside Bud Clark We knew the second-round rookie Bud Clark would feature heavily in his first NFL preseason game, but A.J. Finley proved to be the other starting safety alongside the former TCU star. Finley had the impressive interception off Sam Darnold during the Lumen Field practice last week, going full circle at the same place (and same practice) in which he tore his ACL a year ago. With Rodney Thomas II, D’Anthony Bell, and Maxen Hook all vying for one of those coveted safety spots, Finley has had extensive work with the second unit, and Finley played well into the fourth quarter. Rodney Thomas II, curiously enough, was shut out of any defensive snaps until the third quarter. We’ll see if that trend continues deeper into the preseason. Connor O’Toole, Jared Ivey, and Mike Morris function as edge rushers in first half The Seahawks sat Dante Fowler Jr, who might have been the only borderline player in terms of being an edge rusher who could play in preseason. In the first half, Connor O’Toole, Jared Ivey, and Mike Morris were the primary pass rushers on the outside. Ivey and Morris are obviously big fellas who can (and were) kicked to the inside at times. Jalan Gaines only had two pass-rushing snaps in the first half before a major uptick in the second half. Tyrice Knight’s busy half (more busy than Coach Macdonald would’ve liked) involved some lining up on the edge, which is consistent with what we saw at camp. Hold the camp hype on Andre Fuller, Michael Dansby With full acknowledgement that Shemar Jean-Charles’ horror show might bump one of these two up next week, the Seahawks’ rookie corners did not even get special teams run until the second half, let alone defensive snaps. It was Jean-Charles, Nehemiah Pritchett, and Noah Igbinoghene as the main cornerbacks in the first half, which at this point is more of an indicator of the depth pieces likely to make the roster. As much as Fuller and Dansby have made good strides in training camp, there’s still a lot of work to be done to avoid roster cuts at the end of the month. Add in the impending Terrion Arnold signing and the road for both men just got a little tougher. And now, as John Gilbert likes to say, it’s on to Nashville for a joint practice and second preseason game with the Tennessee Titans.

title: 49ers bring back Nick Zakelj; add an EDGE rusher
summary: The San Francisco 49ers announced that they’ve signed defensive lineman Victor Dimukeje and offensive lineman Nick Zakelj to one-year deals heading into the second week of the preseason. Zakelj was released eight days ago for Doug Kramer Jr. after he missed a week of practice with an elbow injury. To make room for those two, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 8: Offensive tackle Nick Zakelj #63 of the San Francisco 49ers enters the field during player introductions prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears, at Levi's Stadium on December 8, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers announced that they’ve signed defensive lineman Victor Dimukeje and offensive lineman Nick Zakelj to one-year deals heading into the second week of the preseason. Zakelj was released eight days ago for Doug Kramer Jr. after he missed a week of practice with an elbow injury. To make room for those two, the team released running back Khalil Herbert and offensive lineman Kion Smith. Smith played 33 snaps at right guard in last Thursday’s preseason game. He struggled against the run and also allowed a pair of pressures. His performance was enough to bring Zakelj back. Dimukeje was drafted in the sixth round of the 2021 NFL Draft out of Duke by the Arizona Cardinals. He most recently played for the Giants last season. Dimukeje’s best season was in 2023, when he had 17 pressures and four sacks. He’s listed at 6’2″, 265 pounds. Dimukeje only played 16 snaps for New York last season. His playing time has declined since ’23, going from 368 snaps to 152, before last year. He has dropped in coverage over the years, with at least four targets from 2022 through 2024. The 49ers only used five edge rushers in their first preseason game. Dimukeje gives them another body to get through the preseason, especially if they’re not going to play Nick Bosa, and use Keion White or Sam Okuayinonu sparingly in games.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers stock report: A good showing for the rookies; not so much for the ‘25 class
summary: As we turn the page to the second week of the preseason, let’s do a stock report for some of the San Francisco 49ers fighting for roster spots and playing time. We saw the kids get most of the playing time, as the past couple of draft classes make up most of the depth. Here’s who helped […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: Gracen Halton #93 of the San Francisco 49ers tackles Tyjae Spears #2 of the Tennessee Titans during the game at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The Titans defeated the 49ers 19-13. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we turn the page to the second week of the preseason, let’s do a stock report for some of the San Francisco 49ers fighting for roster spots and playing time. We saw the kids get most of the playing time, as the past couple of draft classes make up most of the depth. Here’s who helped themselves during the first preseason game, and here is who needs to dig themselves out of a hole. Stock up QB Kurtis Rourke Rourke may have played himself onto the roster, at least initially, after running a smooth operation in his first real competitive football game in nearly two years. Rourke wasn’t frazzled in the face of a blitz. He completed all three of his passes when Robert Saleh sent extra rushers with an impressive average depth of target of 14.3 yards. All three of Rourke’s completions went for first downs when he was blitzed. He pushed the ball downfield, knew where to go with the football, and played on time, all while maintaining his aggressiveness. Rourke looked like he was good enough to be a QB2 in this league. S Ashtyn Davis Davis played the fourth-most defensive snaps and played on every kick coverage unit. He had only one tackle, but he played the run well and was aggressive with his run fits. Davis was where he needed to be in coverage and should’ve had an interception. For somebody who signed in June , Davis looked the part. He’s making the roster. OG Carver Willis Willis was a pleasant surprise. Watching him in college, I thought his lack of arm length and ability to anchor would be an issue as a pro. While those issues could still surface, only one rep showed Willis’s arm length mattered. And for the most part, Willis looked like he had enough sand in his pants to hold his ground. Willis earned reps with the starters based on his play in the first preseason game. Stock Down LT Enrique Cruz Jr. In that video of Willis above, it’s hard not to notice Cruz Jr., and not in a complementary way. It’s as if he’s guessing what his assignment is and figuring out what to do on the fly once the ball is snapped. Week 1 was a doozy for Cruz Jr. If you didn’t know any better, you would have thought it was the first time he’s played the sport. CB Jakob Robinson The door was open for Robinson, and he didn’t walk through it. He only allowed two receptions on five targets, but that was due more to errant throws than sticky coverage. On the non-targets, Robinson was often out of position. While Robinson had a run stop, he was blocked into oblivion on the first play of the game. CB Alfred Collins Oof. Collins was one of the players we listed as having the most to prove ahead of Week 1. Unfortunately, his struggles were on full display. Collins was easily moved multiple times. His technique was shoddy, and he got washed out of his gap all too often. Collins is supposed to be a run-stopper. CB Darrell Luter Jr. Luter Jr. seems like the athlete who can jump out of the gym and beat everybody in a race as a freshman, but never lifts weights, watches film, or does what he needs to do to become a better player. I don’t think he makes the roster. He gave up one catch for 17 yards on three targets, but was lucky the stat line wasn’t something like three catches for 45 yards. There were coverage busts on route combinations where there shouldn’t be busts. Barring a couple of stellar performances to end the preseason, Luter Jr.’s time is up. Stock up WR Malik Turner Turner had a strong showing. He won at every level, competed well as a blocker, and had more nuance in his routes than arguably any other player. The box score wasn’t kind to Turner, but he held up his end of the bargain in every facet. Turner is unlikely to make the roster, but he certainly did enough to make the practice squad. DT Bryson Eason Aside from making plays, Eason showed the kind of IQ some four-year pros don’t have when it comes to taking on blocks. Eason had tremendous awareness. I loved that he always knew where the ball carrier was and found a way to work back toward him. Unlike Collins, Eason used different techniques, like a drop leg, to hold his ground against double teams. DT Gracen Halton Halton tied for the most stops of any defensive tackle with four in Week 1. He’s a finisher. Even in a preseason setting, that’s noteworthy, as the Niners’ interior struggled mightily to make plays a season ago. What was encouraging about Halton was his ability to make plays against the run. He was supposed to be a pass rush specialist. But should we be surprised about Halton getting off to a hot start? He fell to Day 3 of the draft, but he was projected to go in the second round during the mock draft cycle. Perhaps Halton is showing his true colors and proving mock drafters right.

full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Khalil Herbert #40 of the San Francisco 49ers carries the ball against the Tennessee Titans in the second half at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Khalil Herbert signed with the San Francisco 49ers at the beginning of August . After a couple of weeks of training camp and a preseason game where he had six carries for 18 yards, including nine yards after contact and one forced missed tackle, the 49ers are releasing the veteran running back, according to Adam Schefter. This could signal that Christian McCaffrey may return to practice this week after missing time due to muscle tightness. The Athletic’s Matt Barrows noted running backs Jordan James (rib), Kaelon Black (adductor), and Isaac Guerendo (pec) were working on the side of the field during Sunday’s practice. However, James and Black aren’t expected back at practice this week or to partake in the preseason game against the Chargers. Barrows noted that they could return for the preseason finale. With Herbert released, that leaves Sincere McCormick and Zamir White as the only healthy backs. He’s not listed as a running back on the depth chart, but Deebo Samuel would likely be the first player up in the backfield if neither of the top four backs were healthy. We’ll provide updates once there is a corresponding move to Herbert’s release.

full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers looks on before the fourth quarter of a preseason NFL game between the Tennessee Titans and the San Francisco 49ers on August 13, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have been without running back Christian McCaffrey for roughly a week now after he suffered an injury described as “ muscle tightness .” According to Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio , somebody who seemingly always has a bone to pick with the Niners, McCaffrey is holding in and wants a new contract: “People are starting to wonder if it’s a hold-in. The tightness happens just days after Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs blow up the running back market, and McCaffrey is in the next-to-last year of his contract. $12.5 million; none of it is guaranteed. Well the average is 19. Guys only care about what they’re making now. It’s for the team to structure the deal in a way where the guy feels like, in the out years, he’s getting properly compensated. He’s looking at 12.5 saying, What’s wrong with this picture? It could be that he’s taking a stand quietly to get more money without it being obvious like it was with Robinson and Gibbs because they weren’t practicing because of their contract.” Florio’s co-host, Chris Simms, said the timing of the injury was curious and that McCaffrey’s wallet is feeling the tightness. Simms also said the 49ers should be reluctant to attach themselves to McCaffrey for a few more years when it comes to guaranteed money at his age. McCaffrey is the only player to have more than 400 touches in a season since the league expanded to 17 games. He’s also the only person to have over 400 touches in the past decade. McCaffrey is on the list twice. If this is true, McCaffrey understands this may be his last chance to cash in on a lucrative deal. It’ll be interesting to see if, for one, it’s a hold-in involving money, and two, the 49ers end up adding guarantees to McCaffrey’s contract. He’s been the focal point of the Niners’ offense. It shouldn’t be a surprise that CMC wants to be compensated after last season. Simms said there were rumblings in training camp last year that McCaffrey wanted a “refresher” on his contract. He also mentioned how history isn’t on McCaffrey’s side. There’s no data on Le’Veon Bell, the last person to have a 400+ touch season, because he was ineligible to return in 2018 after failing to report to the Steelers. Former Seahawks running back Shaun Alexander went from an 1,880-yard season after playing every game to an 896-yard season in 2006, when he missed six games. He never played a full season again and retired three seasons later. Larry Johnson of the Chiefs was never the same after his 400+ touch season in 2006. He missed half the season in 2007 and never ran for over 875 yards in the seasons after. McCaffrey isn’t an outlier when it comes to injuries, but he is as a football player. Will the 49ers reward him as such?
