title: How important is pass protection for a running back? Ask Jaxson Dart
summary: Dart was leveled after Tyrone Tracy missed a block, reflecting how important the underrated skill is for running backs.
full_text:
IT WAS SUPPOSED to be a routine dropback.

 In the  New York Giants ' preseason opener against the Minnesota Vikings on Saturday, starting quarterback Jaxson Dart dropped back and was looking left at his downfield options. On his right, chaos was looming.

 Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr . drifted a bit too far right, tried to reverse course and slipped. Vikings safety Jay Ward sprinted toward Dart and leveled the quarterback. All Tracy could do was crane his neck backward while kneeling on the turf as Dart was crushed at the midfield logo.

 Dart went through the concussion sideline exam and later returned. That didn't stop Giants coach John Harbaugh from saying, "There's no way he should have been hit there. It just shouldn't have happened. It was a basic protection."

 The preseason play highlighted one of the most overlooked aspects of football: a running back's role in pass protection. Typically, the glory and grandeur for ball carriers depends on the number of yards and touchdowns they produce. But a running back who can block is invaluable, especially in the modern game. It's a skill that can secure a spot on the 53-player roster, earn offensive reps and even extend contracts.

 

 And at its core, it sums up the nature of football.

 "It's mano a mano," said Bengals running back Samaje Perine , who is one of the better backs at pass protection in the league. "Everybody else is covered up by linemen. It's just me and you, and may the best man win."

 

 IN 2014, PERINE set the NCAA single-game record with 427 rushing yards in Oklahoma's win over Kansas. While he hasn't been as prolific in his 10-year NFL career, he still has been effective, averaging 4.5 yards per carry or more in five of his past six seasons.

 But the primary reason he has earned nearly $14 million in his career is what he does when he isn't carrying the ball.

 "As a running back, you can't be one-dimensional," Perine said. "If you can only run the ball and if you're not that [No. 1] guy, then your chances of staying in the league go down a lot.

 "So I've learned that just the more you can do, the longer you can stay in."

 What Perine and other effective pass-blocking running backs excel at is typically referred to as a "jet" protection -- where the offensive line will slide to block any defenders and the running back picks up an extra blitzer.

 But here's what that actually looks like: a defender who weighs 200 pounds or more sprinting toward a player who is stationary and bracing for impact.

 After his rookie year in 2017, Aaron Jones was at a charity event during Super Bowl week and ran into Brian Westbrook, an All-Pro running back who played for the Philadelphia Eagles from 2002 to 2009. Jones had one question: How do you get better in pass protection?

 "He was like, 'That's your mom in the pocket,'" Jones recalled. "'Are you going to let him touch your mom? Are you going to let him hit your mom?'

 "I was like, 'When you think about it like that, you're right.'"

 

 Jones wasn't the only running back to gain counsel from a veteran during an early stage in his career. Before New England Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson went to the Senior Bowl in 2021, ex-Dallas Cowboy DeMarco Murray, then Stevenson's position coach at Oklahoma, told him that being a proficient pass blocker would generate more interest from teams.

 Murray was right. Stevenson was drafted in the fourth round and is set to enter his sixth season with the Patriots.

 And when Stevenson and other running backs execute a pass block to perfection, it can lead to big things from their offense.

 

 "The underrated part about pass blocking is picking up a pass block and watching [Patriots quarterback Drake Maye ] sit back there with time and throw a [deep ball]," Stevenson said.

 Zach Allen , the Denver Broncos ' 6-5, 285-pound defensive end who had seven sacks last season, has noticed something different about the 6-foot, 227-pound Stevenson.

 "We played the Patriots, we did a stunt and I wrapped, and Stevenson was right there," Allen said. "Usually, you just bull the running back, but I gave him that first contact and I was like, 'OK, I might have to work to a side against him.' Powerful guy.

 "A big body and he takes pride in it. It's easy to see when a guy doesn't."

 

 WHEN THE 2024 season opener was on the line, Baltimore Ravens running back Justice Hill had one of the most daunting tasks in football: blocking Kansas City Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones , one of the game's fiercest pass rushers.

 Hill, despite being 8 inches shorter and 115 pounds lighter than Jones, had to keep Jones off Lamar Jackson on back-to-back plays to give the Ravens a chance to win. And Hill did his job. Jackson nearly threw the game-tying pass at the end of regulation in a 27-20 loss.

 The clip went viral as Hill received praise for one of the game's unsung jobs.

 "Obviously I'm not the biggest guy, but it just takes a mindset of like, 'You're not going to get to my quarterback, and I don't care how big you are, how small you are,'" Hill said.

 What makes pass blocking as a running back unique is that it is one of the more teachable skills in football. The calculation is pretty simple.

 

 "It's probably 90% grit, 10% technique," Perine said. "Because at the end of the day, you just have to get in the way."

 That is always easier said than done, especially when facing someone like  Derwin James Jr ., the Los Angeles Chargers ' 6-2, 215-pound safety.

 "Most everybody else, they'll run at you, but then they'll break down at least a little bit to give you a chance to think what you're going to do," Perine said. "Him? He doesn't care. He's just going to run full speed straight into you, torpedo style."

 But a lot goes into that 10% of technique. At the beginning of each game week, Bengals assistant coach Justin Hill will spend considerable time identifying defensive fronts, patterns and what makes different players effective as a pass rusher. Any edge gleaned that can give the quarterback an extra split second is valuable.

 "It's not just about being physical at the point of attack," Justin Hill said. "It's also about you got to be smart enough to understand what the different looks are."

 And sometimes, looks can be deceiving. The Giants thought it was  Jamal Adams  who was going to be blitzing on the play that dropped Dart.

 "I didn't really think I would have a free rush, but our big nickel -- Jamal -- he sold it, so the protection slid to him," Ward said. "The back so happened to get ready to go into a route and ... he didn't think he had anyone [to block] and he seen me come late, and he couldn't adjust."

 Aaron Jones said pass blocking is a two-part process, with the first part being able to understand the protection scheme.

 "And then it comes to a want-to and a fight," he said. "So, I would say part of it is understanding protection, and the next part is having the willingness to do it.

 "Now we know every protection is not going to be perfect, but if you get in there and fight and you hit them first, that negates a lot of their charge. Now you're just hand fighting and standing in front instead of this guy hitting you. A lot of times when you get up there and you make that contact, it slows it down and it makes your job a lot easier."

 

 BEING A RELIABLE pass blocker and adding value to teams will be paramount across the NFL over the next couple of weeks. As teams prepare to trim their rosters from the 90-player limit in training camp down to the allotted 53 roster slots for the regular season, protecting the quarterback could prevent a running back from being cut.

 "It's crazy how long that can extend your career," Justice Hill said. "If you told me my second year when I felt like s---, 'You'll be playing here,' standing here at eight years, I wouldn't have believed it.

 "So yeah, just keep doing those little things, and it pays off long term."

 Hill didn't mean to minimize it,…

title: 2026 Carolina Panthers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Panthers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Panthers writer Mike Kaye will have the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Panthers camp. Will QB Bryce Young and the Panthers take another step forward after making the playoffs in 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Panthers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 Monday, Aug. 17 
 New Panthers tight end Darren Waller 's free agency waiting game ended last Wednesday. He said his agent called him about the opportunity that morning right before he was heading out to a training session.

 Waller, who will turn 34 in September, didn't practice on Monday after officially signing with his fifth NFL team. Instead, he watched the workout, chatting with coaches and new teammates throughout the session.

 In Carolina, he is reunited with safety Tre'von Moehrig , whom he played with previously in Las Vegas, and outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and associate head coach Darrell Bevell, whom he worked with in Miami last season.

 According to coach Dave Canales, Waller isn't likely to mix it up with the Jaguars in joint practices on Wednesday in Jacksonville. But the veteran playmaker might be able to suit up in his newly issued No. 35 jersey and get some individual work with starting quarterback Bryce Young .

 

 More observations: 

 
 Ja'seem Reed , a training camp wide receiver-turned-summer standout, sustained a calf injury against the Buffalo Bills on Saturday, according to Canales. He was set to undergo imaging on the ailment Monday after practice. 
 Outside linebacker Cam Gill played through a shoulder injury against the Bills, posting a sack in the second preseason game. He was held out of the first workout of the week due to increased soreness, according to Canales. 
 Rookie cornerback Will Lee III played through a groin injury against Buffalo but was sidelined Monday during practice. 
 The Panthers cross-trained offensive linemen during the workout. Rookie Albert Reese IV , who was signed as an offensive tackle, played second-team right guard, while veteran Jake Curhan worked with the second-team line as a left guard. Chandler Zavala , who had an underwhelming outing against Buffalo as the starting left guard, played second-team center. Backup center Nick Samac took his turn as the third-string right guard for the third time this summer. 
 The highlight of the hottest practice session to date was an intermediate sideline toss from Young to wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan over cornerback Akayleb Evans , who was wearing a red non-contact jersey. Young fit the ball perfectly in front of McMillan to grab it right before heading out of bounds. 
 Third-string QB Kyle Trask , who was signed last week, fired an excellent deep ball shot to depth wide receiver Casey Washington for a touchdown in 11-on-11 drills. 
 

 
 Who is the Panthers' top performer so far at camp? 
 Third-year wide receiver Jalen Coker 's immediate returns after receiving a three-year, $34 million contract extension in July have made the Panthers' brass look wise this summer. The former undrafted playmaker has gotten open with regularity and caught the ball cleanly and consistently throughout training camp.

 Coker has looked dynamic opposite Tetairoa McMillan , who has impressed in his own right. The top tandem's summer production has been encouraging, especially with third-round pick  Chris Brazzell II  (knee) out for the season and 2024 first-round pick Xavier Legette still working to live up to his draft pedigree.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Will the offensive line be able to overcome a litany of injury adversity to begin the season?

 The Panthers' longtime starting tackles,  Ikem Ekwonu  (knee) and Taylor Moton (blood clot), will be sidelined into the regular season. They'll be replaced by free-agent addition Rasheed Walker at left tackle and first-round pick Monroe Freeling at right tackle, respectively. Walker has plenty of starting experience, but Freeling is switching to the opposite side of the line as a rookie.

 Left guard Damien Lewis (calf) and right guard Rob Hunt (back) missed several practices during the first few weeks of training camp. Brady Christensen , a versatile backup, will be an important insurance policy for both.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 The Carolina Panthers consider running back Chuba Hubbard to be "week-to-week" after he injured his hamstring in Wednesday's practice.

 Head coach Dave Canales said Hubbard underwent an MRI on Thursday before practice and the starting running back will be sidelined for the second preseason matchup against the Buffalo Bills in Orchard Park, New York on Saturday.

 According to Canales, Hubbard sustained the injury during a one-on-one drill.

 With Hubbard sidelined, Jonathon Brooks and Trevor Etienne will rotate in with the starters for a couple of series, Canales said. A.J. Dillon will also receive an early workload against Buffalo.

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Defensive end Derrick Brown (knee) and outside linebacker Pat Jones (illness) wore uniforms during Thursday's non-padded practice. Brown took part in individual drills after working with a trainer before practice. 
 Left guard Damien Lewis (calf) and right guard Rob Hunt (back) took team reps together. They were replaced by Chandler Zavala and Brady Christensen later in practice. 
 Wide receiver Jimmy Horn Jr . was getting open with ease throughout practice, but he was rarely targeted by the quarterbacks. 
 Starting quarterback Bryce Young had an excellent sequence to end practice during the two-minute drill in 11-on-11 work. He hit wide receiver Xavier Legette on a shallow cross and the playmaker sped up the field untouched for a touchdown. On the next and final play, Young rolled around the pocket with no one open and zipped a laser through defenders to tight end Tommy Tremble for a touchdown. 
 Tight end Darren Waller didn't make his practice debut on Thursday because he had to undergo a physical. The team still needs to make a corresponding move to fit him on the roster. A source with knowledge of the situation told ESPN the team plans to sign Waller following the preseason matchup against the Bills on Saturday. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan has gotten "bigger and stronger" this offseason, according to head coach Dave Canales . And that improved physique was on display throughout Wednesday's practice in Charlotte.

 McMillan started the day with a nifty double move against starting cornerback Mike Jackson in one-on-one drills. McMillan was able to create increased separation with his route progression after beating Jackson off the line. The wideout then hauled in the ball for a touchdown a few paces in front of Jackson.

 "At the line of scrimmage, just hasn't really had an issue this camp," Canales said. "Getting off the line, I think that he's really translating all the work he did in the offseason. ... I'm really excited where he's at."

 Later, during team drills, the connection between quarterback Bryce Young and McMillan was apparent.

 Young was picked off by Jackson on an early rep while targeting McMillan. But following that miscue, the starting quarterback connected with McMillan on more than a handful of tosses.

 Other observations: 

 
 Along with Jackson's interception against Young in team drills, safety  Demani Richardson  intercepted a pass from backup QB Kenny Pickett in 11-on-11 drills. 
 Left guard Damien Lewis (calf) returned to practice in pads…

title: DB Wright leaves Bengals preseason to pursue acting
summary: Rookie Ceyair Wright -- who starred alongside LeBron James in 'Space Jam: A New Legacy' -- is giving new meaning to dual threat.
full_text:
It's not usually particularly noteworthy when an undrafted rookie leaves an NFL team during preseason. But Cincinnati Bengals defensive back Ceyair Wright's reason seems to be far from typical.

 Wright is leaving the team to reportedly further his acting career.

 "Two things he's really passionate about were colliding, and he decided to pursue this opportunity," Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Saturday . "We wish him the best. He was fun to be around, he really competed hard for us. It was fun watching him play. I thought he was ascending as a player, but obviously he's chosen to go a different path."

 

 The switch isn't a spur-of-the-moment change for Wright. In addition to being a former top-200 recruit who finished his collegiate career with 109 total tackles and three interceptions, the former USC and Nebraska defensive back has built an acting résumé away from the field over the years as well.

 Wright has appeared in seven films and television shows dating to 2014 -- including, most notably to sports fans, a role as LeBron James ' son in "Space Jam: A New Legacy" (2021).

 

 What's next for Wright in his acting career remains publicly unknown. But he won't be the first former gridiron staple to transition from football to film.

title: 2026 Cleveland Browns training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our updates from Browns training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Browns reporter Daniel Oyefusi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Browns camp. The biggest question for Cleveland remains who will be the starting QB? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Browns' top camp performer and biggest lingering question.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Browns stories 
 
 Deshaun Watson returns with 'awesome' first half for Browns 
 What are the Browns looking for in their QB competition? 
 Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs 
 AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Deshaun Watson: Preseason is 'great opportunity' after injuries 
 Deion Sanders gives Browns 'insight' on Shedeur Sanders 
 GM Andrew Berry 'hopeful' Browns can reunite with Jadeveon Clowney 
 

 
 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 Shedeur Sanders is slated to start at quarterback in the Browns' second preseason game against the Bills on Saturday, but he could be playing without Cleveland's starting offense.

 Coach Todd Monken said he and Bills coach Joe Brady agreed to hold out starters if their No. 1 units get enough work in during joint practices on Thursday.

 "Would I like to have a decision today? Of course," Monken said. "Would I like a decision by next Monday? Of course. I'd love to have that decision. And we'll see. We've got a lot of football this week. We've already had a lot of football. We've got four days of practice and a game. That all adds into any decision with the roster and who the starters are.

 "Some are further along than others, right? We already know. That's part of it. And I'm OK. By the time we get to next week, that'd be great. We can start planning that way, have some practices, and here we go."

 More observations: 

 
 Michael Coats Jr . and Nate Evans practiced after leaving the preseason opener with injuries. 
 Zak Zinter , Myles Bryant , and Elijah Chatman returned to practice after missing multiple sessions, as well as the preseason opener. 
 Thirteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Cedric Tillman , D'Angelo Ross , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger ,  Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Jack Conley , Jack Stoll , Alex Wright (new), Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . 
 Monken said the Browns are being "overly cautious" with Schwesinger, who hasn't practiced since July 31. The team is hopeful he will return to practice next week. 
 The Browns signed tight end Jermaine Terry II and waived tight end Brenden Bates with an injury designation. 
 

 

 Who has been the Browns' top performer so far at camp? 
 WR Denzel Boston . The No. 39 overall pick is trending to be Cleveland's No. 1 receiver sooner rather than later. Boston has dazzled with plenty of highlights, using his 6-foot-4, 215-pound frame to make contested catches almost daily. He's also made himself a friendly target for quarterbacks as a smooth route runner. Boston recently got promoted to the No. 1 offense as Cleveland's boundary receiver.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Who will be the Browns' starting quarterback? Deshaun Watson will start the preseason opener;  Shedeur Sanders will start the second preseason game. The exhibition matches will allow Todd Monken to evaluate the quarterbacks in a bevy of game-like situations. The first-year head coach is placing an importance on pre-snap operation and playmaking ability.

 
 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Browns are hoping quarterback  Deshaun Watson 's return to health will mean a return to the Pro Bowl form he displayed with the Texans, but Watson said Wednesday that "my game has definitely changed."

 "I'm different, man," Watson said before practice. "I think ever since I've been here early on, bringing up Houston was cool, but I'm 30 now. I had some injuries and things like that. So, my game has definitely changed. But the mentality in how I play and how I approach it doesn't."

 Watson was one of the NFL's top dual-threat passers in Houston, but suspension and injuries have limited him to just 19 games since Cleveland traded for him in March 2022.

 "I think you have to be who you are because if you try to be something you're not, you're not going to play at the highest level of your skill set," coach Todd Monken said. "So it's just the way it is with him; he's going to have to play or utilize his athleticism in order to play at the top of his skill set. ... But one of the superpowers is his athleticism. I mean, that always has been. So you can't take that away or you've basically taken away a part of what made him special."

 More observations: 

 
 In a lighter practice ahead of the team's preseason opener against the Bears, Watson and Shedeur Sanders led successful two-minute drills to cap the session. Both quarterbacks connected on deep passes during their possession. Sanders had a deep completion to wide receiver Isaiah Bond , who made a diving catch. Watson lofted a pass to receiver Luke Floriea along the offense's sideline. 
 Teven Jenkins and Tyre Phillips split snaps at right guard with the No. 1 offense. 
 Cornerback Denzel Ward and offensive tackle Izavion Miller returned to practice. Cornerback Tyron Herring left practice with a member of the team's medical staff during individual drills. 
 Fifteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Cedric Tillman (new absence), D'Angelo Ross , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall, Parker Brailsford , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Elgton Jenkins , Dae'Quan Wright , Jack Stoll , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis . Veteran edge rusher Tyus Bowser had a tryout with the Browns on Wednesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Four days before their preseason opener against the Chicago Bears on Saturday, the Browns listed " Deshaun Watson  OR Shedeur Sanders " at starting quarterback in their first unofficial depth chart.

 Coach Todd Monken has yet to announce which quarterback will start in Chicago, but spoke about the value the preseason adds for evaluating the two passers.

 "It does, in terms of getting the ball out, got to learn to get the ball out. Got to learn how to slide," Monken said. "You're not going to be able to just run around. I do want playmaking ability, so there is a balance there between playmaking ability and taking some sacks. You're going to have to live with that to an extent.

 "The other part is stacking plays, where it matters, because they got the scoreboard on in terms of points you put on the board. In terms of the flow of the game, that's a big part of it. We're going to be on the road. The ebbs and flows of positive plays and negative plays, overcoming that. I think there's a part of the quarterback's body language, how they are around the team. Do I sense, 'Hey, that's over. I've moved on to the next play.' So there's a number of things you get to evaluate once you get to the closest we have in terms of games, which is preseason."

 With rookie Spencer Fano securing a starting role at left tackle, Monken said the only starting position on the offensive line up in the air is right guard. Teven Jenkins and KT Leveston have been rotating at the spot.

 "I think Teven has the advantage there from experience," Monken said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Special teams coordinator Byron Storer said the team is "definitely taking a hard look at" punters Wes Pahl and Nik Constantinou , but "It's Corey [Bojorquez]'s job to lose." 
 Monken said he is "hopeful" that defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr . will return to practice "soon." Hall hasn't practiced since Aug.…

title: 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Cowboys training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Cowboys reporter Todd Archer has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Cowboys' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Miller to play 15th season after getting 1-year deal from Cowboys 
 Sources: Cowboys, Quinnen Williams reach 3-year, $105.9M deal 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Who is the Cowboys' top performer so far at camp? 

 George Pickens . He has essentially made a big play in every practice as he gets set to play on the $27.3 million franchise tag. Whatever disenchantment some might have expected from Pickens without a long-term deal has not materialized. Coaches have noted his attention in the meeting rooms since the start of training camp.

 He and Dak Prescott have picked up where they left off in 2025 when the receiver had career highs in catches, yards and touchdowns. Does that mean he will surpass those figures again in 2026? Not necessarily, but his performance so far has shown a focused player as the season inches closer.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 Because the Cowboys aren't going to play their starters in the preseason, it's impossible to completely answer anything about the defense. There have been encouraging signs there, but let's look to the offense for what can be answered in the preseason games: Who will back up Prescott?

 Joe Milton III and Sam Howell have alternated as Prescott's backup in practice and both have had good moments and not-so-good ones. The Cowboys believe they have line play and skill players to give both QBs a fair shot to perform in the preseason and not have them running for their lives. Read more below:

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 For the second time this month, the Cowboys will hold a joint practice, hosting the New Orleans Saints  on Tuesday after traveling to the Los Angeles Rams a week ago.

 The importance of the work isn't lost on tight end Jake Ferguson , who, like the rest of the Cowboys' starters and regulars, will not play in any of the three preseason games.

 "It's usually their starting defense going against our starting offense," Ferguson said. "That's where we get a good read of what we're looking like, what we're feeling like, what we need to clean up. We had that one against the Rams and came out firing. It was a lot of things we needed to clean up, but this is a good tell."

 The Saints will bring a familiar face with coach Kellen Moore. Ten years ago, Moore was Tony Romo 's backup for Dallas before breaking his ankle early in training camp. It helped pave the way for Dak Prescott to become the starter. Moore became a Cowboys assistant coach and served as offensive coordinator from 2019 to 2022. Moore also interviewed for the Cowboys head coaching vacancy that went to Brian Schottenheimer.

 "Kellen and I have kind of laid it out," Schottenheimer said. "It'll be similar to what we did with the Rams. A few less reps since they have another joint practice coming up [with the Rams], but you'll see a lot of the same situational work, some of the special teams stuff."

 More observations: 

 Monday's practice was conducted in helmets and jerseys, with no shells or pads, since the players were just two days removed from a preseason game. With the late return from Seattle, the Cowboys could not meet until late in the morning, and they held a practice that ran about 75 minutes.

 A sign the starters will get most of the work versus New Orleans: The backups had only 12 reps in practice; the starters had 30.

 Jaydon Blue was the only running back to not take any snaps during practice. He went through individual drills, but he is dealing with a shoulder injury. Phil Mafah (chest) did not get a carry, but he caught one pass. The bulk of the work went to Javonte Williams , Malik Davis and Israel Abinkanda .

 

 Friday, Aug. 14 

 Most of the regulars will not play in Saturday's preseason opener against the Seattle Seahawks , but there is one important position that could start to take shape: backup quarterback.

 Throughout training camp, Joe Milton III and Sam Howell have alternated days as Dak Prescott 's backup as they compete to be the No. 2.

 "It's been a very highly competitive contest," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "I think Joe's talent and ability to throw the football and athleticism jumps off the practice field when you see it. I think Sam's doing a great job of moving the team. But at the end of the day, the preseason games, they're going to play really the entire preseason, and that's where the bulk of the evaluation will be."

 Schottenheimer said there has been a back and forth between the quarterbacks. Milton served as Prescott's backup last year, appearing in four games and completing 15 of 24 passes for 183 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. Howell signed a one-year deal worth $2.5 million guaranteed in free agency.

 He has started 18 games in his career, including all 18 for the Washington Commanders in 2023.

 Milton said having a full year in the offense has "definitely made a huge difference. Shoot, coming in here last year at this time I probably knew 85% of the playbook, 75% of the playbook. Now it's pretty much everything and picking up all of the small stuff, the new stuff, so it's been great."

 Howell has liked what he has done in training camp.

title: DeMarcus Ware on Von Miller to Cowboys: 'This is all he wanted'
summary: Signing with the Cowboys, Miller is headed back home to Texas, where he grew up and played for Texas A&M.
full_text:
OXNARD, Calif. -- Not long after news broke that the Dallas Cowboys and Von Miller had entered into a one-year agreement, DeMarcus Ware made a video call to his former Denver Broncos teammate.

 The smile on their faces told the story.

 "I can go all the way back to when we played the Broncos [in 2013], and I remember talking to Von after the game, and he's like, 'Man, it would be so cool to play for the Dallas Cowboys,'" said Ware, who played for the Cowboys from 2005 to 2013.

 Over the past two months, the conversations between Ware and Miller had mentions of Miller joining the Cowboys this year. Miller told Ware that the Cowboys were the only team to make serious inquiries about signing him. More than once, Miller posted pictures of himself in a Cowboys uniform.

 "He kept saying, 'I think I'm going to the Dallas Cowboys,'" Ware said. "He was over [near The Star] working out. He just felt like something was going to work out."

 

 Miller's homecoming is not just about the DeSoto native, who played his college ball at Texas A&M, playing for his boyhood team. It's about helping the Cowboys win games and maybe even get to the Super Bowl. Miller can bring to Dallas' locker room his championship experience from winning Super Bowl 50 with the Broncos, when he teamed up with Ware, and Super Bowl LVI with the  Los Angeles Rams .

 "You got a lot of guys that come in, older guys that come in, former guys and they can teach, but it's different when you got somebody sitting in the seat with you that's going to get padded up with you, learning the same things as you and performing," Ware said. "Those guys, they looked up to you their whole careers, but now [they realize] I get to play with him? It's a totally different mindset that the boys are going to have now."

 Ware believes Miller can help the Cowboys' young edge rushers, such as  Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence , just like Ware helped Miller when he joined him on the Broncos in 2014 as a free agent.

 "It's the same mentality as when I came to Denver," Ware said. "It's like, 'I know I'm not going to get 20 sacks,' but I do know that he can make all the guys around him [better]. ... As a conglomerate, everybody's going to get better from the expertise, how to prep for the game, all the little keys and things he can teach, and you're still probably going to get 8-11 sacks out of this guy. I would sign up for that any day."

 

 Miller had nine sacks last season in Washington. The Cowboys view him as a piece of their pass rush group, not the leader of the group. At 37, it would not be fair to ask Miller to be the player he was in Denver.

 Miller's 138.5 sacks are the most among active players and tied with Ware for 13th all time. Ware thinks it's somehow fitting Miller will surpass him in a Cowboys jersey.

 "I don't think the Dallas Cowboys know how big of an opportunity this is for them, but not just them, for Von, too," Ware said. "For him, putting that jersey on, this is like icing on the cake. Like this is all he wanted. I know that's how he feels.

 "I know a lot of people might downplay it, but right now this dude is like a kid in the candy store."

 Monday, Aug. 17 
 Rookie running back Jonah Coleman continues to work his way up the depth chart toward a spot in the regular-season rotation, so much so that coach Sean Payton gave Coleman a fairly quick hook from the preseason opener. Coleman played 12 snaps Friday night in Atlanta and had four carries for 24 yards, with his last carry coming with 47 seconds left in the first quarter. Payton said he's seen enough from Coleman on the practice field to get the rookie out of the preseason opener that early.

 "I kind of felt it ... and there was a point when he got like two or three carries and I'm like 'alright, I've seen enough,'" Payton said. "I didn't need additional evidence of what I've been seeing for three weeks.''

 Coleman continues to get practice snaps with the first- and second-team offenses in camp in a variety of situations.

 More observations: 

 
 Inside linebacker Levelle Bailey suffered a fractured leg in the win over the Falcons, so the Broncos might be on the hunt for depth to finish out the preseason. Seventh-round rookie Red Murdock played the most defensive snaps in Friday's game (47) and continues to close in on a roster spot. Karene Reid (28 snaps) tipped the pass that cornerback Jahdae Barron returned 97 yards for a touchdown and undrafted rookie Taurean York played 22 snaps. Payton said "we'll see" when asked if they would add an inside linebacker, adding it was too soon to know if Bailey would be able to return this season. 
 Linebacker Drew Sanders played in his first game Friday since the playoff loss in Buffalo to close out the 2024 season -- he finished with a sack in 13 snaps against the Falcons. Sanders was held out of Monday's practice and worked on a side field. 
 Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle return to practice Monday and worked in team drills. Wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr . also returned to practice but worked on a side field after individual drills. 
 

 

 Who has been the Broncos' top performer at camp so far? 

 It is a close race between two receivers, second-year man Pat Bryant and Marvin Mims Jr ., with Bryant getting the nod in part due to Mims being slowed recently by a leg injury suffered last Friday.

 Mims started camp with a flourish, creating impact plays until he was limited by a soft-tissue injury that knocked him out of practice for a couple days. And on a team where most of the depth chart is settled, his efforts have been the most noteworthy.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 The Broncos suddenly have an issue at center, as starter Luke Wattenberg and backup Alex Forsyth have missed significant practice time with injuries while the No. 3 center -- Michael Deiter -- suffered a season-ending thigh injury this past week. It has put Calvin Throckmorton , who has gotten far more work at guard in his time with Denver, as the starting center, with undrafted rookie Gavin Ortega backing him up. Until either Wattenberg or Forsyth return to practice, center is a spot that could significantly impact how effective the Broncos are upfront.

 Since Bo Nix will not play in Friday's preseason opener in Atlanta, there will be a chance for Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger to continue what has been one of the most spirited position battles of camp. On a team that returns 20 of 22 starters on offense and defense from the AFC Championship Game and returns most of the backups, too, Stidham and Ehlinger have had a heated battle to be the No. 2 quarterback. And Friday might be their best chance to show what they can do given Nix is expected to play some snaps in the Broncos' two other preseason games.

 Coach Sean Payton said after Wednesday's practice that each of the quarterbacks will play a half against the Falcons. Stidham is expected to start the game and play the first half.

 "They're focused on like their best stuff, they're competing against the 31 other quarterbacks (in the league) like any other position," Payton said. "... It's a great room, they get along well."

 Ehlinger, who led the team with 412 yards passing last preseason, has been consistently lauded by Payton for his work in camp and has routinely moved the second- and third-team offenses in practices. Stidham led the quarterbacks in touchdown passes last preseason, with four in three games.

 More observations: 

 
 Payton expects most of the healthy starters to get about 15 plays against the Falcons and said some of the injured players will remain back in Denver to continue to rehab their injuries. Wide receivers Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims Jr ., who are both working back from leg injuries in camp, are expected to be among the group that remains in Denver. 
 When asked why he, unlike many other coaches, will likely have several starters play in all three preseason games, Payton said: "[You're] trying to win everything, I just believe in that." 
 Veteran center Michael Deiter , who was carted off the field during Tuesday's practice, will miss the remainder of the season with a thigh injury that will require surgery. "[I] feel bad for him and where he's at," Payton said. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Broncos owner/CEO Greg Penner, who had not spoken publicly since the league meetings in March, covered a variety of topics with local media on Tuesday. At one point he was asked about his expectations for the season, and he made it clear a team that returns all but two starters from the AFC Championship Game has the same expectations from him as the next year's team and the ones that come after that.

 "Our goal is to compete for championships every year and if we put ourselves in that position every year, we're going to be successful and win Super Bowls," he said.

 He also talked about the new five-year deal for coach Sean Payton that Payton signed in June, saying: "I've been really pleased with what he's built here, the culture, the performance on the field (and) it enabled us to line up he and [general manager] George [Paton's] contracts now. George has done a fantastic job building this roster."

 More observations: 

 
 Center is suddenly a trouble spot, as injuries continue to happen at the position. The Broncos' top two centers -- Luke Wattenberg and Alex Forsyth -- have missed time in camp and on Tuesday Michael Deiter -- who was signed for depth in the offseason after spending seven seasons in Miami, Houston and Washington -- was carted to the locker room. Calvin Throckmorton slid in as the first-team center, with undrafted rookie free agent Gavin Ortega providing depth. All-Pro guard Quinn Meinerz played some center early in his NFL career and could shift over if needed, but moving one of the NFL's best guards to another…

title: Texans ready to feature David Montgomery's dual-threat ability
summary: Houston traded for the running back and hopes he will complement quarterback C.J. Stroud.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- Days before hosting the Los Angeles Chargers in their preseason opener, the Houston Texans transformed practice at NRG Stadium into a dress rehearsal as they ran through a game-day simulation, knowing most starters wouldn't play in the exhibition.

 So during a competitive back-and-forth for the starters, quarterback C.J. Stroud surveyed Houston's stifling defense, searching for the crack that could finally spring the offense loose.

 Then, running back David Montgomery caught a floating pass from Stroud down the sideline and burst untouched into the end zone for an 80-yard touchdown. A sea of teammates flooded the field behind him as their celebration echoed through the otherwise empty stadium.

 The reception offered a glimpse of what Montgomery plans to deliver on game day: being an all-around back.

 

 "[Texans offensive coordinator] Nick Caley let me know that I will be able to showcase [my dual-threat ability] because I know I can do it," Montgomery told ESPN. "So, I'm excited."

 When Houston acquired Montgomery from the Detroit Lions in March for offensive lineman Juice Scruggs , a 2026 fourth-round draft pick and a 2027 seventh-rounder, it was to be a lead back.

 But Montgomery wants to shed the label of being only a physical back while he's the lead back for Houston. That includes showing his multidimensional ability to run downhill, outside the tackles and catch passes out of the backfield. He scoffed at the notion of being solely a physical back, confirming his attempt to distance himself from the label.

 "I can do everything," Montgomery told ESPN. "I try not to categorize myself."

 During Montgomery's three years with the Lions, he had a running mate in All-Pro Jahmyr Gibbs as they sported the nickname "Sonic and Knuckles" after 1990s video game characters that ran together. But in Houston, Montgomery is expected to be the star of the show -- even though running back Woody Marks has received rave reviews.

 In terms of doing it all, Montgomery has been effective running outside the numbers. Since his rookie season with the Chicago Bears  in 2019, he has averaged 4.6 yards running outside zone, and that's in multiple schemes for different teams. While running inside, he averaged 4.1 yards. He has 1,890 receiving yards with four touchdowns, and he believes that he has more to offer as a receiver.

 Through the first offseason with Montgomery, Caley has been pleased with the new addition to the backfield. Montgomery had 2,506 rushing yards (17th) and 33 touchdowns (eighth) in the past three seasons with the Lions. The Texans are hoping he can bring that production to an offense that ranked 22nd in rushing yards per game (108) last season.

 "He's all business," Caley said. "He's a really, really good player. He's grounded as a runner, but he's a very good pass-game player, and he's tough as nails in protection. Those guys have really fed off each other and just really pushed the needle and helped each other improve. I'm excited about them."

 

 A team with Super Bowl hopes wants to take pressure off Stroud. Relying on Montgomery and a physical run game that matches coach DeMeco Ryans' identity should help the offense become more effective.

 But don't be fooled, Ryans loves seeing Montgomery show some finesse to his game, just as he did on that 80-yard score last week.

 "It was a huge play. A huge momentum boost for our offense," Ryans said. "What David has done a really good job of is route running. Him and linebacker [ Henry To'oTo'o ] have had a lot of battles thus far in camp. It was cool to see David make a big play for us.

 "That's the type of player he is. That's why he's here for us. He can spark an offense. He can lift us with just making those plays, or it's just by him being a leader, being vocal and encouraging the other guys."

title: What we've seen from Travis Hunter at Jaguars training camp
summary: Hunter is almost through his second NFL training camp. What has stood out from his split time at receiver and cornerback?
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- For the first time in training camp, the  Jacksonville Jaguars  limited Travis Hunter to one side of the ball in 11-on-11 work.

 Hunter played exclusively at cornerback Monday, getting on the field for 20 of the 24 snaps. Coach Liam Coen said the move was done to allow Hunter to focus more on playing without missing any mental reps when switching to offense. 

 "When he's not in [on defense] and he's coming [onto] offense every time, we're losing out on even more coaching in those moments," Coen said. "And so wanted to just be very intentional today about getting him some of those visual reps so [defensive pass game coordinator Matt Araujo] can coach him even when he's not in [on defense]. He's not running over [to switch to offense]. So we just wanted to get him a little bit more of that."

 The 20 defensive snaps were the most Hunter has played on defense in a training camp practice, excluding last week's joint practice in New Orleans. Hunter, who did play five offensive snaps in the 7-on-7 period Monday, said he welcomed the extra work.

 "It's definitely beneficial," he said. "I needed to knock the rest off. I've got to get better somehow, somewhere, so I definitely took my time to hone in on [the] defensive [side], get better, get my feet up under me.

 "Can't let nobody catch the ball. That's my motto right now, just continue to focus and get better."

 Hunter has been on the field in 11-on-11 for 178 snaps so far in camp (minus the joint practice): 116 on defense, 61 on offense and one on special teams. Veteran cornerback Jourdan Lewis is still amazed when watching him play on both sides of the ball.

 "I told him he's a beast, man," Lewis said. "You've got camp two times, man, because you have to do it as a receiver and a corner, and I think he's handled it really well."

 As the Jaguars prepare for their second preseason game  Friday, here are three other takeaways from Hunter's second training camp in the pros:

 

 Hunter has 'elite ball skills' 
 Defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said Hunter, who has two interceptions in 11-on-11 so far in camp, has "elite ball skills." One takeaway came on a leaping snag of  Trevor Lawrence 's pass to Parker Washington on the goal line. The play was pretty much dead on a likely sack, but Lawrence threw the ball up anyway and Hunter came running in from the middle of the field for the interception.

 "The thing about Travis, you can see even in some of these practices, he can go up and tear the ball out of the air," Campanile said. "He goes after the ball like a receiver, so that's what's exciting about him. And you saw a little bit of that in practice the other day. I thought he made a heck of a play, honestly, coming out of nowhere and tearing the ball out of the sky."

 Coen described it this way: "Travis just came out of nowhere and makes the play. Like, I can't coach it [the ability to make plays like that]."

 On the first day of camp, Hunter broke up one and almost came down with a twisting, leaping catch on a Lawrence throw that was behind him. His body control to even get a hand on that throw was reminiscent of the body-contorting catches he had against the 49ers and Chiefs  last season.

 "When he has the ball in his hands, he can create something special," wide receiver  Jakobi Meyers  said. "He can make guys miss. He has a great awareness of defenders and space out there on the field, but he also has great ball skills. So those things kind of pop off the tape."

 
 

 He hasn't been targeted on defense a lot 
 One play from Monday's practice perfectly illustrates why Hunter hasn't been targeted a lot. Hunter had wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr . in man coverage, locking him up from the moment Thomas left the line of scrimmage. So Lawrence took a quick look Thomas' way then went elsewhere.

 It's not like the Jaguars' quarterbacks are completely avoiding him, as Washington beat Hunter off the sideline for a deep touchdown pass last week. On Monday, Lawrence threw twice to a receiver Hunter was guarding. He knocked down a pass intended for  CJ Williams , but he allowed Tim Jones to catch a short pass on the other.

 "When you have length and anticipation and have a good feel for routes, I think that the playmaking, getting your hands on balls or just denying the ball with good coverage, that's a win in itself that I think goes a little bit unnoticed from corners," Coen said. "It's like, yeah, when they don't get a lot of work, it's probably because they're doing their job and doing it at a high level, so I've been pleased with him."

 

 Hunter and Thomas are sharing reps 
 As expected, Hunter is being used in some packages as the third receiver.

 Washington and Meyers have been getting the most snaps of the receivers in camp -- even though Thomas was arguably the best player on the field in the spring and has had a great camp, showing some of the toughness and ball security that seemed to be missing last season.

 Coen likes using 12 personnel (one running back, two tight ends and two receivers), and the Jaguars are reluctant to put Washington on the sideline. When the Jaguars use 11 personnel (one back, one tight end and three receivers), Hunter and Thomas have shared reps.

 That doesn't mean Hunter and Thomas won't be on the field together once the season begins, but it's a little hint as to how this full receiver room will shake out. And while Coen hasn't announced their exact offensive plan for Hunter, the coach did hint that it could be bigger than some might expect.

 "We all know he's our 3A, 3B receiver right now, and [we're] trying to get him the exposure to every opportunity that we have out here," Coen said. "But right now, I mean, we need a lot of the communication, a lot of the repetition needs to continue obviously on both sides of the ball."

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 Wearing the usual white jersey for defenders, Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane fully participated in Monday's practice for the first time since camp started.

 Delane missed Saturday's preseason opener as the Chiefs held him out while he continued to let his right shoulder heal, an injury that had led him to wear a noncontact yellow jersey and miss the 11-on-11 reps. In Monday's work, Delane did well to cover receivers such as Rashee Rice , Nikko Remigio and rookie Cyrus Allen . If Delane continues progressing this week, he should make his preseason debut Saturday when the Chiefs face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 "He did everything and was in all the drills," coach Andy Reid said of Delane. "[He] looked good, so that's good work for him as he goes through that. We'll just monitor him and see how he does with the extended play."

 More observations: 

 
 Monday's practice was the Chiefs' longest of camp -- a session that lasted two hours and 15 minutes. Reid said backup left tackle Esa Pole left practice early because he was dehydrated. Receiver Andrew Armstrong sustained a strained hamstring, linebacker Jack Cochrane left early with a knee injury, and undrafted rookie safety DeShon Singleton tweaked a hamstring. 
 Missing practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms), safety Chamarri Conner (knee) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). "Trey is doing [well]," Reid said. "He's getting close. We'll see where it goes. I don't know if you'll see him this week, but he's getting close. 
 The lone major lineup change among the projected starters was along the offensive line. Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, switched from right guard -- the position he played in Saturday's preseason loss to the Los Angeles Rams -- to right tackle. Jaylon Moore , a five-year veteran, switched from right tackle to right guard, the spot where Smith starts. Reid suggested that Benson was moved to get him ready to play the right tackle position in Saturday's exhibition against the Buccaneers. "Moore has been doing a great job in there for us," Reid said. "With that, Benson doesn't get any reps at [right tackle]. We want him to go against the better players and have a chance to continue to grow there. We just flopped them over and let Moore get some reps at guard and Benson gets some reps at the tackle spot. Benson held his own at the guard spot in the game. They need to be able to play both [positions]. It's good experience for them." 
 

 

 

 Who has been the Chiefs' top performer so far at camp? 
 Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods has been a revelation. Not only has the first-round pick made an impact in each practice, but Woods has quickly shown that he has the quickness and strength to be a potential impact player next to pass rusher Chris Jones . Veterans including center Creed Humphrey , right guard Trey Smith and defensive end George Karlaftis  have praised Woods throughout camp.

 Woods' explosive ability has helped him produce highlight moments in the trenches, whether blowing by Humphrey on a running play or showing off his pass-rush skills in one-on-one drills. Just last week, the 6-foot-3, 310-pound Woods sprinted to chase down Patrick Mahomes , impressing the quarterback.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 The lone major position battle is at the right tackle position. Coach Andy Reid is eager to see how Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, performs in the preseason.

 The Chiefs have given Benson most of the first-team reps, hoping he can provide true competition to Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran. If Benson continues to overachieve, even in the preseason -- especially since he's expected to play snaps at right tackle and right guard -- the Chiefs will have to decide if they feel comfortable with him protecting  Patrick Mahomes  despite not having any NFL experience.

 Moore is the safer option, but Benson should have plenty of snaps to demonstrate that he's ready for the spotlight that is opening night on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos on "Monday Night Football."

 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 As expected, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Thursday that quarterback Patrick Mahomes will not play in the preseason opener Saturday against the Los Angeles Rams . Reid said the decision to not play Mahomes is a precautionary measure since the quarterback is still recovering from the surgery he had in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in left knee.

 "It'll be Justin [Fields] and then Garrett [Nussmeier] and then Chris [Oladokun] will take it from there," Reid said of Saturday's quarterback rotation. "We'll just see how the reps go as we work through that."

 Without Mahomes, Reid could decide to not play several starters against the Rams, a decision that would be different from previous years. One of those veterans who requested to not be in uniform was pass rusher Chris Jones , the defense's longest-tenured member.

 "Why play the starters?" Jones said. "I mean, it's so much risk you're taking to play the starters in the preseason. I hope Coach Reid [will] be like, 'You know what, starters don't play.'"

 More observations: 

 
 The players who missed Thursday's practice were safety Chamarri Conner (sore knee), right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerbacks L'Jarius Sneed (rest) and Kader Kohou (sore ankle), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 Although he wasn't selected in the NFL draft, Chiefs rookie right tackle Kahlil Benson was confident he'd be able to compete for a roster spot. Benson, however, has impressed the Chiefs enough so far into their training camp that he has a chance to win a starting spot on the offensive line. Benson will get his opportunity to make a strong first impression Saturday when the Chiefs host the Los Angeles Rams for their preseason opener.

 "Honestly, I kept my head down and knew my time was going to come," Benson said after Wednesday's practice. "I really just stayed humbled, stayed faithful and just kept praying to God that I was ready to be on-call when it was that time."

 Against the Rams, Benson is expected to play two positions in the first half: right tackle and right guard. This week, Benson has taken all his reps at right guard since starter Trey Smith has been out with a hip injury. When the second-team offense enters the game, Benson is expected to slide to the right tackle spot. Showing quality versatility could be a factor in Benson winning the right tackle role over five-year veteran Jaylon Moore .

 Cousins gets nod over Mendoza to open Raiders camp 
 What's next for Crosby, WR and CB rooms? 
 

 
 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 Right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson left Monday's practice early with a trainer.

 Powers-Johnson went down during the red zone period while playing with the second-team offense. He quickly popped back up and walked to the sideline. Once the red zone period was over, he headed into the facility.

 Powers-Johnson, who has started in 21 of 23 games in two seasons, has competed with second-year offensive lineman Caleb Rogers for the starting right guard spot. Both players alternated reps with the starting offense. Rogers spent the rest of practice with the starters after Powers-Johnson left.

 Coach Klint Kubiak did not speak to reporters on Monday. He won't address the media until after the team's joint practice with the Houston Texans on Tuesday.

 Tight end Brock Bowers returned after missing Sunday's practice because of personal reasons. Bowers caught two of quarterback  Kirk Cousins ' five touchdowns in the red zone. Bowers also made a contested catch over linebacker Quay Walker , but the play was nullified due to a holding call.

 Meanwhile, wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . stretched and did agility work at the beginning of practice for the second straight day. He did not participate in individual or team drills, as he is working his way back from an injury.

 

 Who is the Raiders' top performer so far at camp? 
 Malik Benson . The rookie wide receiver has had a strong camp, showing the coaching staff that he could play a meaningful role during the regular season. Whether playing with the first- or second-team offense, Benson has found ways to make plays. On top of that, he has developed a strong connection with quarterback Fernando Mendoza .

 Benson has shown solid footwork, the ability to create separation from defenders and generate yards after the catch. Benson is listed behind Jack Bech on the team's unofficial depth chart. But if he can translate his strong performance from the practice field onto the preseason games, Benson could overtake Bech as WR3.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 What does Mendoza have to do to make a serious push to be the starter? Kirk Cousins is currently in the driver's seat to be named the starting quarterback for Week 1. And even though Mendoza has been solid during training camp, Cousins has been the better quarterback. Cousins has only played with the first-team offense, while Mendoza only did so once, and that was because coach Klint Kubiak decided to hold Cousins out of practice due to his scuffle with defensive end Maxx Crosby .

 If Mendoza wants to change the narrative, he will have to play flawlessly in the preseason games, starting Thursday night against the Arizona Cardinals . By doing so, he could push the team to give him more first-team reps. Mendoza has impressed the coaching staff and remains on track in his development. But he still has a ways to go before being considered QB1.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 Under the bright lights at Allegiant Stadium on Tuesday, the connection between rookies Fernando Mendoza and Malik Benson continued to thrive.

 In the team's final practice before the preseason opener against the Arizona Cardinals , Mendoza relied heavily on the sixth-round wide receiver. He connected with Benson on an out route while playing with the second-team offense. Later in practice, Mendoza zipped the ball through tight coverage to Benson on a slant route.

 Benson said he and Mendoza began developing a strong bond when they first met at the scouting combine in February -- two months before they officially became teammates. The former Oregon pass catcher said after they were both drafted by the Raiders, he wanted to make sure he could be a player who Mendoza could rely on.

 That has been the case since OTAs and mandatory minicamp.

 "I know, when it comes to Sundays, when it comes to practice, he's going to rely on me to be in that spot, and I'm going to rely on him to place the ball where it needs to be placed," Benson said.

 Overall, Mendoza was solid in what can be described as a light practice. The only blemish on his performance was a tipped pass and interception by linebacker Cody Lindenberg .

 More observations: 

 
 Second-year wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . missed his fourth straight practice. Rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford did not wear a red non-contact jersey and was a full participant during practice. He recorded a sack on Mendoza while playing with the second-team defense. 
 Quarterback  Aidan O'Connell  had the best throw of the evening --- a 55-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Brandon Johnson during the 7-on-7 period. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 10 

 Maybe coach Klint Kubiak's decision to hold Kirk Cousins from Saturday's practice due to his scuffle with Maxx Crosby sparked a fire within the veteran quarterback. Maybe it didn't. Either way, Cousins had his best performance of training camp.

 Monday featured Cousins fitting the ball into tight windows and effectively conducting two-minute drives. He threw a touchdown pass to Brock Bowers in the corner of the end zone despite tight coverage from Taron Johnson . Both players later connected on a deep pass over the middle, positioning the offense near the goal line.

 Cousins delivered a nice pass to wide receiver Tre Tucker on a crossing route with rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses in coverage. He also connected with Malik Benson , who made a contested catch against cornerback Darien Porter .

 During the two-minute period, Cousins completed four passes, including a touchdown throw to wide receiver Jalen Nailor .

 Fernando Mendoza , on the other hand, went back to playing with the second-team offense. He didn't put together his best performance. He ran into running back Dare Ogunbowale during the handoff exchange.

 He threw his third interception of camp. Mendoza attempted a pass to wide receiver Deven Thompkins on an out route. Greedy Vance was in front of Thompkins in man coverage, and Mendoza threw the ball directly into the second-year defensive back's hands.

 His best throw -- a back-shoulder pass to Benson -- was called back because he was sacked on the play.

 Other observations: 

 
 Defensive end Kwity Paye returned to practice, but did not participate in the team period. Rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford practiced, but wore a red non-contact jersey. Guard Caleb Rogers , tight end Carter Runyon and wide receiver  Dont'e Thornton Jr . did not participate. 
 From a health standpoint, rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy said he feels closer to how he was in 2024. McCoy, who missed the entire 2025 college football season at Tennessee, said the Raiders' rehab plan has him feeling much better. "I'm still getting there. It's been a long time since I really played football. 
 McCoy mentioned that the biggest challenge was getting back into football shape…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Vikings camp. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Vikings' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Vikings stories 

 
 What Kyler Murray as QB1 means for Vikings, J.J. McCarthy 
 Vikings, O'Neill reach $96M extension 
 Top Vikings storylines after minicamp, from QBs to new GM 
 Will Vikings start Caleb Banks, other rookies on defense? 
 Jefferson says decision on Vikings starting QB 'coach's call' 
 

 

 Who is the Vikings' top performer so far at camp? 

 Receiver Tai Felton has demonstrated remarkable improvement from his rookie year, when he struggled to catch the ball consistently in training camp and wound up with a near-exclusive special teams role during the season. He has made one-handed catches in the end zone, demonstrated soft hands at the end of deep routes and displayed his top-end speed while running quick hitters. Coach Kevin O'Connell said he has noted exceptional route running at times as well.

 Is Felton the Vikings' best player? Of course not. But no one has opened more eyes since camp began. He'll push veteran No. 3 receiver Jauan Jennings for playing time.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 The entire NFL world wants to know how quarterback Kyler Murray , who was named the starter after a two-week competition with J.J. McCarthy , will perform in the Vikings' offense. But Murray isn't likely to play nearly enough during the preseason to answer that question.

 The most important question the Vikings can realistically answer is how much of their talented draft class will truly be ready to contribute in Week 1.

 That list most notably includes defensive linemen Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange , linebacker Jake Golday , safety Jakobe Thomas , cornerback Charles Demmings and running back Demond Claiborne .

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 Second-year quarterback Max Brosmer did not participate in a relatively light practice Monday because of an injured right wrist, a development to keep an eye on as the Vikings prepare for their second preseason game Saturday against the Baltimore Ravens .

 
The Vikings and Ravens are scheduled for two days of joint practices Wednesday and Thursday, and historically coach Kevin O'Connell has not played starters in the preseason game that immediately follows. O'Connell has not revealed his plans for Saturday's game. But assuming that starter Kyler Murray doesn't play, and if Brosmer isn't available, that would leave all the snaps for J.J. McCarthy and Carson Wentz .

 
In 2025, Brosmer played 58% of the Vikings' offensive snaps in the second preseason game following joint practices with the New England Patriots .

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said earlier this week that both of the quarterbacks who took part in their two-week competition for the starting job would play in Saturday's preseason opener at the New York Giants . That means Kyler Murray will start, along with most of the team's first-team offense, and J.J. McCarthy will play next.

 
The Vikings held a relatively brief practice Thursday, similar to what they would do for a Friday practice during a regular-season week. Two notable veterans did not participate -- receiver Justin Jefferson and left tackle Christian Darrisaw -- making them unlikely to play Saturday.

 
Right guard Will Fries , who had sat out the previous two days of practice, was back on the field and participating in team drills.

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 While the world has been focused on the Vikings' quarterback competition, another part of their offense has been more quietly under development. 
Coaches are in the process of tweaking the team's run game to give it more variety and, they hope, more production. Once pads came on at the start of the second week of training camp, Vikings running backs have ripped through the line of scrimmage on a regular basis, especially via outside zone concepts. 
"We're running the football very, very well against a really good defense right now," coach Kevin O'Connell said this week. 
On one play Wednesday, running back Jordan Mason followed a block from right tackle Brian O'Neill to reach the sideline and sprint for a touchdown. As Mason was running, O'Neill, right guard Joe Huber and center Blake Brandel sprinted after him in celebration.

 Other observations:

 
 Right guard Will Fries again sat out practice, with Huber taking his place with the first team. 
 Rookie safety Jakobe Thomas participated in individual drills, but his absence from team drills continued. 
 
 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 

 After his first public practice with the Vikings this spring, Kyler Murray uttered a four-word phrase that hovered over the team's quarterback competition all summer.

 "My confidence," Murray said in May, "is unshakeable."

 That helps explain why Murray didn't sound much different Tuesday after coach Kevin O'Connell named him the team's starter as the third week of training camp began. Murray said he did not expect to be handed the job and acknowledged that not every practice this summer has gone smoothly as he split reps with J.J. McCarthy .

 "There's going to be good days," Murray said. "There's going to be bad days. We're facing adversity every single day. But I'm definitely getting more comfortable as each day goes."

 Murray had a sharp practice Tuesday while taking all of the first-team reps for the first time since Week 5 of last season when he was with the Arizona Cardinals . McCarthy said he would address the decision publicly Wednesday.

 More observations:  

 
 Right guard Will Fries did not practice Tuesday. He was replaced on the first team by second-year guard Joe Huber . 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 9 

 As the third week of training camp began in the evening, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was not ready to name a winner in the QB1 competition between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy .

 "Nothing has really changed from a standpoint of the timeline and things like that," O'Connell said before the Vikings took the field at TCO Stadium for their annual night practice. "So we'll see how the reps continue to go and when we feel like we're at that place, we're going to make sure we communicate that both in house and internally and obviously to you guys as soon as possible."

 The Vikings have a scheduled off day Monday to reset the competition if they desire. Murray entered training camp as the favorite for the job, and sources say they believe he still is. Asked Sunday where Murray is in the offensive system compared to where he thought he would be at this point, O'Connell said: "I think mentally he's definitely probably ahead of where I thought." O'Connell went on to say there are some parts of the offense that are new to everyone.

 
 It was a rough practice for the offense as defensive pressure made it difficult for quarterbacks Kyler Murray or J.J. McCarthy to get into a rhythm. Murray threw two interceptions, to cornerbacks James Pierre and Isaiah Rodgers , the latter when he was scrambling and tried to get the ball to Justin Jefferson on the sideline. McCarthy continued his theme of hitting deep out routes, including another to receiver Myles Price . McCarthy completed a deep pass to Jefferson down the right sideline but it forced Jefferson to slow down to bring it in, and he struggled later in a red zone drill. 
 Part of the protection issue was caused by the absence of…
