title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Patriots' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 Patriots TE Hunter Henry signs extension worth up to $20M 
 Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice? 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 
 Quarterback Drake Maye  delivered a beautiful deep pass to receiver A.J. Brown for a 65-yard(ish) touchdown over the middle, which was the highlight play of practice.

 Maye thrust his right arm into the air in celebration, with his right index finger extended. A few yards behind him, coach Mike Vrabel did the same.

 The play, and celebration, served as a fitting preview for what is to come: Brown's former team, the Eagles, visiting New England for practice on Wednesday and Thursday. Brown is scheduled to address reporters after Wednesday's practice.

 Maye and Brown have been working behind the scenes, and on the field, to develop a connection. Their lockers are next to each other. Brown also said they often sit next to each other in meetings.

 Some of their best work leading into Monday has been in the red zone, where Brown's size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) and physicality have shown up. They hadn't experienced consistent success on the deep ball before Monday, which might have explained the emphatic reactions from Maye and Vrabel.

 More observations: 

 
 In a rare drill that fourth-year DT Cory Durden said he's never seen before in the NFL, the team gathered on one field and rookies and first-year players were challenged to one-on-one drills as everyone watched. One highlight was first-round pick Caleb Lomu (right tackle) blocking second-round pick Gabe Jacas (outside linebacker). "Coach was giving them an opportunity to perform in front of their teammates. It's a pride thing," Durden said. "It brings energy to everybody. Nobody wants to lose in front of the whole team." 
 Kicker Andy Borregales was once again challenged in a full-team field goal drill by kicking into skinny posts (about half the width of regulation goal posts). Two days after going 6-of-6, he was 3-of-5 from a distance between 37 and 52 yards. The two misses were estimated to have been successful on regular goalposts. 
 Starting LB Christian Elliss and reserve OLB Jesse Luketa left the full-pads practice early, while starting DT Christian Barmore returned. 
 CB Christian Gonzalez has remained out of practice since appearing to injure his ankle Aug. 12. 
 

 

 
 Who has been the Patriots' top performer at camp so far? 
 CB Christian Gonzalez . The question entering training camp was if he might be a hold-in due to ongoing talks on a contract extension. Instead, he was a full participant the first 13 practices and played a significant role in elevating the competition level for the entire team with his back-and-forth, fire-breathing one-on-one matchup with WR A.J. Brown -- which was arguably the top storyline of camp.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How much is the rookie class ready to contribute? First-round pick Caleb Lomu ideally projects as the swing offensive tackle, second-round pick Gabe Jacas as a top backup OLB who creates havoc as a pass rusher, and third-round pick Eli Raridon as the No. 2 tight end behind Hunter Henry . Their performance in games can solidify those roles, along with other rookie-based questions, such as whether seventh-round pick Behren Morton earns a roster spot as the No. 3 quarterback.

 

 Saturday, Aug. 15 
 Two days after Andy Borregales was 2-of-5 on field goal attempts in the preseason opener, he was put in a pressure-filled spot by coach Mike Vrabel in practice Saturday.

 Borregales had to kick through skinny goalposts that are about half the width of regulation goalposts. He aced the test, going 6-of-6 from a distance between 32 and 47 yards.

 "Obviously, the skinny posts are posed as a challenge after the game," Borregales said after the practice attended by season-ticket holders. "At the end of the day, whatever two poles are in front of me, that's my target and that's my job that I have to do.

 "I felt like I bounced back today, going back to the basics."

 After Thursday's 13-13 tie with the Colts, in which Borregales was wide left from 56, 55 and 49 yards, the second-year kicker said he planned to watch the tape and make improvements. The miss from 49 came at the end of regulation.

 What did he learn?

 "Just some technical stuff. I came out here today and fixed those little issues," he said. "I think today was a great day to build off."

 One change that also might have helped was the return of incumbent snapper Julian Ashby , who missed the last week with an ankle injury.

 More observations: 

 
 Top backup center/guard Ben Brown , who was knocked out of the preseason opener with an undisclosed lower-body injury, will miss multiple weeks throughout the preseason, according to Vrabel. 
 Another top backup center/guard, Andrew Rupcich , also didn't finish the preseason opener after appearing get rolled up on. He didn't practice Saturday. The injuries to Brown and Rupcich led the team to sign free agent interior offensive linemen Darrian Dalcourt (Alabama) and Joe Michalski (Oklahoma State). 
 WR Romeo Doubs delivered multiple highlight-reel touchdown catches, including one in the end zone over CB Charles Woods to cap off a red zone drill. Doubs threw the football high in the air to celebrate in a rare show of emotion. 
 Starting CB Carlton Davis III returned as a full participant for the first time since leaving practice July 28 with what he said was a hamstring injury. He acknowledged after practice that he was knocking off some rust. 
 Starting CB Christian Gonzalez remained out of practice after appearing to injure his ankle Monday while defending Doubs in the end zone. 
 Starting OLB Dre'Mont Jones didn't finish practice for unknown reasons, so second-round pick Gabe Jacas elevated into the starting lineup opposite Elijah Ponder . 
 Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla was a guest of the team at practice. He spent time talking with WR A.J. Brown at one point. 
 

 

 
 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Patriots' had an official ribbon-cutting ceremony for their new 160,000-square-foot New Balance Athletics Center on Wednesday, with owner Robert Kraft and coach Mike Vrabel among those sharing remarks before VP of football operations and strategy John Streicher led a behind-the-scenes tour.

 "There's not a better place to teach and prepare our players," Vrabel said.

 The facility includes a 15,000-square-foot weight room; 11,000 square feet of dining and kitchen space; a 10,500-square-foot virtual reality room; 3,700 square feet dedicated to hydrotherapy; and a state of the art draft room.

 The 160,000 square feet is more than double the amount the team previously occupied at Gillette Stadium.

 On one notable part of the tour, Streicher stopped at QB Drake Maye 's locker and explained the thought that went in to selecting the details of each locker -- which includes two separate areas to dry shoulder pads/helmets and cleats.

 Maye's…

title: Saints' offense passes one test, with Cowboys, Rams up next
summary: Shough and the starting offense got about 50 snaps of work against the Jaguars' first team in their joint practice.
full_text:
METAIRIE, La. -- The New Orleans Saints ' offense took almost three weeks of training camp to have its first standout day. After 11 practices of up-and-down offensive performances, it couldn't have come at a better time. 

 The Saints hosted the Jacksonville Jaguars for a joint practice session last Thursday, and New Orleans' starting offense held its own against a Jacksonville defense that was No. 1 against the run, 21st in passing defense and 11th in total defense last season. 

 It might have been the spark the Saints needed after weeks of facing their own teammates.

 It also came right before a few days of rest for the starters -- who didn't play in the first preseason game against the Jaguars on Saturday. 

 The Saints lost that game 24-20 after a quick start that featured a 86-yard kickoff return by Ty Chandler and a 9-yard touchdown run by Audric Estime on the first play.  Spencer Rattler  started the game but struggled, completing 8-of-11 passes for 42 yards. He was also sacked twice and fumbled.

 Quarterback Zach Wilson came in during the second quarter and showed good chemistry with Bub Means and Barion Brown , both of whom had more than 70 receiving yards. He also threw a touchdown pass to Oscar Delp after a previous touchdown by Means was reversed.

 The starters will ramp things back up in California for a joint practice against the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday followed by a joint practice session against the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday.

 Those practices will be the next big tests for the starting offense, as the Saints will face a Rams defense that led the league in total yards allowed last season and a Cowboys defense that finished second in that category. 

 
"I think more than anything, it was good to go against a really good defense in the Jaguars. And continually we're going to be able to do that the next couple of games against the Rams and Cowboys," Saints quarterback Tyler Shough  said. "So, we feel really good where we're at, but we also know that we have so much more to go. We're nowhere close to where we need to be, but I also know that we're kind of light-years from where we were last year as well."

 

 The offense didn't take off immediately at the start of camp, but there were some standout moments, with rookie wide receiver Brown making a name for himself.

 There were ugly days, particularly on Aug. 11, when the defense won a red zone period by relentlessly pressuring and picking off Shough twice. 

 The question of whether the offense was facing a good defense or simply struggling wasn't fully answered against the Jaguars, but both the offensive and defensive units came away happy after seeing where they stacked up against new competition.

 "I thought it was a great day. I think every single period I felt like we kind of had the edge a little bit," Shough said Thursday. "The run game was working really well. I feel like we had some good chunks in the pass game and there was some good, some bad. They were a really good team, too."

 Some highlights included a deep pass by Shough to rookie WR Bryce Lance , who was working against Travis Hunter . Shough targeted WR Chris Olave several times, including on a deep ball Olave fought for but which fell incomplete.

 Later the quarterback connected with Olave for a toe-tapping touchdown. Backup quarterback Rattler worked on his chemistry with reserve receivers such as Brown and Trey Palmer , who caught a deep ball and spiked it in the end zone after scoring a touchdown.

 "I think we don't necessarily use other teams as a metric, but it's also a competition-based sport. And so I think it was a good day to focus on us as an offense," Shough said after practice Thursday.  "I feel like we really improved."

 

 Shough and the starting offense got about 50 snaps of work against the Jaguars' first team -- far more than it would in a normal preseason opener. Saints coach Kellen Moore said this allowed for an evaluation of the starters in a situation that has the intensity of a game, while letting the backups put together a stronger résumé with more work in the actual preseason game.

 "I think sometimes the challenge for these young guys is, you come to these preseason games and you wait till the fourth quarter for your eight snaps and one snap doesn't go your way and it gets magnified," Moore said. "These guys are going to get to play a ton of snaps, which I think is awesome for us because inevitably there's going to be some good snaps, there's going to be a snap you want back. And it allows us to let these guys respond to those situations and just keep playing."

 Moore hasn't said how he'll handle snaps in the Week 2 preseason game against the Rams after two more days of joint practices, but the practices will be critical for the continued development of the offense. 

 Every snap is necessary to fix a unit that finished last in 2025 with a red zone efficiency of just 44.4%. The Saints' rushing offense finished 28th in yards per game and their scoring offense ranked 28th. Their field goal unit is in flux as well after Charlie Smyth took over for a struggling Blake Grupe last season. 

 Smyth, now competing against former UFL kicker Tanner Brown , hasn't yet maintained his hold on his job in a battle that'll likely go down to the wire. 

 He took a step back in Saturday's game against the Jaguars, missing a 52-yard field goal while Brown made both of his field goal kicks.

 Smyth made all six of his kicks against the Jaguars in practice, bringing his camp total to 33-of-41, while Brown missed a 51-yarder that went off the upright, bringing his camp total to 33-of-33. 

 The red zone offense was having trouble converting field goals to touchdowns in two-minute situations to end several practices. The Saints added Travis Etienne Jr . in free agency to upgrade their run game, and Etienne has been leaned on heavily with the starting unit. With no live tackling in most of their practice periods, it's hard to know how that run game will translate to the regular season. 

 "I feel like we've got to continue to grow and get better and I feel like it kind of helps us just jell and get those real live reps that some teams don't get until game time," Etienne said. "Going out there against a different defense, it was good to see what we did, get a couple of runs, a couple of things springing and see us all on one page."

title: 2026 New Orleans Saints training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Saints training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Saints reporter Katherine Terrell has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Saints camp. Kellen Moore enters his second season as head coach, and expectations are higher after  Tyler Shough  impressed while starting the final nine games of the 2025 campaign. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Saints' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.  

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Saints news 
 
 Drew Brees' greatness, as seen through eyes of teammates, coaches 
 Saints place WR Ja'Lynn Polk, 24, on reserve/retired list 
 Saints starting DT Bryan Bresee to have season-ending ACL surgery 
 The legacy of Taysom Hill in New Orleans: 'There's only one' 
 WR Chris Olave signing four-year extension 
 
 

 

 Who was the Saints' top performer at camp? 
 Saints defensive end Chase Young estimated he had six sacks in Thursday's joint practice against the Jacksonville Jaguars ' first team. The actual number likely wasn't far off.

 That summed up a terrific camp for Young, who is coming off a career-best 10 sacks in 12 games. Young has spent the offseason making life very difficult for the Saints' young offensive tackles. Coaches told Young before camp that expectations had been raised for him this year, both as a leader and a performer. He's risen to the occasion on the field and recently told the media that he was willing and hungry to step up as a leader in the locker room as well.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 The Saints offense was impressive against the Jaguars' first-team defense in practice on Thursday after a few weeks of up-and-down performances. The Saints starters likely won't see much preseason action due to three separate sets of joint practices, but they passed their first test. The red zone offense is one of the areas in which the Saints could use improvement, as they've often settled for field goals instead of touchdowns after driving down the field during practices this summer.

 

 Friday, Aug. 14 

 The Saints held a walkthrough in the Superdome on Friday afternoon, going through everything from where they'll line up to stretch to a brief run through of what Saturday's game against the Jaguars might look like. The Saints won't be playing most of their starters against Jacksonville, preferring to use Thursday's lengthy practice session instead.

 Coach Kellen Moore didn't say if that would also be the case next week when they hold joint practices against the Cowboys and Rams in California. Moore said he likes the joint practices because it allows the starters to get work, while backups will now get more reps in the actual games that they would have previously.

 "That's the way this one has certainly been structured. Every week's going to be a little bit different," Moores said. "I think there's still merit to getting guys preseason work. And certainly that's still something that we'll let this preseason take its course and make decisions as we go week by week. But I thought our guys were able to get essentially a full game yesterday. It was really even more than the full game as far as the intensity [and time spent practicing]."

 Other observations:  

 
 QB  Spencer Rattler will start against the Jaguars, and the team will go to Zach Wilson "at some point." Moore also expects to get Hunter Dekkers , who has not gotten a practice rep this summer, into the game. 
 Moore said RB  Kendre Miller is making "good progress" in his return from his back injury. 
 Moore said it's to be determined whether WR  Jordyn Tyson , who injured his hamstring, travels with the team to California on Monday. 
 Both kickers will kick in Saturday's game and will rotate back and forth. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 The Saints came away from their joint practice against the Jaguars with positivity on both sides of the ball. The offense had one of their best days of camp. Some highlights include a deep touchdown by QB  Tyler Shough , who completed a deep pass to Bryce Lance working against Travis Hunter with pressure in his face. Hunter would have attempted to tackle Lance if it were game situation, but there was no live tackling to the ground in practice.

 Other highlights included a QB  Zach Wilson to Bub Means touchdown; a Shough to Chris Olave touchdown, where Olave kept his toes in bounds for a score; and a Spencer Rattler to Trey Palmer deep touchdown. Shough said he felt his personal highlight occurred during the two-minute drill where he had six straight completions to set Charlie Smyth up for a 53-yard field goal as time ran out. Defensively, Julian Blackmon kicked things off with an interception of Jags' QB  Trevor Lawrence while the defensive line was active and in position for multiple sacks. At the end of the day, Young estimated he was involved in six sacks.

 More observations:  

 
 Jonas Sanker and Hunter Dekkers both got new numbers, with Sanker switching to No. 7 and Dekkers now wearing No. 13. 
 Sanker finished the day on the sideline with what appeared to be a cut above his eye. 
 Jordyn Tyson came down hard after a reception, jogged off and did not return to practice. 
 Charlie Smyth went 5-for-5 and Tanner Brown went 4-for-5 in a kicking session, where Brown's 51-yard attempt clanked off the uprights. Both made long field goals at the end of the two-minute drill 
 Spencer Rattler will start the preseason game against the Jaguars. 
 The final period for the first-team defense against the Jags first-team offense in the two minute situation had two pressures and two sacks. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Saints took a step back in anticipation of Thursday's joint practice session against the Jacksonville Jaguars . The Saints will practice against three different teams over the course of camp, and tomorrow's practice will essentially function as their preseason game. The starters won't play in Saturday's game, but they will get extensive time against the Jaguars' first-team tomorrow. The Saints had a short, non-padded inside practice to get ready for that.

 They still ran some 11-on-11 drills with a few highlights -- Isaac Yiadom broke up a Spencer Rattler pass to Bryce Lance , continuing to work through the play until the ball came out. Some teammates rushed over to celebrate the play. In the next team session, Lance caught a touchdown from Rattler in the end zone, making the catch over Jordan Howden and Elliott Davison before spiking the ball in celebration. They'll be back in pads tomorrow against Jacksonville.

 More observations: 

 
 There were multiple bad snaps among all their units, including a high snap from Erik McCoy to Tyler Shough . That comes a day after the offense had several penalties. Moore said the team is a work in progress. "We need to play more consistent football. We have to get there and that's what this time of the year is about," Moore said. 
 The Saints ended practice with red zone work, scoring a touchdown off a handoff to  Travis Etienne Jr . up the middle. Shough's two passes in the four-play session were incomplete, including an attempt to Juwan Johnson on the run with pressure from Chase Young . 
 The Saints experimented with multiple combinations, including an offensive line shuffle ( Cesar Ruiz got a few snaps at center again) and also moving Jonas Sanker around the field, while cornerback Jayden Price got some first-team reps. Moore said Price's consistency has been impressive and he earned more opportunities because of it. 
 The Saints brought former Lions CB Terrion Arnold in for…

title: 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Giants training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Giants' top camp performer and biggest lingering question.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 Giants' Malik Nabers 'felt good' in 1st full-speed live drills 
 Giants QB Jaxson Dart 'puzzled' by latest concussion test request 
 A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp -- an inside look 
 QB Jaxson Dart lauded for inbounds slide at Giants camp 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 
 The referee at practice threw a flag on Colton Hood after he cut off wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr . in the end zone. The rookie cornerback didn't like the call and made it known.

 Coach John Harbaugh saw it unfold. He didn't agree with Hood's assessment and sent him to the sideline. But not until they had a quick chat.

 "I wasn't angry. I just wanted to make the point that, you know, what are you arguing about?" Harbaugh said. "The ball was in the air and you pushed the receiver and redirected him. It was a restriction. That's going to be pass interference. But he's competitive. He's competitive. He wants to win every snap. And I think [that's] part of the journey for the young corners."

 Hood had his ups and downs in the preseason opener -- a 13-10 loss against the Minnesota Vikings . And again at Monday's practice. Harbaugh said Hood was going to be playing plenty and just wanted to accelerate the learning curve.

 Hopefully this was a lesson learned.

 More observations: 

 
 C  John Michael Schmitz Jr . (concussion) and CB Paulson Adebo (leg) returned to practice after sitting out last week and the preseason opener. 
 The defense closed practice with interceptions of Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston  deep in its own territory. First, Kayvon Thibodeaux tipped a pass into the arms of Abdul Carter , who raced the other way for a touchdown. Then Winston was picked by Ar'Darius Washington . Good for the defense, not so much for the offense. 
 

 

 

 Who is the Giants' top performer so far at camp? 
 TE Isaiah Likely  The offseason acquisition has been the Giants' No. 1 receiver with Malik Nabers not participating in team drills. He's been quarterback  Jaxson Dart 's safety net, leading all first-team receivers in catches by a wide margin.

 "Zay's done a great job," offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said.

 The way Likely smoothly gets in and out of breaks has just looked different from incumbent starter Theo Johnson . He also seems to have the best handle on the new offense given his familiarity with coach John Harbaugh and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman from Baltimore. Given the way Dart likes to throw to his tight ends, it suggests that Likely is in for a breakout season given the chemistry they already have developed.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Can the offense put it together? There are a lot of things working against Dart early in camp. He's learning a new offense, doesn't have Nabers in live drills and the structure of practice prohibits endless freelancing, which is perhaps what he does best. So it has been a struggle.

 The offense has failed to put together many big days in practice throughout the summer. Nagy said they expected there to be "highs and lows through this process" for their young quarterback. To see Dart and the first-team offense have some success in the preseason, even if it's just flashes, would be a welcome sight and could provide a confidence boost entering the season.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 The Giants are working hard at training camp. There is no doubt about that. Even on a rare day when they weren't in pads and ran a mental-rep practice that resembled a walk-through, coach John Harbaugh had the Giants on the field for two-plus hours.

 The practice concluded with them going over pregame introductions and the new routine for warmups. Every detail is important at the difficult Camp Harbaugh, which had players in full pads at seven of the past 10 practices.

 "My toughest training camp in 10 years," said fullback Patrick Ricard , who came over from Baltimore with Harbaugh.

 In a way, this has reminded some Giants of a college camp. With fewer rules, the big school colleges are known to run much harder and longer practices than the NFL.

 "I was with another Harbaugh [Jim Harbaugh at Michigan] for five years and it seems very similar to that," guard Jon Runyan  said.

 Now the Giants will see if it leads to better results.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Wide receiver Malik Nabers wore a red jersey for the first time and participated in a good chunk of the walk-through. The star receiver caught close to a handful of passes as he inches closer to live drills off a torn right ACL. "Soon," Harbaugh said earlier this week. Sometime next week would seem likely. 
 The Giants have their preseason opener on Saturday afternoon against the Minnesota Vikings . Harbaugh wouldn't say whether QB Jaxson Dart and the starters would play. It seems like they might get some work as they learn a new offense. "That is a big part of it, executing the new offense," Harbaugh said. "But also a young quarterback. You've got a young quarterback who is just in his second year and didn't play a whole season even last year. So he's just getting started." 
 Players who didn't practice Thursday: CB Paulson Adebo (worked on side), C John Michael Schmitz Jr . (concussion) and WR Jalin Hyatt (leg). 
 Players who returned to practice (limited): CB Greg Newsome II (knee) CB Dru Phillips (knee) G/C Lucas Patrick (knee) WR JuJu Smith-Schuster (knee). 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 

 The kicking competition continues: Ben Sauls went 5-of-6 on field goal attempts in Wednesday's practice. Rookie Dominic Zvada went 7-of-7, including a 61-yarder to end practice.

 Overall in camp, Zvada is now 48-of-51 on kicks. Sauls is 41-of-48.

 "They're both having really good camps," coach John Harbaugh said.

 Running back Cam Skattebo and tight end Isaiah Likely peer-pressured Harbaugh into having Zvada attempt the 61-yard kick after the offense repeatedly sputtered in end-of-game situations. There were 10 seconds remaining on the clock and Harbaugh had the offense out on the field ready to run a play from the 44-yard line.

 He reconsidered. Zvada drilled the kick with plenty of room to spare (it clanked off the back fence) as the offense went wild.

 At this point, it seems a fait accompli that the Giants will carry a kicker with little to no experience come Week 1.

 More observations:  

 
 Odell Beckham Jr . caught a pair of passes in live drills after a couple of quiet days. Harbaugh said Beckham will play in Saturday's preseason opener against the Vikings. 
 Harbaugh took the high road on whether QB Jaxson Dart will play. He decided to intentionally "dodge" that question. 
 Backup cornerback Art Green had a really strong practice. He knocked down a handful of passes. It comes at a time when the Giants are looking for someone to step up at cornerback. 
 CBs Dru Phillips (knee), Greg Newsome II (knee) and Paulson Adebo worked on the side at Wednesday's practice. Harbaugh said Adebo was "day to day." 
 G Francis Mauigoa was a full participant after being limited Tuesday. 
 WRs Juju Smith-Schuster (knee) and Jalin Hyatt (leg), C John Michael Schmitz Jr. (concussion), C/G Lucas Patrick (knee) and DB DJ James did not practice.

title: 2026 New York Jets training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Jets training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
Jets' RB Hall strains right groinJets' RB Hall strains right groin 

 The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Jets reporter Rich Cimini has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jets camp. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Jets' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jets camp 
 
 RB Breece Hall strains groin, Glenn says its not serious 
 Jets CB Stiggers taken to hospital after collapsing at practice 
 No. 2 pick Bailey living up to hype, bringing 'juice' to Jets 
 Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq to miss time after hernia setback 
 Jets' Smith rues being 'distraction' after dispute with girlfriend 
 2026 Jets training camp preview 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 It was a rough way to end practice.

 RB Breece Hall was in the locker room, nursing a groin injury from earlier in practice. WR Garrett Wilson was nowhere to be found; he showed up sick in the morning, vomiting, and was held out. QB Geno Smith was on the field, taking his full share of reps, but he was favoring his left ankle -- an injury that occurred Wednesday and kept him out of the preseason opener Friday.

 Not a great day for the Jets' big three on offense.

 Smith powered through the relatively light practice, though he did have one hiccup -- an overthrow that was picked off by S Andre Cisco in a two-minute drill.

 Coach Aaron Glenn acknowledged that Smith still is feeling the residual effects of the injury, adding, "I want to see exactly how he feels coming out of this practice to see how we're going to continue to move forward."

 Something to watch. Rookie Cade Klubnik started the opener and played well.

 Other observations:  

 
 There was some positive injury news, as NT T'Vondre Sweat and edge  Joseph Ossai practiced for the first time. Both are projected starters. "We want to make sure we take our time with [Sweat]," Glenn said of the 360-pounder. 
 The cornerback room has absorbed some hits. Nahshon Wright (undisclosed), Qwan'tez Stiggers (concussion) and rookie D'Angelo Ponds (calf) didn't practice. Ponds, who was expected to compete for a starting job, still hasn't practiced. Rookie free agent Mory Bamba , who recorded four passes defensed in the opener, injured a knee in the game and will be sidelined at least two weeks. 
 WRs Isaiah Williams and rookie Omar Cooper Jr . stayed after practice for about an hour, each catching about 100 balls from the JUGS machine. They also caught tennis balls and bean bags. Williams, known for his kickoff and punt return abilities, said he wants to improve his hands. 
 Despite two consecutive days with no practice, LB  Demario Davis  and S Minkah Fitzpatrick received veteran rest days. Load management is one of the themes in camp. 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13  
 
 Who has been the Jets' top performer so far at camp? 

 Let's go with a rookie -- edge rusher David Bailey , the No. 2 overall pick. Those who criticized the Jets for drafting Bailey over LB Arvell Reese have been quiet lately. As a pass rusher, Bailey has been dominant at times, demonstrating elite first-step quickness. In joint practices with the Bucs, he caused a lot of problems for veteran RT Luke Goedeke , a $22 million-a-year player. Bailey still has to answer questions as a run defender -- he must clean up some technique stuff -- but his speed off the edge will make him a fun watch in 2026. 

 "He looks like he's everything that was advertised -- and more," MLB Demario Davis said.

 
 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 Can Geno Smith and the passing game get off the ground? They added some weapons, drafting TE Kenyon Sadiq and WR Omar Cooper Jr . in the first round, but this has been a slow-go for Smith & Co. On some days, Smith looks fantastic. Other days, not so much. Look, no one expects immediate success, but there should be incremental progress -- which is why the preseason games are so important. All told, the starters are expected to play 25 to 30 snaps. Another player (WR Adonai Mitchell ?) needs to step up as the No. 2 option, behind Garrett Wilson . That'll make it easier for Smith.

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 Baker Mayfield beat the Jets with a two-minute drill last season in Week 3, setting up a game-winning field goal for the Buccaneers as time expired, and he did it again on Wednesday in the second of two joint practices.

 The Bucs' QB burned the Jets with three straight completions, hitting Dennis Houston with a short TD pass with three seconds left in a two-minute drill.

 "Baker does a really good job in that situation, and I wanted to see exactly how our guys operated in that situation," said Jets coach Aaron Glenn, adding that he could've helped the players with better defensive calls.

 It was another uneven day for the Jets, who had some hiccups in their own two-minute drive -- a drop by RB Braelon Allen , a holding call on RT Armand Membou and a false start. QB Geno Smith completed only two of seven passes on the drive, which ended with a missed field goal (61 yards) by Jason Sanders .

 "I felt like we could've made a few more plays," Smith said.

 The same could be said of the entire two-day experience. The Bucs, a playoff team in three of Todd Bowles' four seasons as coach, proved themselves the superior team.

 Silver lining for the Jets: This was a learning experience, a not-so-subtle reminder they still have a lot of work to do. Their young players got quality work, which should benefit them in the long run.

 More observations: 

 
 CB Qwan'tez Stiggers , who passed out during Tuesday's practice and was taken to a hospital, is in concussion protocol. Glenn said Swiggers experienced "symptoms" on Tuesday, but didn't elaborate except to say "something must have happened." Before collapsing and briefly losing consciousness, he was involved in a fight with some Tampa Bay players. He lost his helmet in the skirmish (it was flung by Bucs RT Luke Goedeke ). Stiggers was released from the hospital on Tuesday night. 
 Edge rusher Joseph Ossai , removed from the PUP list, is expected to start practicing next week. Rookie CB D'Angelo Ponds (calf), who hasn't practiced at all, also could return, although that seems less certain. Ponds' hopes of landing a starting job for Week 1 are fading by the day. 
 The two teams didn't fight as much as they did on Tuesday. This time, there were only a couple of scuffles. WR Tim Patrick and LG Dylan Parham were involved in "dust ups," as Glenn likes to call them. 
 Free agent CB Terrion Arnold visited the Giants on Wednesday, but there was no meeting with the Jets, a source said. They inquired about Arnold when he was released by the Detroit Lions , but their interest -- if there was any interest beyond due diligence -- appears to have cooled. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Geno Smith and the rest of the starters will play Friday night against the Buccaneers in the preseason opener, coach Aaron Glenn announced Tuesday.

 They can use the work.

 The first-team offense struggled in Tuesday's joint practice with the Bucs, as Smith was intercepted twice (one returned for a touchdown). The offense, learning new coordinator Frank Reich's system, is trending downward after an encouraging start to camp.

 The Jets were out of sync and allowed the Bucs to control the line of scrimmage, with running back  Breece Hall saying, "They beat us up a little today." And, no, he wasn't alluding to the four fights that marred practice.

 There was a spark in a red zone period late in practice, with Smith…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Eagles reporter Tim McManus has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and -- of course -- the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Eagles camp. How will quarterback  Jalen Hurts fare in the reimagined offense? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Eagles news 
 
 Moro Ojomo, Fred Johnson scuffle at Eagles camp 
 Eagles QB Jalen Hurts' speed in camp drawing rave reviews 
 Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Eagles' Nolan Smith apologizes for 'unacceptable' speeding arrest 
 Eagles, DT Carter agree to four-year, $152M extension 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 17 
 Eagles No. 1 receiver DeVonta Smith returned to the practice field after sitting out the previous seven sessions because of a hamstring injury. Smith was a limited participant but looked like his normal self -- explosive, quick getting in and out of breaks -- during individual drills. Monday also marked the return of corners Quinyon Mitchell (glute) and  Cooper DeJean  (groin).

 Rookie receiver Makai Lemon (hamstring) sat out his eighth straight practice but has been ramping up his side work over the past handful of days.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts and the offense had an unremarkable day. Hurts didn't throw downfield much. One pass he did let fly was intercepted by Michael Carter II , who got good positioning on Quez Watkins to make the play. 
 Hurts was able to connect with Hollywood Brown for a chunk gain. Brown found a pocket in the defense between Zack Baun and Riq Woolen and Hurts zipped it in. 
 

 

 

 Who is the Eagles' top performer so far at camp? 

 WR Darius Cooper . No one has made more of their opportunities than Cooper, the 2025 undrafted free agent out of Tarleton State. He came out of nowhere to make the team as a rookie and is making another strong push this summer, standing out in a deep group that includes Hollywood Brown , Elijah Moore and Dontayvion Wicks . Hamstring injuries have sidelined both DeVonta Smith and rookie Makai Lemon for most of camp. Cooper has stepped in and has developed good rapport with QB  Jalen Hurts while showing off strong hands and a willingness to go over the middle.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How will the offensive operation look? The starters are expected to sit out the preseason but there is still plenty to learn about how things function under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion . He has never called plays and has yet to commit to whether he'll be doing so from the booth or the sideline on game days. The team's hope is the offense is quick out of the huddle, light on penalties and looks efficient during Mannion's test-drive.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts had an up-and-down day. He was intercepted by CB Mac McWilliams on an end-zone fade to Hollywood Brown during 7-on-7s early in practice. He got into a flow as the session went on, though, hitting Elijah Moore and Dontayvion Wicks in rhythm before connecting with tight end Dallas Goedert over the middle for a touchdown. Later, Hurts and Wicks hooked up for a touchdown in the corner of the end zone over Riq Woolen , who has come back to earth some this summer following a highly-productive spring.

 More observations:  

 
 Someone should block linebacker  Jalyx Hunt . He's come free far too many times this camp, including from the left side on Thursday to blow up the play. 
 Cooper DeJean (groin) and Quinyon Mitchell (glute) were both sidelined. They were replaced in the lineup by McWilliams and Michael Carter II , respectively. 
 Brown dropped a short pass from Hurts in the red zone. The competition feels tight further down the receiver depth chart, with Darius Cooper , Moore, Brown, Britain Covey and Johnny Wilson among those hoping to find their way onto the 53-man roster. 
 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts and receiver Elijah Moore connected for another big play on Tuesday.

 Hurts uncorked a deep shot for Moore, who sped past safety  Andre' Sam  and hauled in the pass for a touchdown. Moore celebrated by punting the ball well over the practice field gate.

 Hurts has been without DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon the past six practices because of hamstring injuries but is finding a lot of value in building chemistry with some of the other receivers.

 Moore is one of the primary players capitalizing on that opportunity, generating a number of highlight plays alongside QB1.

 More observations: 

 
 Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell sat out of team drills after pulling up during a one-on-one rep against Hollywood Brown . Mitchell went to the sideline and had his right leg stretched out by a trainer. Mac McWilliams took over for him with the first team. 
 Reserve corner Jakorian Bennett has had a good number of pass breakups this summer. He had another one on a Hurts attempt for Moore down the right seam on Tuesday. 
 Cooper DeJean came up with an interception on a reckless downfield throw from Andy Dalton . Later, DeJean blitzed Hurts and registered the "sack." 
 Edge rusher Jalyx Hunt has been one of the more impressive players on the field during camp. He came clean on one rush and chased Hurts to the other side of the field, eventually forcing him out of bounds. 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 10 
 Eagles cornerback Quinyon Mitchell came up with his second interception of camp -- perhaps foreshadowing a breakout year for him in the takeaway department. Mitchell sniffed out a Jalen Hurts pass intended for Hollywood Brown over the middle and came up with the pick on the first play of a simulated two-minute drive.

 
"Just his patience, his confidence," CB Riq Woolen said on what stands out about Mitchell. "He's been in this defense ... so he has a good understanding of how he can play certain techniques and certain coverages. Being able to watch him make plays, it inspires me to make plays."

 
Mitchell, a first-team All Pro in 2025, has yet to record a regular-season interception in his two years in the league but is tied for the most career playoff interceptions (four) among active players. It feels like a matter of time before he starts posting INTs more regularly.

 More observations: 

 
 Receivers Makai Lemon and DeVonta Smith both missed their fifth straight practice with hamstring injuries. 
 Interior lineman Willie Lampkin continues to make a push for a roster spot. Listed at 5-foot-11, 290 pounds, he doesn't have the same size as most of his counterparts but is shining despite being asked to flip-flop from center to guard midpractice. Nick Sirianni said when the coaches review these sessions, they find themselves saying, "Willie did it again." 
 Emotions flared on the ninth day of camp. Guard Tyler Steen and DT Ty Robinson appeared to be at the center of an O-line vs. D-line scrum that took a little time to defuse. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 8 

 Eagles running back Saquon Barkley made his presence felt. He got animated after a short touchdown run, chirping at Cooper DeJean before giving Quinyon Mitchell a playful shove.

 The offense switched from goal line to backed up work a short time later. Barkley used a nifty jump cut to speed to daylight on one play and followed that up by shaking defensive tackle Jordan Davis on his next carry.

 Barkley believes this new system can open up some things for him that he hasn't been able to fully showcase to this point in his career.

 "That's the plan," said offensive coordinator Sean Mannion . "Saquon, he's a tremendous player, and I think everything we do offensively ultimately is…

title: 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Steelers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Steelers camp. How will coach Mike McCarthy shape this roster and the offense in his first year in Pittsburgh? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Steelers' top camp performer and biggest lingering questions.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Steelers camp 
 
 Steelers' Benton agrees to 4-year, $72M extension 
 Rookies Drew Allar, Will Howard 'very poised' in Steelers' preseason win 
 Steelers bring back veteran LB Roberts on one-year deal 
 'Tempered': Inside Mike McCarthy's new vision for Steelers 
 Steelers' Broderick Jones cleared after eight months (neck) 
 Rodgers: 'Zero debate' 2026 will be last season 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 17 
Mike McCarthy's first Steelers training camp ended unceremoniously Monday thanks to another round of inclement weather.
 Thunderstorms in the area caused the head coach to not only close today's scheduled practice to fans, but to cancel his team's scheduled work entirely and break camp a day early. Now, the Steelers will return to their southside Pittsburgh practice facility and resume practice Wednesday.

 "It's disappointing, frankly, for the fans, just because those are our best practices when everybody's out there," McCarthy said. "But just based off the weather, we've been kicking this thing around all morning."

 McCarthy said they'll now go through Monday's script on Wednesday, followed by a light walk-through on Thursday and the preseason game against the New York Jets on Friday ( 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network ).

 Despite the weather challenges -- the Steelers had three other practices affected by inclement weather -- McCarthy said he doesn't envision moving camp away from St. Vincent College in the future.

 "I'm actually looking forward to next year because I'm going to enjoy training camp next year," McCarthy said. "I just think anytime it's a first year, just with all the administrative responsibility and going through it the first time. ... There's classrooms I'm going to flip next year. You want to get it to what you feel is the best classroom environment for your team, the best practice environment.

 "As far as the support staff, the facilities, St. Vincent's just as a whole, it's an A-plus. I really think this is not only a special place, but this is a great place to train a football team, just the whole environment and so forth. The only really negative was, I don't know, we had to cancel a couple practices because our best practices are when our fans are out there and it's an awesome environment to be in.

 "Players might not want to hear this, but hell, we'll look to see if we can stay longer next year."

 

 
 Sunday, Aug. 16 
 The Steelers' eighth and final install wrapped up with a bang Sunday afternoon.

 In the final team period, rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings lowered his shoulder into wide receiver Max Hurleman as Hurleman made a play to cross the goal line. The hit sent Hurleman flying, and as the wide receiver slowly got up, tight end Lance Mason  got in Spears-Jennings' face. Once on his feet, Hurleman joined Mason and shoved Spears-Jennings.

 Seconds later, several others ran over and a fight broke out, with pockets of several skirmishes. The seeds for the altercation, though, were planted several plays before the hit. Guard Mason McCormick chirped at recently signed inside linebacker Elandon Roberts for having "fresh legs" when he felt Roberts crossed a line with a hard hit of wide receiver Levi Wentz .

 "Everybody just been going for so long," safety Jaquan Brisker said afterward, acknowledging that a scrum like that was typical at the end of training camp. "You know how everybody just been in camp, body, things like that. Stuff happens there. ... It's physical. I mean, that's part of the game. You can't take that away from the game. Even it happens on game day, sometimes.

 "... You want some dogs out there. You rather have a dog than tell somebody to keep going or whatever, then bite. But guys are out there ready to play, ready to go. Got some dogs out there for sure."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie seventh-round pick Eli Heidenreich won the team's annual home run derby Saturday night. The Mt. Lebanon, Pennsylvania, native played baseball in high school, but he admitted that he hadn't swung a bat in at least four or five years. "Don't know if I ever poked one out in a game," he said. "I was more of like a contact hitter." 
 Special teams coordinator Danny Crossman said some of the penalties called against his units in Thursday's preseason game were technique issues that can be easily corrected. Others, though, he characterized as "things that take no talent," and he wants to eliminate those from the game. "We can't give away field position with penalties," he said Sunday. "We can't waste opportunities with substitution errors. So, things that you don't ever want to see that sometimes pop up in the first preseason game, but that stuff has to be eliminated from our game." 
 Despite the threat of stormy weather Sunday, the Steelers held their final installation practice outside and went through the two-hour practice as scheduled. "The only thing that's going to take me off the field is lightning," coach Mike McCarthy said. "If it's 8 miles, 8½, that's close enough. So, it's just being practical about it. That's my line between toughness and stupidity." 
 Rookie WR and kick returner Kaden Wetjen returned to practice Sunday after being sidelined Saturday. The rest of the banged-up players, including WRs Michael Pittman Jr . and DK Metcalf , didn't practice. 
 Safety DeShon Elliott had his longest day of participation as he works back from last season's knee injury. He was also involved in the end-of-practice scrum, shoving tight end Jaheim Bell . "The physicality showed up today, I know that," defensive coordinator Patrick Graham said. "And then just he's always active in the meetings. He's active bringing the guys together. He's a solid communicator, and that's what we need with that position." 
 

 

 Who has been the Steelers' top performer so far at camp? 
 DB  Asante Samuel Jr . He immensely benefitted from Joey Porter Jr .'s stint on the PUP list with back soreness in the midst of extension negotiations. With his increased playing time, Samuel made play after play in Latrobe, including several PBUs in two-minute drills and against wide receiver DK Metcalf .

 Samuel, whom coach Mike McCarthy said was one of his "favorite" players since arriving in Pittsburgh, was a late add last season coming off of neck surgery, and he signed a one-year, $4 million deal to stay with the Steelers in free agency. If his camp performance is any indication, Samuel's value will be significantly higher than his cost.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How does this new-look defense operate under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham? While there's plenty of questions about how Aaron Rodgers and the offense will look with McCarthy, perhaps more important to the team's success this season is Graham's ability to bring a fresh perspective and scheme to the NFL's highest-paid defense. Of course Graham won't show all of his tricks in the preseason, but these games will give an early preview of the defensive communication and the quality of depth across the board.

title: Cooper Kupp's latest route? Opening a new coffee shop
summary: Cooper Kupp and his wife, Anna, are part of a group that owns Dodo Coffee, which is having a grand reopening in Arkansas in August.
full_text:
Cooper Kupp has hauled in plenty of touchdowns across his nine-year NFL career. Now, he's looking for a score in the coffee world.

 Fresh off his second Super Bowl ring, the Seattle Seahawks wide receiver is opening a coffee shop in Fayetteville, Arkansas, for his brand, Dodo Coffee. Kupp and his wife, Anna, are part of an ownership group that includes Kupp's sister-in-law and her husband, as well as Anna's parents.

 

 Designed by esteemed architect Jeffrey Dungan, the roughly 500-square-foot brick-and-mortar shop opens next Monday. Kupp told ESPN that at first glance it looks "a little bit like an old orthodox church," but it's ultimately meant to be a gathering place for people in the community.

 "As much as we look forward to being able to provide people with the very best coffee, the very best product," he said, "it's also about providing them the best service and also being able to connect with people [in] a very meaningful way."

 The endeavor ends a challenging chapter in Dodo Coffee's history. It launched in 2024 and operated out of a small, white brick store in Arkansas that originally pawned gold. Kupp and his group took over the building and began selling gold in the form of sourced coffee beans from around the world.

 However, eminent domain shut down the building in early 2025, sending them scrambling. They operated out of a trailer while the search for a new shop began.

 Dungan was working on a house for Kupp and his family when Kupp came to him with a proposition: "Any chance you want to build a little 700-foot coffee shop for us?" Dungan graciously accepted.

 

 "We shared what we were about, who we are. And he just built us, designed for us basically this building that was going to fit all the things, all the intentional things, that we're about and try and make them a physical place to come drink coffee," Kupp said.

 The new building had to reflect the effort the company puts into creating an intentional product, Kupp explained.

 Dodo makes its own syrups and sources milk from a farm. The coffee beans originate from places such as Indonesia, Ethiopia and Hawai'i. The shop had to be as much about the experience of walking through it and enjoying the space as it is about the caffeine rush after first sips.

 In came Dungan, who began to think about how drinking coffee is a daily ritual for many people. He likened it to an athlete repeating the same exercises. That led him to design "a cathedral to coffee," he told ESPN.

 The compact shape and structure had to be one that people would notice. Dungan wanted to go all-in on making it the coolest "500-square-foot building that you could do."

 "I wanted it to sort of make people stop and go, 'Well, what the hell is that?'" Dungan said. "I think we might've overshot that goal a little bit."

 But, Kupp's enthusiasm surprised Dungan the most. The first renderings didn't drive him away, which Dungan added says a lot about the star receiver.

 The result is what Kupp referred to as "incredible" and "beautiful." What he's looking forward to the most is the reaction of people when they first walk into the white stucco building with a curved roof and big overhangs.

 

 Dungan described the shop's entrance as "this sort of procession." He compared it to an ancient Roman bath with a hole in the roof and plants on the ground. It reminds Dungan of his favorite morning routine: drinking coffee.

 "There's all this stuff going on in a pretty small area, so it's sort of, to me, it's kind of like caffeine," Dungan said. "It's there to stimulate you. It's there to kind of make the place more interesting and fun of an experience."

 It all ties into Kupp and his ownership group's vision for the brand.

 The first-team All-Pro wide receiver's passion for coffee poured over when discussing elements of Dodo Coffee that are important to him. It's about bringing the brand's vision to life in an artistic way.

 Kupp diligently broke down the process that goes into drinking coffee, from the farmer picking beans to having it steaming in one's favorite mug.

 The brand makes sure to work with the farms to offer the best coffee possible. Oftentimes, there's exploitation and a "lack of intention" from the beginning in the coffee world, Kupp explained. They pay a premium to take care of communities, which in turn takes care of coffee "the way they are supposed to," he said.

 The beans are imported to temperature-controlled warehouses to eliminate potential mold. Dodo Coffee then completes a washed process to prepare them for roasting.

 Once the beans reach the customers' hands, there are special instructions for certain beans. Kupp pinpointed the expensive and rare Geisha bean. It follows a specific brewing process , and the full taste won't be achieved if not brewed properly. It's a situation they hope to avoid when a customer roasts the beans themselves.

 

 "There's an intention all the way through to be like how can we also just make sure that you're getting the very best. That you are going to, by the time you're enjoying the coffee, that you're having it the way you're supposed to," Kupp said.

 Kupp's step-by-step breakdown to ESPN might make him seem like the Willy Wonka of coffee. But he's not the first professional athlete to be involved in the coffee business.

 Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback Patrick Mahomes helped launch Throne Sport Coffee  last year , a ready-to-drink cold brew. NBA star Jimmy Butler famously started "BIGFACE Coffee" during the 2020 NBA bubble, charging $20 a cup . The brand now has a shop in Miami.

 As Kupp opens his own shop in Arkansas, he's looking to express a new coffee process, too.

 "We don't want you to come here and feel like you walk up to the window, they hand you your coffee, you're gone. ... Some people have to have coffee that way and I get it," he said. "But we also want to have the opportunity for you to come in and open the door, walk into the coffee shop, walk through, walk into our space, see the space, see what we've created for you to enjoy."

 It's Kupp's latest golden ticket in what's been a golden year.
